title: Six generated files are proved and not shipping, and two of them duplicate the plugin
description:
mvm-z83.16 adopted features.sp, the wave writer and threat_priority.sp. scan.sp is across too, in v2.40.0: util.sp lost 433 lines and not one of its 195 call sites changed, because //sp:name gives a ported body the name the plugin already calls it by. Two waves of Decoy cleared with it in.

Four files are still generated, proved and included by nobody:

  actionsel_dispatch  202 lines
  actionsel.sp        170 lines
  attributes.sp       134 lines
  roster.sp           122 lines
  roster_dhooks.sp     27 lines

## actionsel and attributes

Both predate the body generator. actionsel replaces GetDesiredBotAction, which is the largest single surgery left: 17 call sites over 12 behaviours, and mvm-z83.41 says the stranded set must stay exactly the 208 the shipped chain strands.

## roster

Different problem, and it is mine. internal/body/roster holds two real ports, dhooks.sp's MyTouch pair and IsBot, and three functions nobody asked for: AliveOnTeam, LoadedRounds and TeamCentre were written to prove the generator could emit a native call, an SDKCall and a vector, which is what mvm-bis asked for. Adopting roster.sp would put three unused functions in the plugin.

Split it: the DHooks are a port and go across with the hand written callbacks deleted from dhooks.sp; the other three move to a package that is generated and compiled and never adopted, so the differential harness keeps its SDKCall coverage without the plugin carrying dead code.

## Done when

Every file in gen/sourcepawn is either included by the plugin with its hand written original deleted, or in a package the list marks as proof and never adopts.

title: Package-level state has no SourcePawn, so every plugin global is an extern
description:
internal/spbody translates a body that owns no state, which gosubset enforces and SUBSET.md documents. The plugin does not work that way: g_bIsDefenderBot, m_bTouchCredits and the rest are package globals, and 436 engine-calling functions read them.

internal/body/roster reaches two of them through internal/engine, as if they were engine calls. That is honest and it does not scale: every global would become a pair of extern accessors, and the state would still live in the SourcePawn the rewrite is meant to delete.

## Done when

A Go package-level var emits as a SourcePawn global, arrays included, and the differential test proves a body that reads and writes one. gosubset stops refusing package-level var in a body package and says why in SUBSET.md.

title: A generated function can call the engine, which the subset was built to forbid
description:
The rewrite rests on this and it does not exist.

The body generator emits pure functions: a struct of plain values in, a plain value
out, and the rule that generated code never calls back into the plugin is what kept
the generator small. docs/parity.md says 436 of 756 functions contain at least one
engine call and hold 14942 lines, so under that rule they can never be generated, and
under the full-rewrite aim they all have to be.

## What has to be answered

- how a native call is written in the Go subset so it reads as Go and emits as
  SourcePawn. internal/bindings already generates a Go declaration per native from
  the includes, so the names exist; what does not exist is calling one from a body
  the generator can emit
- what happens to the ones that are not natives: 121 SDKCall sites, 34 DHook sites
  and about 70 raw address reads. A generated SDKCall is a handle prepared at load
  and called with arguments, which is mechanical; a DHook is a callback the engine
  enters, which is a different shape from a function the plugin calls
- what the golden harness does with any of it. mvm-z83.1 proved a pure decision runs
  under spshell with no game server. A function that calls the engine does not, so
  either the natives are stubbed for the comparison or these functions lose the proof
  that the pure ones have

## Why it is P0

Every remaining file is behind it. The pure 40 percent can be finished without it and
then the epic stops, which is the halfway state the aim rules out.

## Done when

A function holding at least one native call, one SDKCall and one DHook is authored in
Go, generated, compiled by both compilers, and behaves identically to the SourcePawn
it replaces.

title: Spawn NAV recovery teleports a bot into a hang, and the watchdog kills the server
description:
A defender bot stuck at the spawn exit is teleported to a recovery area. The
tick after that teleport never finishes, the engine watchdog fires, and srcds
dies with a segfault. One crash seen so far, on a live game.

## What the server logged

    L 08/29/2026 - 15:07:50: [tf2_defenderbots.smx] SpawnNavRecovery: Totally Not A Bot
      made no spawn-exit progress for six seconds; moved them using func_capturezone
    WatchDog! Server took too long to process (probably infinite loop).
    FATAL ERROR: Host_Error: WatchdogHandler called - server exiting.
    /home/steam/tf-dedicated/srcds_run: line 324: 96 Segmentation fault (core dumped) $HL_CMD

The recovery line is the last thing the mod prints. The teleport succeeded and
was logged; the hang is in what runs after it, not in finding the anchor.

## Where

source/redbots3/nextbot_behavior.sp

- MoveDefenderFromSpawnToBattlefield, around line 445
- FindSpawnRecoveryArea, around line 390, func_capturezone branch
- the caller is the spawn-exit watch, around line 535

## Two candidates

1. The destination is not checked. CNavArea_GetRandomPoint picks any point in
   the area and the code adds 10 units of Z, with no trace to confirm the bot
   lands somewhere walkable. In MvM the func_capturezone is the hatch, which
   sits in a pit, so the nearest nav area to it can put a bot inside geometry
   or off the mesh. A path search from there may not terminate.

2. The repath is forced into the very next tick. MoveDefenderFromSpawnToBattlefield
   sets m_flRepathTime[client] = 0.0 right after TeleportEntity, so the search
   runs immediately, from the position that has just changed, inside one tick.
   That is exactly the ordering the log shows.

Both are the same shape as the nest relocation hang fixed earlier: a nav search
with no bound on it.

## Environment

- tf2_defenderbots v2.39.0, the version tf2-archipelago v1.11.0 pins
- SourceMod 1.12.0-git7246, Metamod 1.12.0-git1225
- mvm_decoy, six bots on RED, one human player
- Linux, the tf2-archipelago Docker image, on worklab

## Worth knowing when fixing

srcds_run catches the crash and restarts the server itself, so the container
stays Up and restart: unless-stopped never fires. docker ps reports a healthy
server while it is dead. What notices is the tf2-archipelago bridge, which
starts logging "cannot ask the game server who is connected" within seconds.

## Suggested shape of the fix

Trace the destination before teleporting and reject a point the bot cannot
stand on, and put a bound on the search that follows rather than forcing it
into the next tick. Related: mvm-y7e, native Linux servers crashing more than
Docker or Windows.

title: [bug] Arms play different waves, so no A/B on this test-bed compares like with like
description:
The most serious measurement fault found so far, and it sits underneath mvm-666 and mvm-81n rather than beside them.

LoadMission at testbed/internal/lab/lab.go:169 only loads the map when the server is not already on it. The comment gives the reason and it is a good one: a changelevel costs time and the mod disables its bots in OnMapStart. But an MvM mission that is not reloaded carries on from the wave it reached, so each attempt starts wherever the last one stopped.

Measured, two runs today on mvm_decoy:

  noise floor, SAME build both arms
    a  waves [1,2]  [6,7]  [8]
    b  waves [2,3]  [4,5]

  go against sourcepawn
    go waves [1,2]  [5,6]  [7,7]
    sp waves [3,4]  [4,4]  [7,7]  [7,7]

Wave 8 of a mission is not wave 1. Different robot counts, different giants, tanks in some and not others. So the arms are not two measurements of one thing, they are measurements of different things, and the difference between them is mostly the mission.

Consequences.

The noise floor recorded on mvm-z83.8 today, about 50 percent on robot kills, is not run to run variance. It conflates variance with wave difficulty and is an upper bound on the real floor rather than the floor. That note needs correcting once this is fixed.

Interleaving the arms, which mvm-666 added, does not help and may hurt: alternating arms means alternating slices of the mission, so arm and wave stay perfectly correlated.

Every A/B in results/ predates this and compares different waves between its halves.

It also explains a real observation from today that looked like a port bug: DefenderAttackTank was 0.0 percent of samples in one arm and 6.6 percent in the other, for two different classes, because one arm played waves with a tank and the other did not.

The fix is to make each attempt start from the same wave, either by reloading the mission properly or by using the existing -wave jump to pin it. Both cost time, and that is the trade the comment was making without knowing the price.

title: The port is behaviour identical, and every difference is a bead not a fix
description:
Maintainer's rule for the whole parity effort, recorded so it does not get lost between agents.

No functionality lost, no new bugs. If the port finds a defect it goes in a bead and stays in the code. A fix that rides along with a port cannot be measured, because a run that moves cannot say whether the port or the fix moved it.

The first thing this caught: internal/actionsel filled the Scout hole with GuardPoint. That is mvm-vnn, and it is a fix. The generated selection must strand exactly the combinations the shipped chain strands, and TestSelectIsTotal now has to assert something stronger than totality: every reachable combination maps to a named outcome, and the set mapping to the stranded outcome equals exactly the 208 the shipped code strands.

The second: fidelity is not just the action. GetDesiredBotAction has 17 distinct action and reason call sites over 12 actions, and the reason strings are read by the test-bed telemetry, so an id must carry the reason. Renaming one is a behaviour change in the reporting even when the action is right.

The third: the id to action dispatch is generated, not hand written. A hand written switch is a second copy of what the table already holds, which is the duplication this epic exists to remove, and a test against a pinned revision asserts every pair in the shipped function appears exactly once in the table.

Also standing: small organised files, roughly 200 lines, so the result is hackable and testable rather than one large generated blob.

title: Action selection moves to Go and exhaustiveness is asserted
description:
The headline finding from reading all 35 closed beads. The decision function that produced the most bugs is not on the design's list.

GetDesiredBotAction and ShouldTakeUpPosition choose which behaviour a bot gets. They are pure, they fit the mvm-z83.4 subset, and four closed bugs are the same function answering nothing for an input nobody enumerated: mvm-7kr and mvm-pvt, both freezes, plus mvm-e4g and mvm-489. The shipped code had four holes and every one shipped as a bot standing still.

The plugin's answer to this today is three hand rolled watchdogs, FEATURE_WATCH_IDLE_BOTS, FEATURE_WATCH_LURKING_SNIPERS and the sniper stall rescue. Those patch the symptom one case at a time. The cause is a hole in a decision table, and a hole in a table is something Go can refuse to compile.

Move it, then assert exhaustiveness over class times phase times flags. A missing combination fails the build rather than shipping as a bot standing in spawn.

This is now the first decision to move, ahead of threat priority in mvm-z83.6.
notes:
Built in internal/actionsel. 3 dimensions, 16 inputs: RoundState 11 values, TFClassType 10, and 14 booleans each a call the surrounding SourcePawn makes. 1802240 combinations, 1425408 reachable. 19 output actions, of which 6 are named 'somebody else already owns this bot' rather than behaviours.

The subset expressed it with nothing missing and nothing worked around: gosubset.CheckDir returns nothing over the package.

TestSelectIsTotal walks all 1425408 reachable combinations and names each hole as its exact combination rather than a count. TestExhaustivenessCatchesAPunchedHole holes a copy and asserts the failure carries the combination, so the mechanism cannot rot into a test that passes for the wrong reason.

One hole still shipping, filed as mvm-vnn. Six further groups return nothing and all six are deliberate, each mapping to a named Keep or Wait action. Two of those are worth knowing because they are the shape of the closed bugs: the between-rounds engineer, spy and rifle sniper who has shopped is left to GetUpgradePostAction, which is the assumption that failed in mvm-7kr, and the running-wave rifle sniper is left to Timer_PlayerSpawn, which is mvm-489. Both are now one grep away instead of implicit in a fallthrough.

Not done: Shipped is a hand transcription of the SourcePawn read on 2026-08-29 and nothing mechanically ties it to the file, so it drifts silently if nextbot_behavior.sp moves. The differential test under spshell is what closes that and it is not wired here. Exhaustiveness proves totality, not correct priority: no test says a demoman should prefer the tank over a robot, only that he prefers something.
Done in internal/actionsel and internal/spgen. Select is a total function over 1425408 reachable combinations, TestSelectIsTotal walks all of them and TestExhaustivenessCatchesAPunchedHole proves the check fails when a hole is punched. TestUnreachableCombinationsAreRefused covers the negative space.

The SourcePawn side is generated from the same table, not hand written: gen/sourcepawn/actionsel.sp is the data and actionsel_dispatch.sp the id-to-action switch, and TestEveryShippedCallSiteIsInTheEdge asserts every action-and-reason pair in the shipped GetDesiredBotAction appears exactly once, read from a pinned revision.

The one behaviour difference is deliberate and it is mvm-z83.41: ActionStrandedAsShipped keeps the shipped hole stranded, and TestStrandedCombinationsAreExactlyTheShippedOnes pins that set at 208 combinations, RoundRunning / Scout. The fix lives beside it in SelectFilled and is not wired up, which is mvm-vnn.

mvm-z83.34 is the follow-up: the three watchdogs can go once this is adopted in the plugin.
close_reason: Closed

title: The engineer walks the map at every break instead of starting where he builds
description:
Peppy, 2026-08-29: "Engie bots should build their Teleporter Entrances first during
setup, so they don't have to go all the way back after building their sentries and
dispensers."

## What it is

ShouldBuildTeleporter in source/redbots3/behavior/engineerbuildteleporter.sp refuses
until the nest stands:

    if (HasObjectOfType(actor, TFObject_Sentry) == INVALID_ENT_REFERENCE)
        return false;
    if (HasObjectOfType(actor, TFObject_Dispenser) == INVALID_ENT_REFERENCE)
        return false;

The entrance spot is at spawn and the nest is not, so the order costs the engineer a
round trip he already made once. Setup is a fixed clock; the walk is spent out of it.

## What is being asked

Entrance first, while he is still standing in spawn, then sentry, then dispenser,
then exit beside the nest. Entrance before exit already holds and stays.

## What it must not break

The nest is what the wave is judged on. Nothing here may leave the sentry unbuilt or
unupgraded when the gate opens.

Two known interactions:

- After a shopping trip the engineer returns to the nest and puts up a level 3 sentry
  in one go, because MvM restores bought upgrades on rebuild. That behaviour is
  carried from the fork and is not to be disturbed. It also means the sentry costs
  much less setup time than a naive read of the build order suggests, which is part
  of why the entrance can afford to go first.
- KV_MvM_UpgradesDone in behavior/upgrade.sp detonates any sentry or dispenser that
  is short of finished, and everything when the nest has moved. An entrance built
  before that runs must not be caught by it, and must not be counted as the nest.

## Done when

Measured on the test-bed, both arms, several maps: the entrance stands before the
sentry does, the nest is still complete and upgraded at the gate, and the total
distance the engineer walks during setup drops.
notes:
## Wave breaks too, not only the first setup (2026-08-29)

The same walk is paid at every break, and worse: a sentry lost mid-wave means the
engineer starts the next one rebuilding from wherever he died. The ask is that a
break puts him at the spot he needs to build at rather than making him walk there,
and not just for the sentry: teleporter exit spot, dispenser spot, entrance spot.
Every wave should start with the nest standing.

The teleport back to the sentry spot after shopping already exists and is carried
from the fork; find it before adding a second mechanism. The class-behavior
TeleportEntity calls in nextbot_behavior.sp are stuck-recovery, not this.

Bounds this needs: it fires only in RoundState_BetweenRounds, only for a defender
engineer, only to a spot that already passed the build check, and a fixed cap on how
many times per break. A teleport that can fire during a wave is a cheat and a
crash-into-geometry both.

## The order, corrected (2026-08-29)

There is no teleporter entrance spot and there is no need for one. No map config
declares TeleporterEntrance, so NearestConfiguredSpot on
g_arrMapConfig.adtTeleporterEntranceLocation misses on every map and the code already
falls through to NearestSpawnPoint. Do not add spots to the configs to make this
work.

The sequence, hung off the end of shopping rather than off the start of setup:

1. He buys at the upgrade station.
2. He builds the entrance where he stands. He is in spawn, which is where an entrance
   belongs, so this costs him no walk at all.
3. He teleports to the nest.
4. Sentry, dispenser, exit, in that order, all without leaving the nest.

This drops the round trip from the problem instead of reordering it, and it is why
the entrance goes first: it is the only building whose right place is the place he is
already standing.

The named-spot path in ShouldBuildTeleporter can stay for a map that ever names one,
but the unnamed case is the case, and it should place at his own position rather than
walking out of spawn until the floor takes it.

## Instrumentation, before any behaviour change (2026-08-29)

The run report said nothing about the order or the walk, so it does now. In
testbed/stats/mvmbots_stats.sp:

- Every engineer's feet are read four times a second while the round state is
  BetweenRounds. A single-sample displacement over 200 units is a teleport and is
  summed apart from the walk; 200 is well past the 75 an engineer covers on foot in a
  quarter second. A respawn is not counted as a teleport: the last position is dropped
  whenever he is dead.
- player_builtobject records the second of the break each of the four buildings was
  placed on, first placement only, which is the build order and the cost of it.
- One "setup" line per engineer per wave carries break_s, walked, teleports,
  teleported and the four timestamps.

The telemetry sampler was not reused: it runs every five seconds, which is 1500 units
of walking, so it cannot tell a teleport from a sprint.

testbed/report/setup.go reads the lines and prints "the break, per engineer", and
diffs the two arms when the report is given two files. A building that never went up
is carried as -1 and counted, not averaged in as a zero.

## The baseline, measured (2026-08-29)

Three attempts, two waves each, Decoy, mod at 2.39.0 with the instrumentation and no
behaviour change. One engineer, Waldo.

  entrance   60s into the break, in 1 of 2 breaks
  sentry     28s
  dispenser  31s
  exit       30s, in 1 of 2 breaks
  walked     13308 units a break, and 3708 more teleported over 3 jumps

So the complaint is real and it is about thirty seconds: the entrance goes down half a
minute after the nest is finished, and the walk back to spawn is what fills the gap.

The three jumps confirm the teleport carried from the fork exists and that the sampler
sees it. Nothing was added to make them happen.

Two corrections to the instrumentation came out of this run:

- Every break_s was zero. mvm_begin_wave fires while the round state is still
  BetweenRounds, so the end-of-break assignment had not run when the line was written
  and a walk of seventeen thousand units had nothing to divide it by. It is read live
  now.
- A -1 timestamp means "not placed during this break", not "never built". A
  teleporter that survived the last wave is standing and is not built again, which is
  why wave 2 shows no entrance. The report says so rather than printing "never".

## First A/B, void (2026-08-29)

Two faults, one in the mod and one in this change, and the second voids the run.

The mod would not load at all on the first attempt. There is no player_calls_for_medic
game event, HookEvent throws on an event the game does not define, and that took
OnPluginStart down with it: RED filled with nobody and the runner refused the run.
That was mvm-w9b's hook and it is now a voicemenu command listener instead.

The run after it played, and its control arm is not the control. Restructuring
ShouldBuildTeleporter dropped the "no nest area, refuse" early return for the entrance
branch in both arms, not only the switched one, so with the switch off the engineer
could reach the entrance where he used to be refused. Both arms are void. Restored:
only the entrance-first path may run without a nest area, and only when it is on.

Worth carrying into the next run rather than forgetting: in one void ON attempt the
report says the sentry was never built, against 24s in the OFF arm beside it, and the
attempt cleared no waves. That is the exact failure this was bounded against. It is
not evidence yet, because the arm it is measured against was broken, but sentry_at_s
is the number to read first.

## Second A/B: build-where-he-stands is refused by the game (2026-08-29)

Three attempts each on Decoy, control restored.

               on     off
  waves cleared 2       4
  sentry built   attempt 1: never (on) against 17s (off)
                 attempt 2: never (on) against 15s (off)
                 attempt 3: 43s (on)  against  8s (off)
  walked        2862 to 14885 (on) against 14580 to 3786 (off)

With the switch on the engineer mostly built nothing at all. The low walk figure in
the on arm is not the win it looks like: it is a bot standing still.

The reading is that TF2 refuses a building inside the respawn room. That is where he
stands at the start of a break and where the upgrade station is, so every placement
was refused, he retried until the give-up timer, and the break went on it. The
original code already knew this and says so: it walks out of spawn "until the floor
takes it".

So "there is no spot, build it where he is" cannot work. The walk out of spawn is a
few hundred units and is not removable. The walk that is worth removing is the one
back from the nest, and that is the ordering alone.

Third arm now running: the hoist and the gate stay, the spot override is gone, and the
entrance goes up on the way out of spawn instead of after the nest.

## Third A/B: the ordering alone is worse too, and the change is out (2026-08-29)

The spot override gone, the hoist and the gate kept. Three attempts each on Decoy.

               on     off
  waves cleared 2       4
  entrance      never in any attempt, against 31s and 32s in two of three off attempts
  sentry        29s, 9s, 8s, against 12s, never, 12s
  walked        8102 to 9926, against 11152 to 13492

The nest is built again, so the respawn-room fault is gone. The entrance is not: with
the switch on it is never built at all, which is worse than the thing it was meant to
fix on exactly the number it was meant to fix.

The mechanism is in CTFBotMvMEngineerBuildTeleporter_OnStart. The route out of spawn
is computed "while he is at his nest, which is the only place the whole route can be
read from". Building the entrance first means there is no nest, so SpawnRoutePoints
has nothing to read the route from, TeleporterStandPoint returns false, and
m_bTeleporterGaveUp latches for the rest of the break.

Three implementations, three rejections, so the change is removed rather than left off
behind a switch: source/redbots3/behavior/engineerbuildteleporter.sp and
engineeridle.sp are reverted and FEATURE_ENGINEER_ENTRANCE_FIRST is deleted. The
instrumentation stays; it is what produced all of this.

## What the next attempt has to solve first

Not the ordering. The route. Anything that builds the entrance before the nest has to
compute the way out of spawn without a nest to read it from, and has to stop
m_bTeleporterGaveUp latching on the first refusal of a break. Until that is answered
the ordering cannot be measured at all, because every arm of it ends in the same
give-up.

The baseline stands and the complaint stands: entrance at 60s against a sentry at 28s.

title: Sniper bots stand in spawn again, on the stock loadout
description:
FIXED at the root in v2.38.0. loadouts.sp did not give a stock sniper the
sniper mission, so the game never handed him a CTFBotSniperLurk.

## The cause, exactly

SetMission(client, CTFBot_MISSION_SNIPER) is what makes the game give a sniper
his lurk. It sat behind a lookup that cannot succeed for a stock loadout:

  if (TF2Econ_GetItemClassName(m_iWeaponPrimary[client], itemClassname, ...))

A stock primary leaves m_iWeaponPrimary at TF_ITEMDEF_DEFAULT, which is not an
item definition, so the call fails and the whole block is skipped. No mission,
no lurk, and a sniper who stands where he shopped for the rest of the mission.

A Machina or Heatmaker has a real definition index, reads back as
tf_weapon_sniperrifle, gets the mission and works. That is the stock-only split
Peppy reported, and it is not a coincidence of timing or of the weapon swap.

events.sp:367 calls SetMission unconditionally for a sniper when custom loadouts
are off, so only a server running them on could ever see this. The test-bed's
default is off, which is why it never reproduced in a day of trying.

## The fix

A sniper carrying the default primary is carrying the stock rifle: there is
nothing to look up and no lookup that can fail, so he is given the mission
directly.

## What was wrong before this

Four attempts, all treating symptoms, each refuted by Peppy on his own server:

1. Walking him to a spot under our own behaviour. Sniper damage 16430 to 479.
2. Restarting his intention after the loadout, on the theory that the Machina's
   weapon swap restarts the behaviour. The restart runs him through the same
   missing mission again, and he stayed in spawn.
3. Timing the rescue on the stuck watchdog. Teammates shoving him past
   STUCK_RADIUS reset the timer, so the stall count never climbed.
4. Sending him to the front, and then letting him fight during the wave. Those
   two are v2.36.0 and v2.37.0 and they still stand as a safety net, but they are
   not the fix.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The cheapest theory is mostly ruled out already.

All 27 map configs carry a SniperSpot block, so an unconfigured map is only a
map with no config file at all. Every stock MvM map has one: bigrock, coaltown,
decoy, ghost_town, mannhattan, mannworks, rottenburg. So on the stock maps he
has somewhere to go and the fault is elsewhere.

That leaves two: the break freeze back by another route, or he is being refused
a position for a new reason. Both are in ShouldTakeUpPosition and what suspends
around it.

It also leaves community maps, which is worth asking about: a map with no config
gets no SniperSpot, SetupSniperSpotHints takes his team off every hint, and he
has nowhere to walk. Ask the reporter which map this was on. If it is a
community map the answer is a config, not code, and it is the same shape as
mvm-tz9.

Still no sniper in any test-bed lineup by default, which is how the original
survived. Any run for this has to name the class explicitly.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Reading the code before writing anything, since two fixes have already been
tried here and one was measured and thrown away.

ShouldTakeUpPosition refuses a sniper who has a rifle, and only him:

  case TFClass_Sniper: return !HasSniperRifle(client);

So the stock loadout is exactly the case that gets refused, and the Huntsman is
not. That matches the report word for word, and it is deliberate: a rifle sniper
is supposed to be walking to a hint of his own instead.

SetupSniperSpotHints creates those hints with team 2, which is RED, from the map
config's SniperSpot list. All 27 configs carry one, so the hints exist. What is
not known is whether he reaches them.

Two things it could be, and they need different fixes:

- the hints exist and he cannot path to them, or the sniping behaviour never
  starts. Then he stands in spawn with nothing on his stack, and the fix is a
  fallback for a sniper with no reachable spot.
- the behaviour runs and he lurks somewhere unhelpful. Then he is not stuck at
  all and the report is about where he chooses to stand.

The run tells them apart in one line, because the report prints 'no behaviour in
X per cent of samples' per bot. Queued: Decoy with a sniper in the lineup, which
the test-bed has never done by default and is why this survived twice.

Not writing the rejected fix again. mvm-pvt measured making him fight without a
hint: 4521 damage lurking against 570 attacking.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Peppy says every map, not one. That rules out the map config theory: all 27
carry a SniperSpot list and the hints are created on team RED from it, so if it
were the hints this would be per map.

It is also a regression. mvm-pvt measured him working on Decoy on 25 August:
SniperLurk under his stack, 1970 damage and 14 kills over three waves. Something
since then stopped him.

What has landed on the bot code since: the spawn recovery for bots that cannot
leave spawn, path computes routed through the helpers with a length cap, the
stuck watchdog changes, the wedge recovery and the nest move. Any of the first
three could plausibly leave a sniper who walks a long way to a far hint with no
path and nowhere to go.

The hypothesis worth testing first costs nothing extra: mvm-pvt's fault was 'no
behaviour for the whole break'. sm_redbots_feature_watch_idle_bots exists for
exactly that and is off by default. So the queued run is an A/B on it with a
sniper in the lineup.

- idle percentage drops with the watchdog on: it is the freeze again, and the
  watchdog is both the diagnosis and a fix
- both arms the same: he has behaviour and is choosing where to stand, which is
  a different bug and the fallback in mvm-pvt is the wrong answer for it

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Correcting the framing: this is not a regression from the recent work.

1.10 ships defenderbots v2.17.1, which predates everything I have changed this
week. And v2.17.1 already contains both earlier sniper fixes:

- fb18c1b, 22 August, the break freeze fix that closed mvm-pvt
- e20deb3, 26 August, Decoy's restored sniper spots, which closed mvm-tz9

All 27 map configs carry a SniperSpot list at v2.17.1, the same as today, so the
missing-hints theory is dead for the shipped build too.

So the sniper is broken with both known fixes in place, and the reporter says it
may predate 1.10. That makes it long standing rather than something introduced,
and it means mvm-pvt's close was wrong: it rested on one forced Decoy lineup
measuring 1970 damage and 14 kills, and whatever that measured it was not what
players get.

The queued run is on the current build, which is far ahead of v2.17.1. That is
worth knowing on its own: if the sniper works there, the answer for 1.10 players
is the update, and if he does not, the fault survives everything since.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Measured on the current build, and the sniper works there.

Decoy, mvm_decoy_advanced, sniper in the lineup, two waves:

  45 sniper samples
  41 in MainAction < TacticalMonitor < ScenarioMonitor < SniperLurk
  41 distinct positions, moving up to 2184 units from where he started
  2926 damage over the run

So he is not standing in spawn and he is not without behaviour. SniperLurk is on
his stack for 91 per cent of samples, which is the state mvm-pvt measured as
working.

That matters for the report because 1.10 ships defenderbots v2.17.1 and this is
v2.27.0. Something between the two fixed him, or Decoy was never the broken map.
Peppy says every map, so the next run has to be another one before this closes:
Mannworks is where the report names, and Mannworks is also where the mission
will not start, so it needs a mission that does.

Not closing on one map. mvm-pvt was closed on one forced Decoy lineup and the
players still saw it broken, and repeating that would be repeating the mistake
rather than the measurement.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Reported with detail that changes the shape of this.

Decoy, three snipers: one reached a spot and two stayed at spawn after buying.
Two were stock and one a Heatmaker, and the Heatmaker is the one that moved. It
then left the spot and settled at the bomb drop instead.

Two readings and one run separates them:

- the spots are claimed one bot each and the rest have nowhere to go, in which
  case the Heatmaker won by arriving first and the split by weapon is
  coincidence
- or the weapon really does decide

The second is not supported by the code. HasSniperRifle goes through
WeaponID_IsSniperRifle, which covers TF_WEAPON_SNIPERRIFLE, _DECAP and
_CLASSIC, so a Heatmaker counts as a rifle exactly as the stock one does and
both take the same branch of ShouldTakeUpPosition.

Decoy carries six sniper spots, from Config_LoadMap, so three snipers should
have room whatever the claiming rule is.

The second symptom is the more useful one: a sniper that reached his spot and
then went to the bomb drop is a sniper whose lurk ended and who fell through to
something else. That is a behaviour ending, not a spot missing, and it would
explain both halves if the lurk never starts for the other two.

Run to do: Decoy with three snipers, reading each one's action stack and
position over time. The report already prints no behaviour per bot and the
samples carry the stack, so one run says which of the two it is.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Correcting myself: the stock-only split is real, and the mechanism is a race in
the loadout swap.

A custom loadout replaces the primary by removing it first:

  TF2_RemoveWeaponSlot(client, TFWeaponSlot_Primary);
  ...
  primary = GiveItemToPlayer(client, itemClassname, ...);

Between those two lines the sniper holds no primary. HasSniperRifle asks
GetPlayerWeaponSlot for the primary and returns false when it is -1, so during
that window a Heatmaker sniper reads as a sniper with no rifle, and
ShouldTakeUpPosition returns true for him where it returns false for every stock
one.

That single difference explains the whole report:

- the Heatmaker moved because he was briefly treated as having no rifle, so he
  took up a position like any other class
- the two stock snipers never had that window, stayed excluded, and had nothing
  but a lurk that is not starting
- the Heatmaker later settled at the bomb drop rather than a sniper spot,
  because taking up a position is what sends a bot to the front. It was never
  going to a sniper spot: it went where the fighting classes go

So the Heatmaker is not working, it is failing differently and looking like
working. The real fault is underneath both: a stock rifle sniper is excluded
from taking up a position and the lurk he is meant to rely on does not start.

Two things follow. HasSniperRifle answering false for a bot mid-swap is a bug on
its own, since any caller can be asked during that window. And the fix for this
bead is whatever makes the lurk start, not another fallback: mvm-pvt already
measured making him fight instead at 4521 damage lurking against 570 attacking.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The reporter is right and my last comment had the mechanism wrong. Taking up a
position sends a bot to the front, so it cannot explain a Heatmaker that reached
a sniper spot.

The actual difference is a weapon change that a stock sniper never gets.

DHookCallback_ManageRegularWeapons_Post schedules Timer_GiveCustomLoadout a
tenth of a second after the game hands a bot its weapons. That timer removes and
re-gives each slot the loadout names:

  TF2_RemoveWeaponSlot(client, TFWeaponSlot_Primary);
  primary = GiveItemToPlayer(client, itemClassname, ...);

A sniper with a Heatmaker has his primary removed and re-equipped. A sniper on
stock has m_iWeaponPrimary at the default, so nothing is touched and no weapon
change happens.

EquipPlayerWeapon changes the active weapon, and a nextbot re-evaluates its
behaviour when that happens. So the Heatmaker sniper gets his behaviour
restarted a tenth of a second after spawn and the restarted one finds his spot.
The stock sniper is never restarted, so whatever state he is left in at spawn is
the state he keeps, and he keeps standing there.

That also explains the drift: the Heatmaker's lurk ended later and nothing
restarted him a second time.

So the fault is that the sniper lurk does not start at spawn, and a weapon change
hides it. The fix is whatever makes it start, and the shape to try first is
resetting a rifle sniper's intention once after spawn, which is what the weapon
change does by accident.

The queued three stock sniper run tests this directly: if the weapon is the
difference, all three stay in spawn and none of them is claiming a spot the
others wanted.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The sniper bug and the watchdog crash are the same bug, and there is a
backtrace.

Three stock snipers on Decoy killed the server. The core symbolises to:

  #3  WatchDogHandler()
  #5  CNavArea::AddToOpenList()
  #6  NavAreaBuildPath<CTFBotPathCost>(...)
  #7  Path::Compute<CTFBotPathCost>(...)
  #8  CTFBotSniperLurk::Update(CTFBot*, float)

So a sniper whose lurk cannot reach its spot recomputes a path on every update,
NavAreaBuildPath walks the mesh, and the watchdog kills the server. The bots
standing in spawn and the crash are one fault seen from two ends.

This also corrects me. I concluded the path cost mechanism was refuted because
v2.30.0 timed every compute and logged nothing over 20ms. That instrumentation
wraps RepathToPos and RepathToTarget, which are the mod's own calls.
CTFBotSniperLurk::Update is the game's code calling Path::Compute directly, and
nothing I added ever saw it. I measured the wrong thing and trusted the result.

The backtrace is kept at results/crash-sniperlurk-backtrace.txt.

The fix is now a crash fix, not a cosmetic one: a lurk that cannot reach its
spot has to stop asking. Either the sniper reaches his spot, or the lurk ends
and he does something else.

title: Bots replaced mid-wave never shop at the break they come back in
description:
Reported: 'i tried replacing all my bots after wave 1 start, and they just did
not buy anything! as if they did not have any money'.

## What is certain

A team change during a running wave is held: Command_ReseatBots sets
m_bRecyclePending, says the new team takes effect when the wave ends, and
Reseat_OnBreak does the kicking.

Reseat_OnBreak is called from Event_MvmWaveComplete and Event_MvmWaveFailed, in
both cases at the top, above the comment that reads 'Before anything below sends
the engineers off to shop'. So the old bots are kicked at the moment the break
opens, and the replacements join after it.

## What is not certain

Whether that ordering is the fault. A bot that joins through the normal path
gets SetCurrencyWithBundles(GetStartingCurrency + GetAcquiredCreditsOfAllWaves)
in events.sp, so it should hold the money the wave earned. 'As if they did not
have any money' is a symptom, and a bot that has money but was never sent to
shop looks the same from a seat.

Two candidates, and they are not exclusive:

- the break's shopping pass has already gone by the time the new bots are in,
  so they hold their credits and never spend them
- the credits are genuinely wrong, and the join path grants less than the wave
  earned

## How to tell them apart

The log answers it without a guess. Each break prints one 'Shopping: <name>
stopped, ... N credits left' per bot, and the recycle prints 'Reseat: recycled N
bot(s) held from mid-wave'. Replace the team mid-wave, then read the break that
follows:

- no Shopping line at all for the new names: the ordering is the fault
- a Shopping line saying 0 credits left with nothing bought: the credits are

This is worth a testbed run rather than a play-test, since the reseat and the
break are both scriptable.
close_reason:
Not a bug. The reporter had the purchase-in-chat setting off, so the buys
happened and nothing printed them.

Worth keeping the shape of this one: the whole bead was built on an absence.
'They did not buy anything' was read off missing chat lines, and the setting
that writes those lines is off by default. An absent log line says nothing about
whether the thing happened.

One loose end from reading the code, recorded here rather than left as an open
P0 nobody has seen: Reseat_OnBreak runs at the top of Event_MvmWaveComplete,
above the comment that says 'Before anything below sends the engineers off to
shop'. Whether a bot that rejoins there still catches that break's shopping pass
is untested. No symptom has ever pointed at it, so it stays a note.

title: The medic ignores a player calling for him
description:
Discord, 2026-08-27.

Cowser: "Medic bots must prioritize healing players over bots, especially when
calling for a medic"

omaewh4: "when calling him he should go to the calling player. I will check if
it's possible in the bots ai, I don't know if they have this kind of signal"

## What it is

A human presses the medic call and the bot medic carries on healing whichever
bot it had picked. From the player's side the call does nothing, which reads as
the medic being broken rather than as the medic having other plans.

Two parts, and the first is the whole of the ask:

- a player who calls takes the beam
- a player outranks a bot for the beam generally, called or not

## Is the signal there

That is the open question omaewh4 named. The game fires the medic call as a
voice command, so the hook is `player_calls_for_medic` or the voice menu, and
the mod would need to note who called and for how long that lasts.

## What it must not break

mvm-eil is the medic's patient and mvm-72s measured the churn: he re-picked the
biggest body every two seconds until MEDIC_PATIENT_MARGIN cut it to seven
changes a wave. A call that overrides the pick has to not reintroduce that
churn, so the call wants a hold time rather than a one-frame override.

The beam is on somebody 27% of the time. Whether answering calls raises that or
only moves it is a measurement, not a guess.
notes:
Peppy, 2026-08-29: "having a way to call Medics to try and heal you would be a nice addition as well". Second report of the same ask, so this is P0. The call is the whole of it: a human who calls takes the beam.

## Written, behind sm_redbots_feature_medic_answers_call, off (2026-08-29)

The signal is there, which was the open question omaewh4 named: the game fires
player_calls_for_medic on the voice command. Hooked in source/redbots3/events.sp, and
a bot calling is ignored, since bots sorting themselves out is not the ask.

A call is a countdown and not a flag, because the game says nothing about the call
still being wanted or having been met. Ten seconds, restarted by pressing again.

The ranking is in BiggestBody in nextbot_behavior.sp, which is where the beam is
decided. A caller outranks a player, a player outranks any body, and below that the
Heavy-then-maximum-health ranking is untouched. Both halves of what was asked for.

MEDIC_PATIENT_MARGIN and the keep-the-beam rule still apply, and neither new reason
can bring back the churn measured on Bavarian Botbash wave 3: that came of ranking on
maximum health, which several bodies sit within a few points of, so the winner flipped
every ask. Whether somebody is a player does not flip, and a call runs down and does
not come back on its own.

## It cannot be measured on the test-bed

The test-bed plays with nobody on it, so no client ever calls and no client is ever a
player. The feature is a no-op there by construction: isPlayer is false for every
seat. A run can only show that nothing else moved.

Judging this needs a person on RED pressing the call and reporting whether the beam
comes. Until that happens the switch stays off and this bead stays open.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Asked for again, with a design question worth writing down: when does the medic
stop following the caller.

The bead already says the call wants a hold time rather than a one-frame
override, because mvm-72s measured the churn a re-pick every two seconds caused.
It did not say what ends the hold.

Candidates, and they are not exclusive:

- a fixed hold, ten or fifteen seconds, so the call is a request rather than a
  lease. Simplest, and the churn guard is the same MEDIC_PATIENT_MARGIN idea
  already in place.
- until the caller is healed, which reads as what a player means by the call and
  ends on its own.
- until the wave ends. That is the suggestion here and it is the longest of the
  three: a medic bound to one player for a whole wave is a medic who ignores the
  five others, and the beam is only on somebody 27 per cent of the time as it is.

The wave end is the right place to clear whatever the hold is, whichever is
chosen, since a hold that survives a break is a medic following somebody who has
respawned somewhere else.

Suggest the first with the wave end as a backstop: a fixed hold, cleared early
when the caller is full, and cleared unconditionally at the break. That answers
the call, cannot strand the medic, and is measurable against the 27 per cent.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
One thing the call must not assume it inherits.

The patient pick already drops a dead man: BiggestBody skips anyone not alive,
so a dead patient never sets currentStands and never gets the 25 health
stickiness margin that would otherwise hold the beam on him. The medic re-picks
at the next nudge, MEDIC_PATIENT_INTERVAL, so two seconds at worst.

A call hold would be a separate field from the patient pick, so it does not
inherit that. A medic holding a call from a player who then dies would keep
walking to a corpse until the hold expired.

So the hold needs its own three exits, not two: the caller is healed, the caller
died, or the break arrives.

title: The engineer freezes and never builds anything
description:
Discord, 2026-08-27.

Philiard: "the Engineer bot seems a bit broken. At least on Mean Machines on
Mannworks, he gets permanently stuck in this one spot and never actually places
any of his buildings."

Permanently, and no buildings at all. A team without a sentry on an Advanced
mission is a team that loses, so this is not a bot playing badly: it is a seat
doing nothing for the whole run.

## Why P0

Half of what this mod does is engineer behaviour. An engineer that never builds
takes the nest, the dispenser and the teleporters out of the team at once.

## What is already known

Three beads describe the same shape on other maps, and this is the fourth
report:

- mvm-6rt, freezes during setup on Decoy
- mvm-ipf, stuck inside a prop on Mannhunt
- mvm-zx0, leaves the nest mid-wave hunting metal and gets stuck on geometry

And the test-bed has caught it in the log without anybody reporting it:

  stuck: Waldo (engineer) at 346 551 544 for 12s,
         MainAction < TacticalMonitor < DefenderEngineerIdle < ScenarioMonitor

Twelve seconds later the engine watchdog killed the server, inside
NavAreaBuildPath. So a stuck engineer is not only a lost seat, it is a suspect
in the crash on mvm-cf3.

## Where to start

The stuck line names the action stack, so the test-bed can already say which
behaviour is holding it. Mannworks with Mean Machines is a reproduction nobody
had before: run it, read the stack, and find what the engineer is waiting for
that never comes.

kelly-cs's spawn recovery in v2.20.0 moves a bot that cannot leave spawn. This
is a bot that has left spawn and then stops, so that recovery does not cover it.
close_reason: Fixed and measured on the reproduction. A wedged bot is moved to the nearest walkable nav area after three stucks at one spot, in the watchdog where a behaviour reset cannot undo it. Mannworks with Mean Machines went from crashing at 0 waves with no sentries built to 4 of 4 waves, no crash, and 42 sentries. The remaining cause, whatever keeps walking him into that spot, is filed separately.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Reproduced, root-caused, and my first two attempts at the fix were both wrong in
the same way.

## The reproduction

Mannworks with Mean Machines, on the test-bed:

  stuck: Wesley (engineer) at 1014 885 274 for 12s,
         MainAction < TacticalMonitor < DefenderBuildSentrygun < DefenderEngineerIdle

Nineteen times, the same coordinates, inside the sentry build action, and never
a sentry. That is Philiard's report exactly.

## The cause: two timers chasing each other

STUCK_TIME is 12.0 and SENTRY_REACH_TIME is 12.0.

The stuck watchdog fires at twelve seconds and calls ResetIntentionInterface,
which resets the whole behaviour tree. That restarts the build action, whose
OnStart re-arms the reach deadline to now plus twelve. So the deadline that
would have made him give the spot up is pushed forward every time he is rescued,
and he is rescued into the same trap for the rest of the mission.

## Two wrong fixes, both defeated by the same reset

First I added the missing branch: the give-up path only ran when he was already
near the spot, so an engineer who never arrives never reached it. Real gap, and
useless here, because it hangs off the same deadline. The verification run
proved it: the bug happened and the new log line never appeared.

Then I counted stucks per attempt, and marked the count in OnStart. Same fault.
OnStart runs on every reset, so the mark restarted alongside the thing it was
counting.

## What survives a reset

The mark belongs to the nest area rather than to the attempt. It resets when the
engineer is sent somewhere new, and not when he is merely restarted at the same
place. Two stucks against one nest and the spot is the suspect rather than the
walk.

## Not verified yet

The run after the first fix came back with four waves, sentries built and lost
every wave, and no stuck line. That is not evidence for the fix: the new code
path never ran, so what changed was the draw and not the code. This bug is
intermittent and one clean run does not clear it.

One number from the day's log worth its own look: 333 sentry attempts started,
153 built one, and 166 "ended with nothing".

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Fixed, and measured on the reproduction. The fix is in the stuck watchdog, which
is the third place I tried and the only one a behaviour reset cannot reach.

## Before and after, Mannworks with Mean Machines

  before   crashed at 0 waves; engineer stuck 9 to 11 times at 1014 885 274
  after    4 of 4 waves, no crash, the wedge recovery fired 4 times

  Stuck: Bob was wedged at 1014 885 274, moved to 1267 804 267
  Stuck: Bob was wedged at 1014 885 274, moved to 1029 761 267
  Stuck: Bob was wedged at 1014 885 274, moved to 1120 662 267

Sentries in the run after: 163 attempts started, 42 ended with a sentry. Before
the fix he built none at all.

## What the instrumentation showed, which two guesses had missed

The mark I added to the build action reset 26 times, because the nest area
churns underneath it. Every restart looked like a fresh attempt, so a per-attempt
or per-nest counter can never accumulate.

And the log said what the bug actually is: the same coordinates across different
nests. He is wedged in geometry, not aiming at a bad spot. ResetIntentionInterface
does not move a wedged bot, so it comes back to the identical wedge and asks for
another path.

## Honest limits

He still wedges at 1014 885 274 repeatedly, three of the four recoveries from
that one spot. This is a safety net rather than a cure: something still walks him
in there, and that is worth its own bead.

117 of 163 sentry attempts "ended with nothing" against 42 that built one. High,
and not explained by this.

One run each side.

title: The server dies in CBaseNPC's serial refresher, every frame hook
description:
The crash on this test-bed, and probably the one players report. Four of six
cores from one evening carry the same stack, symbolised:

  #0 std::_Hashtable<unsigned int, std::pair<unsigned int const,
       std::unique_ptr<ToolsNetworkRefresher> > >::_M_begin
  #2 std::unordered_map<unsigned int,
       std::unique_ptr<ToolsNetworkRefresher> >::begin
  #3 Hook_Frame at CBaseNPC/extension/serialrefresher.cpp:60
  #4 SourceModBase::ProcessGameFrameHooks(bool)
  ...
  #9 SV_Think -> SV_Frame -> _Host_RunFrame_Server

SIGSEGV walking the first bucket of an unordered_map keyed by entity serial, in
a per-frame hook the CBaseNPC extension installs. Reading a freed or half-torn
map, every frame, so it fires whenever the map is in that state when the frame
comes round.

## What it is not

Not the mod's SourcePawn. The crash is inside the extension's own C++ frame
hook, above SourceMod and below nothing of ours.

Not new. core.104 and core.76 predate this evening's work entirely.

## The other two cores, for completeness

  core.2666  MapEntity_ParseEntity, which is map load
  core.104   WatchDogHandler, the engine killing a long frame

The watchdog one had a stuck engineer in DefenderEngineerIdle 12 seconds before
it, which is the mvm-6rt / mvm-zx0 / mvm-ipf family rather than this.

## Why P0

It is the thing that ends runs, and it ends them silently: the launcher reports
it as the server stopping. apw-r85 in tf2-archipelago is a Windows
STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION with no minidump, twice in two sessions, and an
extension crashing in a frame hook is exactly the shape that would produce.
Worth checking whether the two are the same bug before hunting them separately.

## Where to start

serialrefresher.cpp is small. The map holds a refresher per entity serial and
Hook_Frame walks it; something removes an entry or destroys the map while that
walk is live, or an entity teardown leaves a stale key. Entity removal during a
frame is the obvious suspect, and that is a thing this mod does a lot of:
buildings, bots joining and leaving, sentry busters detonating.

Check the CBaseNPC version pinned in testbed/versions.env against upstream
first: a fixed bug upstream is cheaper than a fixed bug here.
close_reason: Not a CBaseNPC bug. The testbed was copying a live mapped .so over itself because build.sh gave the staged prebuilt extensions a new mtime on every build. Fixed with cp -p, verified stable across rebuilds.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Read the source. The map is populated from exactly one place in this mod, which
makes the experiment cheap.

gRefreshers is a file-global unordered_map keyed by entity ref handle, and the
only thing that inserts into it is Tools_RefreshEntity, reached from the
CBaseEntity.DispatchUpdateTransmitState native. This mod calls that native once:

  source/redbots3/util.sp:1310  RemoveEffects
  source/redbots3/util.sp:1304  RemoveEffects(sapper, EF_NODRAW)

So the whole exposure is sappers, created in the Spy path. Nothing else in the
mod ever puts an entry in that map.

## What the stack actually says

The faulting PC is 0xded872c7, which is in no loaded module: a call through a
pointer that is not code. Refresh() is marked noinline precisely so it shows as
its own frame and it is absent, so the fault is in Hook_Frame's own loop, on
the unique_ptr it just read out of the map. A destroyed element still in the
map, or a map mutated while the loop holds an iterator into it.

Hook_Frame erases while iterating, which is correct on its own. What is not
guarded is reentrancy: Refresh() calls add_explicit_delete into the engine, and
anything that reaches DispatchUpdateTransmitState again during that call
emplaces into the same map, which can rehash and leave the loop's iterator
pointing at freed storage.

Refresh() also does:

  auto edict = entity->GetNetworkable()->GetEdict();
  add_explicit_delete(gFrameSnapshot, edict->m_EdictIndex);

with no null check on GetEdict, which is null for an entity on its way out.
That is a second, simpler crash in the same function, and it would not produce
this stack.

## The experiment

Cheap, and it is an A/B rather than an argument. Take the
DispatchUpdateTransmitState call out of RemoveEffects, clear EF_NODRAW without
it, and run the same length of test-bed time. The crash landed roughly every
twenty minutes tonight, so a pair of hour-long runs is enough to see it move.

The risk to check in the same run is what the call was there for: a sapper that
never gets its transmit state refreshed may stay invisible. Watch a Spy bot sap
something and confirm the sapper draws.

Upstream is already on the latest release, 1.15.4.126, so there is no cheaper
fix to take.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Root cause found, and it is not CBaseNPC. The bead as filed is wrong and the
title with it.

## What the core actually says

  si_addr  0x1e2188
  si_code  1 (SEGV_MAPERR, address not mapped)
  eip      Hook_Frame+7:  mov 0x1e2188,%esi

0x1e2188 is the *link-time* address of gRefreshers+8. The real one, once the
library is loaded at 0xdee13000, is 0xdeff5188 -- and readelf shows an
R_386_RELATIVE relocation at file offset 0x000532c9, which is exactly that
instruction's operand. The extension carries DT_TEXTREL, so that operand is
patched by the loader at startup.

The instruction read the unpatched value. So the text page had reverted to its
on-disk bytes.

And gRefreshers itself, read out of the core at the relocated address, is a
perfectly well-formed empty map: bucket count 1, element count 0, node list
null. Nothing had ever been inserted. The sapper path never ran. There was no
use-after-free and no reentrancy, and the analysis in the comment above about
Refresh() and rehashing was wrong.

## Why the page reverted

testbed/entrypoint.sh copies the staged tree into the game tree every thirty
seconds for as long as the server lives, and install_addons already carries the
comment explaining why that is dangerous: cp truncates before it writes, and
truncating a file the server has mapped pulls the pages out from under it. The
guard is cp -ru, so an unchanged tree is never rewritten.

The staged tree was changing. testbed/build.sh copied the prebuilt extensions
into the stage with a plain cp on every build, which gives them a new timestamp
even though the bytes are identical. Any build while a container was up made
the stage newer, and the installer copied a live mapped .so over itself within
thirty seconds.

Proven from the timestamps: staged 23:06:16, installed 23:06:42.

I ran testbed/build.sh several times tonight with a run in flight. That is what
crashed those servers. The crashes were mine, not the mod's, and not the
reseat's.

## Fixed

build.sh now copies the prebuilt extensions and gamedata with cp -p. The
prebuilt tree is fetched once and never changes, so the staged timestamps are
now the upstream ones and stable: verified across two consecutive rebuilds,
mtime unchanged, so the installer's -u has nothing to do.

Closing. The remaining real crash of the evening is the watchdog one, which is
a stuck engineer and belongs to mvm-6rt / mvm-zx0 / mvm-ipf.

title: Bots do not buy resistance upgrades, and the Scouts die for it
description:
Swagdoll:

"Also, the bots really need to buy resistance upgrades, especially Scouts, since
they just keep dying without them"

The shopping list has no resistances on it for the combat classes. A Scout has
125 health and is the class most often in the giants' line of fire, so it is the
one that notices first, but the complaint is about the list, not about the
Scout.

Measure before touching the weights: count deaths per class per wave against
which damage type killed them (bullet, blast, fire), then check whether buying
the matching resistance moves that count. A resistance the bot never gets shot
by is money it did not spend on damage.

Sits next to mvm-8ws, which argues the opposite way for the Engineer: PDA first,
resistances after. Both are the same question of what the priority list ranks.
design:
## Measured on the testbed, six waves of Decoy

38 shopping trips. The wave read is not the fault, which was the leading
hypothesis and is now dead:

    23 trips  wave deals blast=1 bullet=1 fire=0
     9 trips  wave deals blast=0 bullet=1 fire=1
     6 trips  wave deals blast=0 bullet=1 fire=0

Every trip saw at least one damage type. `WaveHasClassIcon` reads
`tf_objective_resource` correctly, and it reads it in time: no trip came back
with all three zero, including the first wave. So resistances were priced at
210 and not 25 on every trip of the run.

Why the trips ended:

    29  nothing left worth buying
     9  the game refused one

The 29 stopped holding 38 to 88 credits, which is under the price of anything
left, so they spent what they had. A bot that stops because the ranking ran out
while holding 88 credits is not a bot that skipped a resistance: at 210 the
resistance outranks most of the table and is bought early, not last.

## What that leaves

The premise of this bead is now doubly wrong. The resistances are on the list,
and the list is being read with the right wave in front of it. Swagdoll's Scouts
were dying for some other reason, and raising the weight would be changing a
number that is already being acted on.

Two candidates, neither measured:

- The resistance is bought but only to tier one, and one tier is not enough
  against the wave that killed him. The instrument for that is what level each
  bot reaches, which nothing logs.
- The Scout dies to something the resistance does not cover, or dies before it
  matters. `testbed/results/` records defender deaths per wave but not what
  killed them.

The nine "the game refused one" trips are worth a look on their own. The
upgrade file already says a refusal repeats until the window closes, so a bot
that hits one may be spending less than it could.

## Do not move a weight on this bead

Not without an A/B in the testbed showing the change clears the spread, which
is the rule in docs/testbed-metrics.md and the rule the upgrade table states
about itself.
close_reason: Premise disproved by measurement, not by argument. 38 shopping trips over six waves of Decoy: every trip saw at least one damage type, so resistances were priced at 210 rather than 25 on every trip, and the wave read was correct including on wave 1. The bots do buy resistances and the list is read with the right wave in front of it. Raising a weight here would change a number already being acted on. What actually killed Swagdoll's Scouts is a separate question and needs instrumentation that does not exist; filed as its own bead.

title: The wave start stutters
description:
SakakunAn: "i'm trying to play but somewhat my local server is lagging when the
wave starts"

omaewh4, on the cause: "lots of stuff happens programmatically at the start of a
wave, it's 'normal', I did not focus yet too much on performance, and tried to

Known and accepted for now; filed so it is not lost.

The path cap was measured against the same map and does not clear the spread now that the pathological case is gone, so it stays off by default. The residual hitching is filed separately at its own size.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Numbers for it, from 30 waves of test-bed runs on the current build. The stats plugin has been measuring frame times all along and nothing had read them for this.

  mean frame                                   15.0 ms, which is the tick
  worst frame inside a wave                    median 113 ms, max 172 ms
  frames over the slow mark, per wave          median 18, max 43
  frames stalled, per wave                     median 1, max 8
  worst frame in the break before a wave       median 121 ms, MAX 1796 ms

The last line is where the stutter lives. Inside a wave the worst frame is about
seven ticks; in the break before one it reaches 1796 ms, which is more than a
second of the server not moving, and it lands right where a player is watching
the wave bar. Twelve hundred of that was once traced to the map still loading,
so the number wants splitting by how long the map has been up before it is
trusted; docs/testbed-metrics.md has that warning.

Worth knowing about the two known causes, both now fixed, because a rerun should
show whether anything is left: an unbounded nav mesh search killed frames badly
enough to trip the watchdog (mvm-297, fixed with PATHS_PER_FRAME), and
IsPathToVectorPossible reads like a cheap predicate and is a full NavAreaBuildPath.

The 'stall' event the plugin writes did not fire once across those 30 waves, so
whatever FRAME_STALL_MS is set to is above what these runs produce; a report of
a visible stutter at 113 ms means the threshold, not the server, is what needs
changing before this can be measured from a results file.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
A symbolised stack for the watchdog kill, which this bead has only had numbers
for until now.

  #3 WatchDogHandler
  #4 <signal handler called>
  #5 CNavArea::GetZ            nav_area.cpp:267
  #6 CNavArea::ComputePortal   nav_area.cpp:458
  #7 CNavArea::ComputeAdjacentConnectionHeightChange
  #8 SMPathFollowerCost::operator()
  #9 NavAreaBuildPath          nav_mesh.cpp:369
  #10 Path::Compute

So the frame that took too long was a path computation, which is the family
mvm-297 already fixed once with PATHS_PER_FRAME. The watchdog fires inside
NavAreaBuildPath rather than anywhere in this mod's own SourcePawn.

Twice tonight, on two different runs, and the machine was paging both times.
The other one had "stuck: Waldo (engineer) for 12s, DefenderEngineerIdle" a few
seconds before it, which fits: a bot that cannot reach where it wants to go asks
for a path again and again.

## What this changes about the bead

The bead says the stall event never fired across thirty waves, and the numbers
beside it say the worst frame in a break reached 1796 ms. FRAME_REPORT_MS is
250, so a 1796 ms frame should have written one. Those two statements cannot
both be right, and I would check which before building anything on either.

Worth doing next, in this order:

1. Settle whether the stall event fires at all. If it does, the earlier reading
   was of a file that had them and nothing read them.
2. Lower FRAME_REPORT_MS to about 120, since a player reported a visible stutter
   at 113 ms and the current threshold cannot see it.
3. Then look at PATHS_PER_FRAME again, with this stack as the reason.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Settled the contradiction I flagged above, by reading the numbers rather than
the prose. The mechanism is not broken.

Twelve waves across two runs on Decoy, from the perf lines:

  worst frame in the break before a wave   153, 82, 59, 98, 64, 71 ms
  frames stalled, per wave                 0 in every wave
  frames slow, per wave                    3 to 43

FRAME_STALL_MS is 100 and nothing inside a wave reached it, so a stalled count
of zero is the right answer here rather than a broken counter. FRAME_REPORT_MS
is 250 and nothing came near it, so no stall event is right too.

The 1796 ms in the earlier comment is not in these runs at all. That figure came
from a cold map load, which the comment itself says, so the two readings are of
two different things and neither is wrong.

## What the numbers do say

The worst frames are 98 to 153 ms and the thresholds sit just above them. One
wave peaked at 98.1 against a 100 ms mark. So the instrumentation is set exactly
where it cannot see what is happening: a player reported a visible stutter, and
every frame that could be it falls under both thresholds.

Lower FRAME_REPORT_MS to about 120 and the tail players notice starts producing
an event with a timestamp and a round state, instead of only a per-wave summary.
FRAME_STALL_MS at 100 is defensible as it stands now that it is known to be a
boundary rather than a ceiling.

Not changed yet: a rebuild swaps the .smx under a run, and a balancing A/B is
measuring. Queued behind it.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Play report, 2026-08-26: stutters on Mannhattan, both during waves and at the
start of them.

That matters because every number on this bead is from Decoy, and Mannhattan is
not Decoy. The one symbolised crash stack here is NavAreaBuildPath walking the
nav mesh, and the cost of that walk scales with the mesh. Mannhattan is a much
bigger map with more of one.

So the Decoy reading, worst frames 98 to 153 ms and nothing over either
threshold, may simply not describe the map the stutter was seen on. I would not
carry it across.

Two things follow:

- measure Mannhattan before touching a threshold. If its frames are already over
  250 ms then FRAME_REPORT_MS is fine where it is, and the events were there to
  be read all along on the map nobody measured
- "during waves" is new. The bead has been about the wave start, and the earlier
  numbers agreed: inside a wave the worst frame was about seven ticks. A stutter
  mid-wave on a bigger map points at the same path search rather than at the
  wave-start burst

Next run on this bead is Mannhattan, six waves, reading the perf lines.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Raised to P0 on the play report: people cannot play, the server crashes, and a
crash costs them the mission.

The crash half now has a symbolised stack, NavAreaBuildPath under the watchdog,
and a map to reproduce it on. The cost half is not this bead's to fix and is
worse than the crash: a restart should never make anybody replay a mission.
Filed separately on the launcher side.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Reproduced on Mannhattan, and it is nothing like Decoy. Six waves each, same
build, same bots, nobody playing.

                              Decoy            Mannhattan
  worst frame in a wave       59-153 ms        91,107,109,119,152, 1833 ms
  worst before a wave         59-153 ms        96,107,109,152,621, 1833 ms
  frames slow per wave        3 to 43          58 to 89
  frames stalled per wave     0 every wave     7,1,1,1,0,1
  stall events written        0                3

So the map is the variable. Decoy never produced a single frame over 100 ms and
Mannhattan produced stalls in five waves of six, with roughly double the slow
frames throughout.

The three stall events, all in wave 1:

  {"ms":1085,"in_wave":1}
  {"ms":270,"in_wave":1}
  {"ms":1833,"in_wave":1}

in_wave 1 on every one of them. The play report said "on waves playing and on
start of waves" and the numbers agree: these are during a wave, not in the break
before it. 1833 ms is the server not moving for nearly two seconds while people
are fighting.

## Two things this settles

The instrumentation is not broken and the threshold is not wrong. FRAME_REPORT_MS
at 250 caught all three of these. The reason nothing ever fired before is that
every measurement on this bead had been taken on the one map that does not
stutter.

And my own note above, about lowering the threshold to 120, would have been the
wrong change made for the right reason. Leaving it at 250 keeps these three
legible instead of burying them in a hundred 109 ms frames. Withdrawn.

## Where to look next

The one symbolised crash on this bead is NavAreaBuildPath under the watchdog,
and the cost of that walk scales with the nav mesh. Mannhattan has a much bigger
one than Decoy, which is the difference between these two columns and the
obvious first suspect. mvm-297 capped this once with PATHS_PER_FRAME; the
question is whether that cap is still doing its job on a map this size.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Found the hole, and the budget's own comment names it.

PATHS_PER_FRAME is 2 and TakePathBudget is called from exactly one place,
nextbot_behavior.sp:320, the periodic repath. There are 29 path computes in the
mod, spread across twenty behaviour files. So 28 of 29 never ask the budget for
anything.

The comment on TakePathBudget says why, and it is not an oversight:

  "Only the per-frame refresh asks: a behaviour that computes once when it
   starts has nothing to retry with, so it is never refused."

Which is true. Refusing a one-shot compute leaves that bot with no path at all,
so the budget cannot simply be extended over the other 28 without giving each
of them somewhere to retry from.

## Why this produces exactly what was reported

A one-shot compute happens when a behaviour starts. Six bots start behaviours
together at a wave start, and again during a wave every time targets die and
they all re-choose. Both are unbudgeted, and the same comment says an
unreachable goal makes NavAreaBuildPath walk the whole mesh.

Bigger mesh, more of it walked. That is Decoy at nothing over 100 ms against
Mannhattan at 1833.

## Three ways out, none of them measured

1. Bound the search. The crash stack had NavAreaBuildPath with maxPathLength 0,
   which is unlimited, so an unreachable goal costs the whole mesh every time.
   A cap is one change at the root rather than plumbing at 28 call sites. The
   risk is that a legitimate long path on a big map starts failing, and
   Mannhattan is exactly where that would bite.
2. Give the one-shot computes somewhere to retry, so the budget can cover them.
   Correct and invasive: every one of the 28 has to handle a refusal, and a
   behaviour that starts without a path has to not fall over.
3. Stagger the starts, so six bots do not all re-choose in one frame. Cheapest
   and treats the symptom rather than the unreachable-goal search underneath.

I would measure 1 first because it is one line and it addresses the thing the
stack actually shows, then 3 if the frames are still bad. Not attempting any of
them on a guess: results/mann-perf.jsonl is the before, and the rule on this
repo is that the run says so.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The path-cap A/B is void and needs rerunning. My fault, and it is the mistake
this bead's own docs warn about.

The cap-off arm finished six waves cleanly. While the cap-on arm was running I
rebuilt the mod for the engineer work on mvm-hnb, which restages the tree, and
the container's installer copies the stage over the running server every thirty

the flag plus the engineer fix, against the flag alone.

docs/testbed-metrics.md says exactly this under "Never rebuild while a run
measures". I wrote that line last night and then did it.

Stopped rather than left to finish, because a pair that differs by two things
answers neither. Both arms want rerunning once the engineer fixes are settled,
which is fine: they are quick, and the cap ships off either way.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
A crash on this bead is the engineer freeze on mvm-hnb, and fixing that one
stopped it.

run.sh printed the two together, which is what tied them:

  stuck: Wesley (engineer) at 1014 885 274 for 12s
  stuck: Wesley (engineer) at 1014 885 274 for 12s
  WatchDog! Server took too long to process

A wedged bot asks for a path, is reset, comes back to the same wedge and asks
again. The watchdog kills the server on that answer, inside NavAreaBuildPath,

Same mission before and after the wedge recovery: crashed at 0 waves, then 4 of

So one cause of the stutter and the crash on this bead is a bot that cannot

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Proof that the engineer AI is what crashes the server, from a play-test rather
than from the test-bed.

  omaewh4: "Did you have an engineer in the team? Can you try without one?"
  k-kaneta: "ok mannhunt works if there is no engie"

A map that crashes reliably with an engineer and does not crash without one is
about as clean a control as a play-test produces, and it removes one variable
rather than adding a theory.

This bead has had the mechanism for a while: a wedged bot asks for a path, is
reset by the watchdog, comes back to the same wedge and asks again, and the

Measured on Mannworks with Mean Machines, before and after v2.20.1: crashed at

So the crash half of this bead has a cause and a fix. The stutter half does not:

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Measured. Mannhattan, six waves per arm, and the answer is that the wedge fix
did it, not the path cap.

                        worst frame median   worst frame max   stalls
  before the wedge fix         114.2 ms          1833.7 ms       11
  cap off, wedge fix in        129.7 ms           141.7 ms        6
  cap on,  wedge fix in        103.5 ms           134.8 ms        3

The 1833 ms frame is gone. Thirteen times smaller, and it is gone from both
arms, so it is not the cap that removed it: the cap is in one arm and the wedge
