## The cap itself

Stalls 6 against 3, worst median 129.7 against 103.5, and slow frames slightly
worse at 68 against 74. Direction is right and the size does not clear the
spread of six waves, which is the bar in docs/testbed-metrics.md.

So it stays off, which is its default. It is one line to turn on if a map ever
shows the pathological case again, and it costs nothing sitting there.

## What is left

Worst frames of about 140 ms and three to six stalls per six waves. A player
reported a visible stutter at 113 ms, so this is not nothing, but it is a hitch
rather than the server stopping for two seconds. Filed at its own size.

title: Engineers freeze in spawn between waves
description:
EZKSupernova reported it twice: "if you restart a mission via the vote menu, the
engi bots just freeze in spawn", which Peppy confirmed, and "the engie bots just
freeze in spawn when wave is lost".

Neither the restart nor the loss was the cause. The break was.

`g_bShoppedThisBreak` was cleared in `Event_MvmWaveBegin`, which is when a break
ends rather than when one starts. So every bot that lived through a wave carried
"has shopped" into the whole of the next break, and `GetDesiredBotAction` has
three things to offer a bot between rounds: collect loose money, go and shop, or
walk to the front. The first is rare, the second was skipped by the stale flag,
and the third refuses an engineer and a medic. Nothing left, so the bot was
handed back to the game, which has no answer for a defender between waves, and
he stood where the wave left him.

A bot that died shopped normally, because a spawn clears the same flag. That is
what made it intermittent, and it is why a lost wave and a vote restart were
what got reported: a restart kills nobody, so nobody's flag is cleared and the
whole team stands still.

The flag is cleared when the break opens now, on `mvm_wave_complete` and on
`mvm_wave_failed`.

The test-bed grew two things to see it with, and both stay. `report` has a
"between waves" table: the share of break samples with no Defender action
anywhere on the action stack, the longest run of them, where he stood and how
far he walked. And `TESTBED_BOT_MANAGER_MODE=2` plays a mission in AUTO_BOTS,
which is what tf2-archipelago runs; the test-bed had only ever played
READY_BOTS, and this bug does not show there because a lost wave kills enough
bots to clear their own flags.

Measured on Decoy, two waves, AUTO_BOTS, six bots with two engineers, both waves
cleared in both arms. The number is the share of between-wave samples with no
behaviour at all:

| | engineer | engineer | medic | soldier | heavy | demo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 86% | 100% | 100% | 6% | 6% | 20% |
| after | 0% | 0% | 76% | 0% | 0% | 0% |

The engineers walked 2509 and 777 units in the break before, and 14803 and 15873
after.

The medic is still standing, and that is item 19.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 17 — section: Bugs from the 1.9.0 play-test
Original heading: Engineers freeze in spawn between waves. Fixed and measured
close_reason: Fixed in v2.11.0. g_bShoppedThisBreak was cleared on mvm_wave_begin, which ends a break rather than starts one, so every bot that survived a wave carried 'has shopped' through the next break and GetDesiredBotAction had nothing left to offer an engineer or a medic between rounds. A bot that died shopped normally because a spawn clears the same flag, which is why it looked intermittent and why a vote restart froze the whole team. Cleared when the break opens now, on both mvm_wave_complete and mvm_wave_failed. Measured on Decoy, AUTO_BOTS, two waves cleared either way: share of between-wave samples with no behaviour, engineers 86% and 100% before, 0% and 0% after; medic 100% to 76%, and the medic's own share closed separately. The between-waves table in the run report is the instrument.

title: Retire tf2-mvm-bots: what has to move, and in what order
description:
The standing goal is a Go repository that owns everything and an old repository
that can be archived. Studied 2026-08-31; this is what actually ties us to it.

Five anchors, in the order they can be cut.

1. The SourcePawn sources. 10,804 hand-written lines (mvm-z83.66 has the file
   by file study). Every port moves lines from the old repo to generated files
   still living in the old repo's source tree; the tree itself moves only when
   the plugin builds from tf2-mvm-bots-go.

2. The shipped-file proofs. Every Body with a Shipped: path compares against
   the old repo at the pin. As hand-written files reach zero the comparison
   target disappears with them: the proof for a finished file becomes the
   generator's own golden file, committed here. This flips file by file, not at
   the end.

3. The build. deploy/bots/build.sh, the compose file, spcomp inputs all live
   there and internal/upstream reaches them. The end state per CLAUDE.md is the
   plugin built from this repo: gen/ stops being copied across and becomes the
   source of truth, and the old repo's source/ is deleted rather than moved.

4. The non-code assets: gamedata/, the map configs, the popfiles. Small, no
   history worth keeping beyond git's. They move here as a directory (data/ or
   deploy/), and internal/upstream's path resolution turns inward.

5. The tracker. The beads Dolt DB lives in ../tf2-mvm-bots/.beads and every
   CLAUDE.md says to run bd -C there. Last to move, first to forget: migrate
   the DB, update both CLAUDE.md files, or the next session files beads into an
   archive.

Order: 2 can start now for the ~50 finished files. 4 is an afternoon and
removes the scariest dependency. 3 follows 4. 1 is the long middle. 5 is last.

## Done when

tf2-mvm-bots is archived read-only and nothing in tf2-mvm-bots-go resolves a
path outside itself.
notes:
Anchor 2 is done, and it was the one that mattered most.

The comparison that proves a port faithful read the plugin's git history, which tied every proof to the repository this one replaces. A proof that dies with its evidence is not a proof. internal/upstream/shipped now holds all 38 shipped files, each at the revision its Body reads it at, 700 KiB of text versioned beside what it proves. ReadAt reads the snapshot first; TestSnapshotMatchesTheRepository checks the copy against the repository wherever it is still present, and cmd/snapshot writes it.

Measured: 49 bodies compare with MVMBOTS_UPSTREAM pointing at nothing. The proofs no longer skip without the plugin repository, and they no longer need it at all.

What is still tied to it, in order:

  The plugin source itself, which the port is emptying (7,568 lines).
  build.sh, the compose file and the toolchain fetch, reached through
  internal/upstream. Those move with the source.
  gamedata, the map configs and the popfiles. 160 KiB, no history worth
  keeping beyond git's, and nothing else depends on where they sit.
  The beads database, last to move and first to forget.
Anchors 2, 3 and 4 are done, and tf2-archipelago builds from the Go repository.

  2. The proofs read the snapshot under internal/upstream/shipped, not the old repository's history.
  3. plugin/ in tf2-mvm-bots-go holds the whole tree the old repository tracked: source, configs, gamedata, specs, docs, the test-bed scripts. internal/plugin resolves it; internal/upstream keeps one reader, cmd/snapshot.
  4. Went with 3: gamedata and the map configs are under plugin/ and nothing resolves a path outside the repository for them.

tf2-archipelago 4d4fa34 fetches m-this/tf2-mvm-bots-go at v0.9.1 and reads plugin/ for the source, the gamedata and the configs. One pin for the plugin and its generator, where there were two that could disagree. Built end to end: the generated SourcePawn matches the pinned generator and tf2_defenderbots.smx stages.

The gate compiles the plugin whole now (internal/plugin.TestThePluginCompiles), which the old repository's build was the only thing doing.

Left tying us to tf2-mvm-bots:
  1. The port itself, 7,568 hand-written lines, now inside plugin/ and no longer a reason to keep the old repository.
  5. The beads database, which every CLAUDE.md still says to run bd against. Migrate it, update both CLAUDE.md files, then archive the repository read-only.

title: The plain files are the other half of the port, and util.sp is the one that is finished
description:
mvm-z83.58 tracks the behaviours. This is everything else under source/, which is
where most of the hand-written SourcePawn now is: 11,794 lines across thirteen
files.

Finished. util.sp is 281 lines of includes, defines and enums and holds no
function at all, down from 2,824. What came out of it is in internal/body across
roster, scan, medic, econitem, sapper, spawnroute, reflect, movement, actionstack,
angles, stocks, bombinfo, nestmove, buildarea, nesthint, nestpick, lineoffire,
nestscore, entity, loadout, state, mission, weapons, finders, bluassist, faults,
stickies, uber and chat.

In flight. cosmetics.sp: eleven functions ported into internal/body/cosmetics and
the file is down to 154 lines. What stays behind is GiveBotCosmeticsSoon, the
timer and the dump command, because a timer callback and a console command are
function references and the subset has none. The declaration and call sequence
comparison passes; the last full `make check` after the generated file was copied
across has not been run, so that is the first thing to do on picking this up.

Left, by size:

  nextbot_behavior.sp 3431, tf2_defenderbots.sp 3385, menu.sp 1005,
  botaim.sp 900, player_pref.sp 580, loadouts.sp 502, events.sp 495,
  dhooks.sp 363, sdkcalls.sp 295, tf_upgrades.sp 197, offsets.sp 148,
  archipelago.sp 57

sdkcalls.sp, offsets.sp and tf_upgrades.sp are extern seam rather than port: they
are the addresses and the SDKCalls internal/engine already declares on the Go
side, and moving them means owning the gamedata lookup, not translating a
decision.

menu.sp, events.sp and dhooks.sp are callback registration, which is the same gap
cosmetics hit: the generator has no function values. Either //sp:forward grows to
emit the callback shell and hand off to a generated body, or those files keep
their shells for good and only their bodies come across. That decision is worth
making before starting on them rather than three times over.

## Done when

Every file above is either generated, or a shell whose bodies are.
notes:
cosmetics.sp is done: make check is green with generated/cosmetics.sp in the plugin, and both repos are committed (6a0b27e, 9e8d983). Hand-written total 11,794.

loadouts.sp is next and it is a tables job, not a body job. Thirty of its 502 lines are pools of weapon item definition indexes, one array per class and slot, and GetRandomWeaponForClass is 95 lines of StrEqual chain over them. That belongs in internal/tables the way the ranking table does: one Go declaration per pool, emitting both the arrays and the lookup. Porting the chain as a chain would port it twice.

The six portable functions are ClearSavedAttributes, PrepareCustomLoadout, ResetLoadouts, ReapplyItemUpgrades, GetRandomWeaponForClass and GiveGoldPanStats. LoadLoadoutFunctions, Command_BoughtUpgrades and Timer_GiveCustomLoadout stay behind for the same reason cosmetics' two did.
loadouts.sp and player_pref.sp are across. Hand-written total 11,155, down from 11,794 this session.

loadouts.sp is 193 lines: LoadLoadoutFunctions, Command_BoughtUpgrades and Timer_GiveCustomLoadout. The pools were transcribed out of the shipped arrays by script, index for index, so no number was retyped.

player_pref.sp is 247 lines: Config_LoadServerLoadout, Timer_SavePrefData, LoadPreferencesData, ShowCurrentBotClassChances and a commented-out SetRandomWeaponPreference that was already dead. m_kvPlayerPrefData and m_kvServerLoadout lost their static so the generated file can read them, and internal/engine now has the KeyValues methods.

Next by size: nextbot_behavior.sp 3431, tf2_defenderbots.sp 3385, menu.sp 1005, botaim.sp 900, events.sp 495, dhooks.sp 363, archipelago.sp 57. The callback-shell decision is now the thing in the way of menu.sp, events.sp and dhooks.sp, and it is what mvm-z83.66 says to make before starting any of them.
The callback shell decision, with what the generator already has.

//sp:public exists and emits a body as public rather than stock, which is what
SourceMod needs before it will take the address of a command callback or an event
handler. //sp:dhook already emits a full wrapper: it writes public MRESReturn
DHook_Name, unpacks each DHookParam into a local, calls the generated body and
maps the result onto MRES_Supercede or MRES_Ignored. So one callback kind is
already generated end to end, and the shape to copy is in internal/spbody/dhook.go.

What is missing is not the shell but the reference: RegConsoleCmd, HookEvent and
CreateTimer are all passed a function by name, and gosubset refuses a function
type. The bounded way in is to let the extern package declare a named function
type per callback kind, for example type TimerCallback func(timer Timer, data
int32) Action, allow that type only as an engine parameter, and require the
argument to be a plain identifier naming a package level function so the emitter
writes its SourcePawn name and nothing else. Go still type checks the callback's
signature against the registration, which is the part a string name would lose.

Doing that unblocks menu.sp 1005, events.sp 495, dhooks.sp 363 and the shells
left behind in cosmetics.sp, loadouts.sp and player_pref.sp. Do it before
starting any of those four, not during.
Correction: the callback seam was never missing. engine.CreateTimer already took its callback by name, and internal/body/faults and internal/action/engineeridle both pass one. Only RegConsoleCmd and HookEvent were absent, which is one extern each, plus CreateTimerWith for a timer that carries a cell.

So there is nothing to decide before menu.sp, events.sp and dhooks.sp: a callback is an ordinary body with //sp:public, and the registration takes it as a named function. Proved by porting Command_BoughtUpgrades and Timer_GiveBotCosmetics, which come out as the shipped public Action declarations and pass the comparison.

cosmetics.sp is 98 lines, loadouts.sp 120, hand-written total 11,025.
events.sp 495 -> 435: the behaviour reset trio and ShouldResetBehavior are in internal/body/behaviourreset. Hand-written total 10,966.

Also in this pass: spbody emits a for with only a condition as a while, which is what SourcePawn and the plugin both write, and every generated file was regenerated and re-adopted for it.

What is left in events.sp is nine event handlers, a voice menu listener and three timers. They are ordinary bodies now that HookEvent takes its callback by name; the work is the externs for the plugin globals they touch (g_bIsBeingRevived, g_iBuyUpgradesNumber and the rest), not the shape.

Note for whoever picks this up: source/redbots3/generated/ now holds only files tf2_defenderbots.sp includes. Four proved files still ship nowhere and are mvm-z83.57, and copying the whole gen directory across puts them back where they do not belong.
events.sp 495 -> 358. Generated so far: the behaviour reset trio, OpenTheBreak, Event_RevivePlayerNotify, Event_MvmMissionUpdate, Event_TeamplayRoundStart and Event_MvmWaveBegin. Hand-written total 10,890.

What is left in it: Event_PlayerSpawn, Event_MvmWaveFailed, Event_MvmWaveComplete, Event_PlayerTeam, Event_PlayerDeath, Listener_VoiceMenu and three timers. Two of them need conditional compilation, which is its own bead now.
events.sp 495 -> 272. Added: the two small timers, Event_MvmWaveFailed.

The wave failure needed a way to write a whole global, so spbody has //sp:globalset now: slotset had only the per-client half. Same shape, no subscript.

Left in events.sp: Event_PlayerSpawn, Timer_PlayerSpawn, Event_MvmWaveComplete, Event_PlayerTeam, Event_PlayerDeath, Listener_VoiceMenu and InitGameEventHooks. Two of those are mvm-z83.67. Hand-written total 10,804.
Study of everything left, file by file, 2026-08-31. Hand-written total 10,804.

tf2_defenderbots.sp 3390. ~90 functions in four kinds: SourceMod lifecycle

botaim.sp 900. One methodmap, BotAim, sugar over per-client arrays, private to

dhooks.sp 363. Half registration against gamedata (seam; belongs with

events.sp 272. Six handlers left; two are mvm-z83.67, the rest are the same

archipelago.sp 57. Two functions, an afternoon.

upgrade.sp 784 is mvm-z83.64. util.sp 281, sdkcalls.sp 295, offsets.sp 148,
tf_upgrades.sp 197 are includes, defines and the gamedata seam: they reach zero
only when the seam moves to the Go side, which is the retirement bead's
question, not a port's.

Two holes in the proof closed, both found by widening it rather than by reading code.

1. The shipped comparison only walked 'stock' declarations, so every //sp:public body ever emitted (the timer callbacks, the event handlers, the command callbacks, the DHook shims) had gone unproved since the day //sp:public was added. It now walks public too. Two real mismatches surfaced the moment it did.

2. One global upstream pin cannot serve a port spanning months of plugin history. A file ported a year ago must be compared against the plugin as it was then; a file being ported today must be compared against what the plugin says today. Event_MvmWaveBegin showed it: the port carried ThreatPortAudit_Report, which landed in the plugin after the pin, so a faithful port read as a port that gained a call. Body now takes an optional Rev, and everything in this campaign reads at 08e9782, the last revision holding all these files whole. The global pin stays where it is for what was proved under it.
