title: A body cannot read a ConVar, so nine behaviours cannot be ported
description:
Nine of the twenty remaining behaviours read a convar: redbots_manager_debug_actions.BoolValue and its like. That is a property on a methodmap, which the emitter can now write, but the convar itself is a global the plugin creates at load and the subset has no way to name one.

internal/tables already generates the feature convars, so the names exist on the Go side. What does not exist is a body saying "this convar" and getting the handle the plugin made.

Blocked: guardpoint, spylurk, gethealth, movetofront, getammo, engineerbuilddispenser, engineerbuildteleporter, attacktank, upgrade, engineeridle.

## Done when

A body reads a convar the plugin declares, the emitted SourcePawn is the property read the plugin writes, and the feature switches go through the same path rather than through the Feature() extern.

title: A body cannot hold a handle, so ten behaviours cannot be ported
description:
Ten of the twenty remaining behaviours reach a handle: TheNavMesh.CollectAreasInRadius returns an AreasCollector that has to be counted, indexed and then deleted, and CTFNavArea comes back out of it.

The subset has no handles and no delete. It cannot simply gain them either: a handle is a lifetime, and the reason the subset has no allocation is that a generated body that leaks one leaks it every frame.

Blocked: guardpoint, evadebuster, markgiant, gotoupgrade, gethealth, movetofront, getammo, engineerbuilddispenser, engineerbuildteleporter, upgrade, engineeridle.

## What has to be decided

Whether a handle is a value the subset knows about with a scope rule the emitter enforces, or whether every collection walk stays behind an extern that takes a callback, which the subset also has no form for.

## Done when

A body walks a collection and the emitted SourcePawn deletes it on every path out, including an early return, and a test proves the delete is there.

title: Every behaviour is generated; what is left is the dispatcher around them
description:
Stale counts corrected 2026-08-31: every behaviour is across. internal/action
holds 25 packages, nextbot_behavior.sp includes 30 generated files, and
source/redbots3/behavior/ holds exactly one hand-written file: upgrade.sp, 784
lines, the shopping trip, tracked as mvm-z83.64.

What this bead still covers is the behaviour infrastructure that lives in
nextbot_behavior.sp itself rather than in a behaviour file: the main action
callbacks (SelectMoreDangerousThreat, SelectTargetPoint, ShouldAttack, the
OnActionCreated dispatcher), GetDesiredBotAction, and the threat priority pair
with its audit. Those are the brain's dispatcher, not a behaviour, and they port
as bodies the way events.sp did.

## Done when

source/redbots3/behavior is empty and nextbot_behavior.sp includes generated
files.
notes: The generator can emit a console command and a timer callback as well as a DHook: //sp:public plus a registration extern that takes the callback by name. Nothing about a behaviour needs it, but the behaviours that schedule their own timers now have the shape to copy.

title: A generated body cannot call the plugin's own SourcePawn
description:
internal/spbody emits a body that calls natives, SDKCalls and DHooks through internal/engine, and a body that calls another body by name. What it cannot do is call a hand-written plugin function that is not an engine call, which during the port is most of the plugin.

The extern directives cover the three engine kinds. A fourth, for a plain plugin function, is the same mechanism with no leading argument, and it needs a rule for what happens when that function is itself ported: the extern goes and the call becomes an ordinary one, and nothing should be able to leave both in place.

## Done when

A body calls a hand-written plugin function through a declared extern, and a test refuses an extern that names a function the port already owns.

title: The end state is a full Go rewrite, not a generator beside a plugin
description:
Recorded because the epic's shape changes with it and the beads under it should be read in that light.

The epic was written as: author the decisions in Go, generate the SourcePawn, leave the 250 sites that have to be SourcePawn where they are. The direction now is a full Go rewrite of this repository, with the test-bed moving into tf2-mvm-bots-go as well.

What that changes about the open work.

The adoption beads stop being about swapping one generated file into a hand written plugin and start being about which half of the boundary a thing ends up on. mvm-z83.16 and mvm-z83.34 are the ones this rewrites.

The vendored copy under source/redbots3/generated/ is a stopgap for measuring a port against the plugin that exists, not a pattern to grow. Nothing checks it against the generator today, which is fine for a stopgap and not fine for a shape.

The scaffolding beads keep their value: mvm-z83.46 and the edge fidelity work are about the boundary between a decision and the engine, and that boundary survives the rewrite whichever language holds it.

The test-bed moving to Go is somebody else's work in flight. Nothing here should assume testbed/ stays where it is.

title: The noise floor for a threat priority A/B was never measured
description:
mvm-z83.8 states the rule and the mvm-z83.6 run did not follow it.

Armed clear counts on mvm_decoy across three runs were 2 of 4, 0 of 4 and 3 of 3, with the same code and the same arm. Unarmed gave 3 of 4 twice, with defenders died at 6.0 and 7.0 a wave. The runner flagged defenders died as outside its band in both A/B runs and the third run refutes reading that as a result.

Nothing here says how much of that is the arm and how much is the bots not being deterministic, because no off against off pass was played. Until one is, no threat priority A/B on four waves an arm means anything.

Play the same arm against itself, same map, same wave count, and report the spread. That number is the floor every later comparison is read against, and it belongs in docs/testbed-metrics.md rather than in one bead.

title: The threat port edge is not yet proved faithful in a running game
description:
Left open by the mvm-z83.6 run and it is the claim that matters.

The differential test proves internal/threat and the generated table agree on all 960 combinations under SourcePawn's own VM. It cannot prove the edge fills the record the way the shipped chain reads it, because it drives both sides from one record. Only a running game answers that, and mvm-z83.46 is what happens when nobody asks.

The plugin on branch go-threat-priority already runs both functions on the armed side and logs where they part company, and reports compared and disagreed at every wave. One three wave run wrote no disagreement lines, before the compared count existed, so it could not tell no disagreements from never ran. The run that would have read the count was stopped part way.

To close: play three waves armed, read the per wave line, and require compared to be a large number and disagreed to be zero. Then delete the scaffolding, which is marked in the source as meant to go with the measurement.

title: The test-bed is Go and lives in the wrong repository
description:
23 Go files under tf2-mvm-bots/testbed: cmd/testbed, cmd/rc, report, sweepreport,
internal/lab, internal/rcon, internal/wave. All of it is already Go and none of it is
here, which is the ownership split this epic exists to end.

It moves whole, with what it depends on. That is the part to think about before
starting: the runner reads testbed/compose.yml, entrypoint.sh, build.sh and the built
plugin package, so moving the Go half alone splits one thing across two repositories
and makes the position worse rather than better.

## What comes with it

- the 7 shell scripts, which are container and toolchain plumbing rather than logic
- checkspots.py, which validates a map config and has a Go home in internal/navmesh,
  whose mapconfig.go already reads the same files
- rcon.py, which is deleted rather than moved: internal/rcon does the same job and
  two implementations of one protocol is one too many

## What it unblocks

internal/runmap already reads the results file this writes, across a repository
boundary, which is the first thing that got awkward. The noise floor work in
mvm-z83.8 and the machine record in mvm-z83.24 are both changes to this runner.

## Done when

A run is started from this repository, the plugin repository holds no Go, and rcon.py
is gone.

title: Draw a run as a map, so a trace can be looked at instead of read
description:
The test-bed already records where every bot stood twice a second, and the only way to
read it is as numbers. Yesterday's engineer work is the argument: "the engineer walks
the map" took four runs and a hand-built statistic to see, and a floor plan with his
path drawn on it would have shown it in one look.

## What it is

A Go command in this repository that reads a run's JSONL and writes a PNG per wave.

- the nav mesh is the background. internal/navmesh already parses it and
  testdata carries the seven MvM maps, and an Area is an axis-aligned rectangle
  in XY, so the floor plan is a rectangle fill per area
- one polyline per bot, coloured by class, from the "bot" samples
- buildings as markers at their sampled position, from the "building" samples
- image/png and image/draw, no dependency

## Why here and not in the plugin repository

The nav parser is here. The alternative was a package in tf2-mvm-bots/testbed beside
report, and it would have had to reimplement the mesh reading or reach across for it.

## What it is not

Not a replacement for the numbers. A picture says where a bot was and says nothing
about whether that is unusual, which is what mvm-z83.28's assertions are for. The two
answer different halves: the assertion fails, the picture says why.

## Done when

A run of the test-bed produces a PNG per wave in which the seven maps are recognisable
as themselves, the bots' paths are distinguishable, and mvm-wb0's wedge on Mannworks
is visible as a knot of samples in one place.

title: A wave counted for an arm can have begun under the previous one
description:
Seen while running the Go threat priority A/B. With -build=false the runner does not restart the server, and LoadMission does not always interrupt a wave already in flight: results/gothreat-race-on-1.jsonl holds a wave_end for wave 2 with no wave_begin for it, because wave 2 started under the previous run's settings and finished under this one's.

The wave is counted for this arm. Nothing in the file says it began under another, beyond the missing wave_begin, and nothing reads that absence.

Two things to decide. A wave with no wave_begin in the file should not be counted at all, which is a change in the report and cheap. And LoadMission should leave the server between waves rather than inside one, which is the real fix.

Related but not the same as mvm-666, which is about the order arms play in. This is about a wave belonging to two of them.

title: Filling a threat record eagerly can call IsClientInGame on a tank
description:
Found porting ThreatPriority in mvm-z83.6, and it is the mvm-z83.40 problem in a new shape: not a side effect, a precondition.

The shipped test is !BaseEntity_IsPlayer(threat) || !IsClientInGame(threat). It short circuits, so IsClientInGame is never reached for something that is not a player. internal/threat takes a filled record, and an edge that fills IsPlayer and InGame independently calls IsClientInGame on every entity it considers. SourceMod throws 'Client index %d is invalid' for an index outside 1..MaxClients, and a tank is exactly that.

The rule is written on the record and in the generated file's comment: fill InGame as IsPlayer && IsClientInGame(threat). Nothing enforces it. The decision cannot: by the time it runs the call has been made.

Enforce it where the record is filled. Either the edge is generated too, so the guard is not a thing anyone has to remember, or mvm-z83.30 lands and the binding for IsClientInGame carries the precondition and the call site is linted against it.

Not hypothetical the moment mvm-ds3 is fixed: the whole point of the record is that a tank can be handed to the decision, and a tank is the index that throws.

title: The comparison lineup must contain the classes the selection branches on
description:
The test-bed default lineup is scout, soldier, demoman, heavyweapons, engineer, medic. Selection branches per class and has its own cases for the sniper and the spy, neither of which is in that lineup, and the pyro is absent too.

So a run with the default lineup exercises 4 of the 10 class branches and would report agreement between the arms while never reaching the sniper or spy code at all. That is mvm-pvt's lesson exactly: no sniper was ever in a test-bed lineup across 3417 samples, which is why the bug survived.

Six seats and ten classes, so the comparison needs at least two lineups. One with scout, sniper, spy, engineer, soldier, medic to reach every branch that has its own case, and the default one so the result is comparable with the runs already recorded.

Both arms play the same lineups, so this does not bias the comparison. It decides what the comparison covers, which is a different and easier thing to get wrong quietly.

title: [bug] The test-bed lock is per checkout, but the server it protects is global
description:
The lock is testbed/.lock under the repository root, taken with flock. The resource it protects is the docker compose project mvmbots-testbed, which is named in compose.yml and is therefore one container for the whole machine.

So a second checkout defeats it. A git worktree, a second clone or an agent working in .claude/worktrees takes a different lock file and then force-recreates the same container out from under the first runner. That is exactly the two-runners-at-once failure mvm-81n closed, reintroduced by a route nobody had at the time.

Found while setting up a worktree to compare the generated selection against the shipped one without touching a dirty working tree. Four worktrees already exist under .claude/worktrees in this repository.

The fix is to lock the thing that is actually shared. A file under /tmp or /run named after the compose project, or the container itself, rather than a path inside one checkout.

Not hit yet: no lock file exists and no runner is live right now.

title: [bug] The selection predicates have side effects, so they cannot be evaluated eagerly
description:
Found while writing the hand-written edge for the generated selection, and it constrains the whole approach rather than one bead.

GetDesiredBotAction evaluates its predicates lazily inside an if and else-if chain, so on any tick most are never called. Three of them are not pure:

  CTFBotAttackTank_SelectTarget, attacktank.sp:164, writes m_iTankTarget[actor]
  CTFBotCollectNearMoney_SelectTarget, collectnearmoney.sp:48, writes m_iCurrencyPack[client]
  CTFBotDefenderAttack_SelectTarget, attack.sp:219, calls SelectRandomReachableEnemy and consumes randomness

An edge that fills a flat struct of fourteen bools before asking the Go function for an answer therefore sets entity state and burns randomness the shipped code never touches. The A/B would measure the edge, not the decision, and it would look like the Go arm changed behaviour.

This is mvm-z83.18 biting at the boundary instead of in the body, and it is the reason a pure function of pre-computed inputs is right for the differential test and wrong for the plugin.

The proposed shape is a table the edge walks: each node a predicate id, the action if true, the next node if false, so a predicate is asked for only when the walk reaches it, in the shipped order. The table is generated data, the walk is a few lines of hand written SourcePawn, and nothing generated calls anything.

The obligation: the walk and the pure function must agree on every compared combination, and the walk must ask for no predicate the shipped chain would not have asked for on the same input. Without the second there is no behaviour equivalence claim.
notes:
Done, and the proposed shape is what was built. internal/spgen emits a table of nodes, each a predicate id with the action if true and the next node if false, plus a hand-written walk in the edge. Nothing generated calls anything, so a predicate is asked for only when the walk reaches it, in the shipped order.

Both obligations are asserted over the whole domain, not sampled:

TestLazyWalkAgreesWithSelect walks every reachable combination through the table and through Select and requires the same answer.

TestTheWalkAsksNothingExtra requires the predicates the walk asks for to be a subsequence of the ones the decision itself reads on the same input. The order it is held to comes from actionsel.AskOrder, which runs Select and records what it asks, so it is the real evaluation order rather than one read off the source.

The three impure predicates are therefore reached only where the shipped chain reaches them, which is the behaviour-equivalence claim mvm-z83.41 needs at the boundary.
close_reason: Closed

title: Wire the bindings package into cmd/gen and make check
description:
internal/bindgen produces a package that builds, and nothing calls it. make gen does not write it and make check does not build it, so the proof lives only in a test.

Add it to the files map in cmd/gen and let the reproducibility check cover it. The emitted package is 205 files, so decide whether it belongs in gen/ beside the rest or in a path of its own.
notes: Done. cmd/gen writes the bindings into gen/go/sm, 205 files, and prints the refusal count. make vet runs go build ./gen/... so the emitted package is proved by compiling, and the reproducibility diff in make check covers it like the rest of the output. It went in gen/go/sm beside the other Go output rather than in a path of its own: it is generated code and gen/ is where generated code lives.
close_reason: Closed

title: The round trip tests read a working tree somebody else is editing
description:
internal/tables validates against ../tf2-mvm-bots as it is on disk. Another session edits that repository live, and an agent run caught features.sp mid-edit at 21 features against the table's 22 and reported five failures that were not real. A forced re-run passed.

A test that fails because somebody saved a file is a test people learn to ignore, and this one is the whole argument that the tables are safe to adopt.

Read from a pinned git object rather than the working tree: git show <rev>:source/redbots3/features.sp, with the rev recorded and updated deliberately. Then a drift between the pin and HEAD is a visible fact rather than a flaky test.
notes: Done. internal/tables/upstream_test.go reads git show <rev>:<path> against ../tf2-mvm-bots with upstreamRev pinned at a0f9490, so a working tree somebody else is saving cannot fail the run. When HEAD has moved past the pin the test logs it rather than failing, which makes the drift a visible fact and the pin bump a deliberate act.
close_reason: Closed

title: Delete the three stall watchdogs once selection is exhaustive
description:
670 lines in nextbot_behavior.sp, and the first time this epic makes the plugin smaller rather than larger.

FEATURE_WATCH_IDLE_BOTS about 285 lines. FEATURE_WATCH_LURKING_SNIPERS with the sniper stall rescue, about 83 net. And a third the epic never named, bigger than either: the spawn exit watchdog at about 302 lines across nextbot_behavior.sp 150-232, 233-259, 390-537 and 538-581.

All three patch the same thing, a bot with nothing on its stack, one case at a time. Exhaustive selection in mvm-z83.22 removes the cause, and mvm-vnn is the proof that the cause is a hole in a decision table.

Order matters: after selection is adopted and measured, never before. Deleting a watchdog while the hole it covers still exists ships the freeze.

One blocker: RecoverDefenderFromDisconnectedSpawn has 4 callers including GetDesiredBotAction and needs a replacement, not just removal.

title: Build placement moves to Go, and the nav model checks where it lands
description:
The behaviour behind mvm-wxp, mvm-fgs and mvm-dx2, and the first place the two halves of this epic meet.

BuildStandPoint at util.sp:630 and ScoreNestArea at util.sp:2160 are pure: numbers in, a point or a score out. They move to Go under the subset, the same way action selection did in mvm-z83.22.

What makes it worth doing here rather than in SourcePawn is that internal/navmesh can then answer the question the plugin never asks: does the point this function chose actually put the building at the declared spot? Today the answer is no on three Bigrock spots and nothing anywhere notices.

The rule the moved code needs: a stand point that lands on an area other than the spot's own is not a fallback, it is a refusal. Either the engineer reaches the spot or the spot is wrong, and both are better than a nest quietly built at the foot of a rock.

Run it across all seven meshes before believing it. The community maps have no nav file here, so 20 configs stay unchecked, which is mvm-z83.27's limit and it applies to this too.

title: [bug] A spot the engineer cannot stand on relocates the building silently
description:
Maintainer: the engineer cannot reach the rock-top spots, so he puts things elsewhere.

That is the failure, and it is not a stall. Bigrock EngineerNest 1, EngineerNest 2 and TeleporterExit 1 sit 60 to 92 above the ground around them, on rocks with no nav on top. BUILD_STAND_SEARCH is 120 and the drops are under BUILD_STAND_STOREY of 100, so every side is accepted and the building goes to the base of the rock instead. Measured by internal/navmesh: 8 of 8 stand sides land on an area other than the spot's own for EngineerNest 1 and TeleporterExit 1, 5 of 8 for EngineerNest 2.

So the map author places a nest on a rock, the engineer builds at its foot, and nothing anywhere says the spot was not honoured. The nest is in the wrong place and the config still reads as if it worked.

Same family as mvm-tz9, where Decoy shipped with zero sniper spots for releases: a config that quietly does nothing reads the same as one that works.

Two fixes and they are different jobs. The cheap one is to refuse loudly at load, folded into mvm-z83.25: a declared spot whose stand sides all land elsewhere is a config error, not a spot. The real one is the placement behaviour, which is where the Go work is going.

mvm-fgs is this bug on TeleporterExit 1 specifically, reported from play. The other two have no report yet, which is the point: nothing would have told anyone.
notes:
A FOURTH, and on a different map. mvm_coaltown DispenserSpot 2 at 453 1092 494: 79 over the ground round it, 7 of 8 stand sides accepted and every one 73 to 82 below. The dispenser goes down at the foot of whatever it is on and nothing says the spot was not honoured.

It was invisible to the first sweep because it was never in the hole list: area 5091 is 79 below and its footprint reaches under the spot, so the old check called it fine. Found only after mvm-z83.32 made height relative to the surround the thing the verdict is computed from.

The four, with the measured separation:

  bigrock   EngineerNest 1    60 over, 8 of 8 sides 58 to 79 below
  bigrock   EngineerNest 2    60 over, 5 of 5 sides 58 to 60 below
  bigrock   TeleporterExit 1  62 over, 8 of 8 sides 60 to 92 below
  coaltown  DispenserSpot 2   79 over, 7 of 7 sides 73 to 82 below

Relocated is now Wrong and LeastDrop over a step height. Wrong alone was never usable: nine ground spots have all eight sides land on a neighbouring area because a 90 unit ring crosses a mesh cut on 25.

title: The hole check cannot tell a rock top from a pit
description:
internal/navmesh reports a spot with no area under it as in a hole, whatever is around it. That produced three false positives on Bigrock, caught by the maintainer and not by the tool: spots on top of rocks read the same as spots in a pit.

The discriminator is in the data already. A rock top has the surrounding ground well below it, so every stand side is accepted and drops 60 to 92. A ground level hole has the surrounding ground level with it, drops 0 to 13, and nothing to snap down to.

Report them as different things, and say which. A tool that cries wolf on deliberate authoring will be ignored on the case that matters.

The same blind spot is already stated for walls against pits in mvm-z83.27's notes. This is the second instance of it, so the fix is to make height relative to the surround a first class part of the verdict rather than a column somebody reads.
close_reason:
Height relative to the surround is now what the verdict is computed from rather than a column somebody reads. SurroundHeight returns the highest surface within reach, and Footing is decided as off the mesh, then raised, then pocket, then ground.

Raised is tested before the footprint on purpose, and that is what found the fourth relocated spot. A coordinate can stand 79 over its surround and still have an area's footprint reach under it 79 below, which Coaltown DispenserSpot 2 does. The old rule missed it entirely because it only ever asked whether there was a footprint.

The reading is not borderline and there is a test saying so: the highest ground level hole reads 4, the lowest rock top reads 60, and the 18 unit line sits in a 56 unit empty band.

The three Bigrock spots the maintainer caught now classify as spot-relocated rather than as holes, so the tool agrees with the bead text that was corrected by hand.

title: [bug] The teleporter exit ring is placed with no drop check
description:
Found offline by mvm-z83.27, and it is the real cause behind mvm-0am rather than the declared exit.

When a nest relocates, the exit is ring-placed around it: TELEPORTER_EXIT_RADIUS_SAFE is 500, eight sides, and nothing checks whether the chosen side is beside a fall. engineerbuildteleporter.sp:431.

Measured share of areas whose exit ring has a hurting fall beside it: Decoy 32 percent with 28 of them lethal, Mannhattan 10, Mannworks 10, Coaltown 6, Bigrock 1, Rottenburg 1.

A third of Decoy is not a rare case. A player taking the teleporter is put somewhere the engineer never stood and never will.

The declared exits that are themselves beside falls are Mannhattan 1 at 264, which is exactly where fall damage starts, Coaltown 1 at 262, Mannworks 1 at 249, Decoy 1 at 207 and Mannhattan 3 at 186.
notes:
NUMBERS CORRECTED after mvm-z83.32.

At the 264 unit damage bar only mvm_mannhattan EngineerNest 2, measuring 267, is a declared spot beside a hurting fall. Mannhattan TeleporterExit 1 was listed here at 264 and measures just under it; the report prints 264 because the column rounds. The Coaltown, Mannworks and Decoy entries in the original list do not clear the bar either.

The ring rule fires on Mannhattan EngineerNest 1 at 282 down and EngineerNest 2 at 272, and nowhere else. Decoy's three declared nests all have safe rings despite Decoy being the 32 percent map.

So the map wide percentage and the declared nests are two different statements, and this bead conflated them. The 32 percent of Decoy figure stands as a statement about where a relocated nest may put its ring; it is not a statement about the spots the config names.

title: [bug] Four declared spots sit in a ground-level hole in the mesh
description:
CORRECTED. The maintainer pointed out that some Bigrock spots are on top of rocks, and the numbers agree: the seven are two different things and only four are the wedge class.

The discriminator is how far the surrounding ground sits below the spot.

  map          spot              offset  sides landing elsewhere  drop
  bigrock      EngineerNest 1      98        8/8                   79
  bigrock      EngineerNest 2      96        5/8                   60
  bigrock      TeleporterExit 1    68        8/8                   92
  mannhattan   EngineerNest 1      19        1/8                    4
  mannhattan   DispenserSpot 2     23        6/8                   13
  mannhattan   DispenserSpot 3     14        3/8                    0
  mannworks    EngineerNest 4      11        4/8                   11

The Bigrock three sit 60 to 92 above the ground around them. That is a spot on top of a rock, deliberately placed, and it is the same authoring pattern as all six Bigrock sniper spots, which sit 65 to 78 above the mesh and are not reported here because they are not enclosed. The engineer does not fail to arrive: BUILD_STAND_SEARCH is 120, every side is accepted, the drops are under BUILD_STAND_STOREY of 100, and he builds at the base of the rock instead of on it. Degraded placement, not a stall. Whether that is wrong is a question about intent, and mvm-fgs is the one case where a report says it is: TeleporterExit 1 at -178 3921 318 is that bead's rock.

The other four sit 0 to 13 above the ground around them. That is a gap in the mesh at ground level with nowhere lower to snap to, which is the wedge class: a path ends at the edge of the hole, the arrival test never comes true, and the bot re-picks forever. mvm-wb0 is Mannworks EngineerNest 4.

So: four spots to fix, three to ask about. The tool reported all seven the same way, which was wrong, and the fix to the tool is filed as mvm-z83.32.

Was: seven declared spots sit over no nav area at all.
notes: The three Bigrock rock-top spots are not a false positive after all. The maintainer says the engineer cannot reach them and puts things elsewhere, which the elsewhere column already measured at 8 of 8 sides. Split out as mvm-wxp. This bead keeps the four ground-level holes.

title: [bug] A Scout with nothing to collect and nothing to shoot is left with an empty stack
description:
Found by enumerating the action selection domain in Go, mvm-z83.22, not by playing. 208 reachable combinations return nothing.

RoundRunning, Scout, upgrades done, CTFBotCollectMoney_IsPossible false, no giant, no tank, no attack target. The switch case falls out, CanGuardTheHatch is false for the Scout, and GetDesiredBotAction returns Plugin_Continue with nothing on the stack.

The comment at nextbot_behavior.sp:2388 excludes him: "The Scout is collecting money, which is his job and takes him wherever the money is." That is true of a Scout with money to collect. This branch is only reached once CTFBotCollectMoney_IsPossible has already answered no, so the justification does not cover the case that reaches it.

This is the same shape as mvm-7kr, mvm-pvt, mvm-e4g and mvm-489: a class and phase nobody enumerated, shipping as a bot standing still.

The Go side fills it with GuardPoint, the same fallback the other four fighting classes get. That is a proposal and not a measured change. It needs a run before it is believed, and a Scout has to be in the lineup for the run to mean anything, which is what mvm-pvt shows: no sniper was ever in a testbed lineup across 3417 samples.

title: Assertions that run over every recorded trace
description:
The substrate exists. A bot sample every half second carries the action stack, the position and whether he fired, and testbed/internal/wave/idle.go already proves the pattern, validated against sm_redbots_debug_empty_stack at 72 of 72.

Make the sample a generated table and grow assertions on top of it. Positions stay inside the spawn polygon is one pass over a trace and it is mvm-78m. N bots in the same 32 unit cube for T seconds is mvm-wb0. Zero length path samples is the exact metric mvm-zx0 names. mvm-6rt stops being a sweep report and becomes a failing test.

The value is that a fault becomes a test that fails rather than a document somebody reads.

title: A nav mesh model in Go, so a spot is a graph query and not a wave
description:
The largest payer among the open bugs. Parse the .nav files and configs/defenderbots/map/*.cfg offline. Areas and connections only, no movement simulation.

mvm-fgs becomes a graph query: the 120 unit BuildStandPoint snap picks the floor below a 70 unit rock. mvm-0am and mvm-778 become is this spot beside a drop, checked across every shipped map config at once rather than one map at a time. mvm-wb0 and mvm-ipf are coordinates. mvm-dop and mvm-nza make ScoreNestArea at util.sp:2160 testable on real areas.

Six open bugs from one capability, and it needs no server.

Explicitly not a movement simulation. mvm-72s already showed that faster plausible readings are worse than none.
notes:
Built in internal/navmesh. The .nav files were not on disk anywhere: they live inside tf2_misc_dir.vpk archive 016. Seven MvM meshes extracted and stored gzipped in testdata, 2.1 MB from 7.2 MB raw.

All seven are nav version 16 subversion 2 and parse to the exact last byte. The parser refuses a file it does not finish on, which is the check that catches a layout misread that stays in bounds. Zero unresolved connection ids across 7628 areas. Geometry, per-direction connections, hiding spots, encounter paths, ladders, the precomputed visibility sets and the CTFNavArea attribute word are all read, so IsCompletelyVisible is real rather than a stub.

All 27 map configs parse. Only 7 have a mesh here: the community maps' nav files are not in the dedicated server install, so 20 configs are uncheckable and every finding is about the Valve maps.

Findings filed as mvm-dx2, mvm-0dn and mvm-1yo, with causes recorded on mvm-wb0, mvm-fgs and mvm-0am. ScoreNestArea is ported term by term and runs on real areas with real visibility, returning range, height, room, sight and crowding separately, which is the split mvm-dop needs before a team term can be argued.

Deliberate limits. The drop query under-reports: a nav file cannot tell a wall from a pit, and a pit with no nav in the bottom is invisible. A version that guessed flagged every area on every map and was thrown out. GetNavArea's ground trace is not modelled, so NearestArea is the engine's answer or a superset, never narrower. CollectBombApproachAreas filters on BOMB_DROP, which is computed at mission load and not written to the file, so the approach set stays a caller's input.

Not a simulation. It says a spot or a score is wrong. It cannot say a bot wedges.
close_reason: Closed

title: The map configs are a checked table, not 22 files nobody walked
description:
mvm-tz9 shipped Decoy with zero sniper spots for releases. mvm-1pq's real cause was one declared TeleporterExit for two engineers. mvm-1oj says 22 configs were never walked.

Config_LoadMap already prints the counts, so the data is there and nothing asserts on it. Make the configs a table with the invariants stated: every map has sniper spots, a map with two engineers has two exits, every declared spot is on the nav mesh.

Cheap, and it catches a class of bug that ships silently because an empty list is not an error.
notes:
Two rules to carry, both found offline and both shipping today.

A declared spot whose stand sides all land on an area other than its own is a config error, not a spot. Measured on Bigrock EngineerNest 1 and TeleporterExit 1 at 8 of 8, EngineerNest 2 at 5 of 8, and it is mvm-wxp.

A declared spot with no nav under it and nothing lower to snap to is unreachable. Four of those in mvm-dx2.

The distinction between the two is how far the surrounding ground sits below the spot, and it must be in the verdict rather than a column, which is mvm-z83.32.
close_reason:
internal/navmesh/check.go: seven rules, three severities in the project's own vocabulary. Note, degraded meaning the spot is not honoured and the bot arrives somewhere else, broken meaning the bot cannot arrive. Twelve findings over the seven maps that have a mesh.

  no-spots              broken    fires 0, mvm-tz9 regression guard
  too-few-exits         degraded  fires 0, mvm-1pq guard
  spot-off-mesh         broken    fires 1
  spot-in-hole          broken    fires 4
  spot-relocated        degraded  fires 4
  spot-beside-fall      note      fires 1
  exit-ring-beside-fall note      fires 2

The checked table pins severity, rule and spot per map, with the numbers left in the golden so float formatting cannot break the classification test. quietRules records the two rules that fire nowhere with the reason, and a rule that goes quiet without being recorded fails the test, so a check that breaks does not read as a bug that was fixed.

One rule was deliberately narrowed after reading the plugin rather than left wide. The first cut required SniperSpot, EngineerNest and TeleporterExit and flagged 21 of 27 configs. SetupSniperSpotHints switches the map's own func_tfbot_hint entities off and logs an error when there is no sniper block, so the sniper genuinely has nothing. A missing nest or exit block falls back to the nest scorer and the bot_hint_engineer_nest entities, and a hand written block is an override rather than a requirement. So the rule requires the sniper only, and 21 configs declaring no nest is a choice.

The 20 community maps have no nav file here. NeedsMesh makes that explicit and CheckConfig with no mesh still runs the two counting rules over all 27, which is not nothing: both bugs those rules exist for were counting bugs.

title: The run records its machine, and arms that differ are not compared
description:
The variance that ruined measurements was not statistical. mvm-ibb was paging, mvm-tnt was an mtime copying a live mapped .so, mvm-8ws and mvm-a8g were unequal machine load.

Record MemAvailable, load and the extension checksums per run. Refuse a comparison whose arms differ on any of them.

This is mvm-z83.8 widened past statistics. A noise floor measured across two different machines measures the machines.

title: A feature that never fired cannot be read as a measurement
description:
mvm-2uj was a P0 built entirely on an absent log line. mvm-666 measured two arms where the feature provably never fired and read the difference anyway. mvm-a8g does the fired check by hand.

Generate a fired counter per feature from the mvm-z83.2 table into the mvm-z83.3 wave record, so every feature counts its own firings with no one remembering to add it. Then refuse an A/B whose armed feature shows zero firings in the armed arm.

That refusal is the point. An arm that did not run the code it was testing is not a result, and today nothing says so.
notes:
A weaker version of the same fault, found by running the Go threat priority A/B and fixed on the go-threat-priority branch.

The published feature list only refreshed when a wave began, and the statistics plugin reads that list in its own handler for the same event. Whichever hooks first is whichever SourceMod loaded first. The test-bed sets an arm by rcon after the map load, so on the first wave of every attempt the list recorded was the pre-arm one.

Measured, not reasoned: results/gothreat-smoke-on-1.jsonl records wave 1 with the feature absent while rcon showed the convar at 1 the whole time. After the fix, results/gothreat-fixcheck-on-1.jsonl records it.

The comment at tf2_defenderbots.sp:585 says this was already fixed by publishing at OnConfigsExecuted. That stopped the list being empty. It did not stop it being stale, and a stale list is worse: an empty one says nothing, a stale one says the arm was off and files the wave under the other side of the comparison.

Republishing on the convar change hook removes the race rather than reordering it. It does not do what this bead asks: the list still says which features were on, not which of them fired. An arm that is set and never reached still reads as a measurement.

title: actions.inc needs ActionComponentFn and the parser refuses it
description:
A typeset is several signatures under one name and Go has no such type, so the bindings refuse all 35 of them. Normally that is correct.

actions.inc needs ActionComponentFn, and actions.ext is how every behaviour in this mod is written. A refused typeset there is not a rounding error, it is the action codegen missing its callback type.

Either hand write that one declaration and say so where it lives, or pick the signature the plugin actually uses and generate from that. Look at what the 30 files in source/redbots3/behavior/ pass before choosing.

Blocks the action codegen.
close_reason:
The premise in this bead was wrong and the correction is the result.

ActionComponent appears zero times in source/. Zero of ActionComponentFn's three signatures are used, so it never blocked anything. What the 27 files in behavior/ actually assign is BehaviorActionListeners properties, whose types are two other typesets in actions_processors.inc: ActionHandler, 7 of 29 signatures used, and ActionContextualHandler, 5 of 7. Twelve distinct signatures live across fourteen property names. All 16 OnEnd handlers return void, so the Action-returning variant is dead here.

So neither option this bead offered was right. Picking one signature is impossible with twelve live, and hand writing one declaration in a package whose whole claim is that nothing is transcribed would have been worse, and would still have left the other 34 typesets refused.

Typesets are now generated: an opaque struct carrying the function reference, which is what the SourcePawn value is and what makes the setters compile, plus one named func type per signature carrying the include's own comment. Bead mvm-z83.11 gets an exact Go signature per callback rather than a name.

Typeset refusals across the tree: 35 to 0.

title: Adopt the generated features.sp and wave writer in the plugin
description:
The tables round tripped but had never been through spcomp. Round tripping is not compiling and it is certainly not running.

## Across

source/redbots3/features.sp is gone; the plugin includes source/redbots3/generated/features.sp. testbed/stats/generated/wave_write.sp holds WriteWaveResult and mvmbots_stats.sp includes it. testbed/build.sh compiles the lot.

Two things the first diff found, neither of them a normalisation:

- the generator dropped cv.AddChangeHook(Feature_OnChanged) and Feature_OnChanged itself. Adopting that would have put back the stale published feature list: an arm set by rcon after the map load is recorded as not set for the whole first wave, which files the wave under the other side of the comparison.
- the generated WriteWaveResult stopped at WriteLine(line) and dropped the perf line, WriteEngineers("end") and the g_flWaveStart reset. Adopting that would have taken frame times out of every run and let the next round reset write a row of zeros.

Both are fixed in the generator, and TestGeneratedWaveWriterIsTheWholeShippedFunction compares the whole function against the shipped one with comments and wrapping normalised, so a third omission fails rather than ships.

The predicted normalisations held: LoadFeatures comes out in enum order, the wave format string is re-wrapped, and the enum and name array are byte identical apart from engineer_entrance_first, which is appended and not inserted.

WriteWaveResult and the four helpers it calls are no longer static: spcomp scopes static to the file and an include is a different file.

TestAdoptedFilesMatchTheGenerator holds all three committed copies against the generator, threat_priority.sp included, which is the drift nothing checked before.

## Left

Replace the hand written subset struct in testbed/report/main.go with the generated parser. It needs mvm-x2c first: the report is in the plugin repository's module and the generated parser is in this one's gitignored output, so there is nowhere for the import to point.

Then run a wave and read the results file.
notes:
Read alongside mvm-z83.49: the direction is now a full Go rewrite, so adopting a generated file into the hand written plugin is a stopgap and not the destination.

What was done for the threat priority port is the stopgap in question. source/redbots3/generated/threat_priority.sp is a committed copy of the generator's output, included by the plugin, refreshed by hand. It compiles, it ran on a server, and nothing checks it against the generator. That is acceptable for measuring one port and it is not a pattern to grow.

title: Two compilers over one generated source, and nothing checks they agree
description:
The differential test compiles with the 1.13 spcomp built beside spshell. The plugin build compiles with SourceMod 1.12 spcomp64. Same lineage and IEEE-754 either way, but the generated source is checked by one compiler and shipped by the other, which means the check does not cover what ships.

The cause is real, not theoretical: SM spcomp implicitly includes its own float.inc declaring the float operators as __FLOAT_DIV__, and spshell binds them lowercase as __float_div, so an SM-compiled plugin dies on the first division with Native is not bound.

Either accept the split and add a check that both compilers agree on the generated output, or find whether a 1.13 SourceMod drop closes the gap. Do not leave it unstated.
notes:
Split accepted and checked rather than closed by hope. TestBothCompilersAgreeOnTheGeneratedTable walks the same 585728-cell sweep twice, once through the 1.13 spcomp built beside spshell and once through the 1.12 spcomp64 in testbed/build, with spshell's VM both times so a disagreement is the compiler and nothing else. They agree on every cell.

Only the compiler is swapped, and it works here because the generated table is integer arithmetic. The float operator gap in the description is real and unfixed: SourceMod's spcomp implicitly includes its own float.inc naming them __FLOAT_DIV where spshell binds __float_div, so anything that divides still cannot cross. spshell.Toolchain.WithSourceMod carries that reasoning.

Not covered: the edge. dispatch_smoke.sp stubs Action, Plugin_Continue, MAXPLAYERS and ConVar, which SourceMod's implicit sourcemod.inc already defines, so spcomp64 rejects it with 4 errors before reaching the generated code. A smoke file that compiles under both needs the stubs behind a guard. Filed separately.
The generated threat priority table and the generated edge both go through spcomp64 as well, so the two compiler check now covers three generated files rather than one.
close_reason: Closed

title: The spshell toolchain is reproducible, not a directory in tmp
description:
The spike built spshell by hand into /tmp/spwork on one machine. Nothing else can run the differential test until that is a target.

A make target that clones alliedmodders/sourcepawn, applies the -Werror patch, builds and caches under testbed/build/ the way build.sh already caches spcomp, plus the env wiring so make check picks it up.

Pin the commit. The spike built HEAD f2d11ff and the patch is against an unpinned tree: AMBuildScript sets -Werror and compiler/errors.cpp:241 has a signed/unsigned comparison GCC rejects because the tree is clang only. An unpinned patch rots.
notes:
Done. tools/spshell.sh clones alliedmodders/sourcepawn at f2d11ff, strips -Werror in place, builds with AMBuild and caches under toolchain/, gitignored. AMBuild is not on PyPI so it is a second pinned clone, 9ed1920, installed into a venv beside it. make toolchain is idempotent: it finds the two binaries and exits. Build noise goes to toolchain/build.log because dropping -Werror leaves every GCC warning about a clang-only tree on stderr.

make check now depends on toolchain and sets MVMBOTS_REQUIRE_SPSHELL through a target-specific variable, so spshell.ForTest fails instead of skipping under the gate. Without it a developer with no clang still gets a skip that names what is missing. Verified both ways.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bindings are generated from the includes, never transcribed
description:
SourceGo transcribes the SourceMod API into Go by hand across 36 files, four years stale, and covers none of what this plugin leans on: tf2utils, tf2attributes, tf_econ_data, CBaseNPC, actions.ext. Transcribing those is the largest cost of a fork and it recurs every time an include moves.

All 67714 lines of those includes are already here under testbed/build/. A native declaration is a one line signature.

Parse the native and methodmap declarations, emit Go. Mechanical, no language design. Regenerated when sp.toml moves a dependency, and a binding that no longer matches its include fails the build.

Done when every native the plugin calls has a generated Go declaration and nothing is hand written.
close_reason:
The includes are parsed and Go is emitted. Nothing is transcribed, which was the whole point against forking SourceGo's 36 hand written files.

Over 204 .inc files: 1175 natives, 915 stocks, 112 methodmaps, 1531 methods, 310 properties, 253 enums, 35 typedefs, 1961 defines. The natives, methodmaps and properties counts are asserted equal to a grep of the declaration lines, so a parser that silently swallows a declaration fails the test rather than under-reporting.

Refusals are loud and counted. 70 parse refusals, all deliberate: 35 typeset, 33 operator overloads, 1 destructor, 1 function-like macro. 97 emit refusals: 70 variadic format functions, 22 defines whose body is not a constant expression, and a genuine duplicate in the source where actions.inc declares BehaviorAction.Set at both :895 and :900. Threading each file's resolved constants into the next drops define refusals from 69 to 22.

Cross-checked against what the plugin actually calls: of 1216 distinct capitalised call sites, 293 resolve to a free native or stock, 150 to a methodmap member, 758 are the plugin's own, and 15 are unaccounted. 14 of those are the plugin's own enum struct fields the definition regex misses. One is real and is filed separately. The external surface is covered.

The finding that would have been a silent wrong answer: SourcePawn passes arrays by reference, so a non-const float vec[3] emits as a pointer to array while const stays a value. Getting that backwards drops every out-parameter write with no error anywhere.

Verified here: go test -race green across the repository, golangci-lint 0 issues, make check passes end to end.

title: A kept change is one that beat the noise floor
description:
mvm-666 fixed arm order biasing damage and wave counts. mvm-81n stopped five kinds of run that measured nothing. What is left is that we still have no number for how much two runs of one build differ, so nothing says whether a difference is a result.

Measure the floor first: the same build against itself, enough attempts and maps to put a figure on the spread of damage, wave clears and defender deaths. Then a stopping rule that names the metric before the run and refuses to read the others as findings.

Until this exists every kept change rests on a comparison nobody can size.
notes:
FIRST MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-29. Same build armed as both arms on mvm_decoy, 2 waves per attempt, arms interleaved.

  robots killed    a=[180, 257] b=[133, 163]   arm means 218 vs 148, 48 percent apart
  damage dealt     a=[28137, 45021] b=[46503, 29579]   means 4 percent apart, but within-arm spread 60 and 57 percent
  defender deaths  a=[9, 13] b=[9, 7]   means 38 percent apart

Nothing was different between the arms. The build was identical, the cvar was set to the same value in both, and the runner interleaved them.

So on two attempts the floor is roughly 50 percent on robot kills and 60 percent on damage. An A/B at this sample size cannot see anything smaller, and every result kept on two or three attempts is a coin toss dressed as a measurement.

This retroactively covers the three sniper pairs in mvm-666. restartsniper 10611 against 15602 is 47 percent, restartab 7776 against 17132, idlewatch 6550 against 13504. All sit inside the floor measured here, so arm order may not have been the whole story: the spread alone explains them.

What it does not say: the floor on more attempts. The point of a floor is the number of attempts needed to beat it, and that needs the same run at 5 and 10 attempts to see where the spread stops shrinking. Filed as the next step rather than guessed at.

title: Golden inputs prove the generated SourcePawn matches the Go
description:
A generated function is worth nothing if the only evidence it matches its source is that we wrote the generator.

Same golden inputs through the Go function and through the generated SourcePawn under spshell, asserting the same output. Runs in the build, not on request.

Blocked on the spshell spike, and it is the bead that decides whether the generator is trustworthy or hoped for.
notes:
Done, and it runs in the build rather than on request now that mvm-z83.12 makes the toolchain a make target.

TestGeneratedSourcePawnAgreesWithGo walks all 585728 reachable combinations through the generated table under spshell and through actionsel.Select, in 213ms. Nothing is sampled. TestThreatScoreMatchesSourcePawn compares on float32 bits, not on a printed decimal.

The helper both use is spshell.ForTest: skip with a message naming the missing variable when the toolchain is absent, fail when MVMBOTS_REQUIRE_SPSHELL is set. make check sets it, so the gate cannot pass by running nothing.
close_reason: Closed

title: One Go table generates the feature enum, the names and the convars
description:
features.sp holds an enum and a parallel array of strings, and only the count is checked. ammo_failover sat at FEATURE_WATCH_IDLE_BOTS for a release, so sm_redbots_feature_watch_lurking_snipers drove the idle watchdog, an A/B armed the wrong feature, and the number was read as a measurement. The comment above the array asks the reader to be careful, which is a note about a fix nobody wrote.

One Go slice of features, each with its name, default and description. It generates the enum, the name array and the CreateConVar calls on the SourcePawn side, and the arm names the testbed offers on the Go side.

Done when the enum and the names cannot disagree because they come from the same slice, and the 22 current features round trip with byte identical convar names.
close_reason:
The feature table is one Go slice and Name is the whole identity: Enum() returns FEATURE_ plus the uppercased name, ConVar() returns sm_redbots_feature_ plus the name. The constant and the string are the same datum, so a name moved in the slice takes its constant and its convar with it. That is the ammo_failover bug made impossible rather than commented about.

Round trip proved, all 22 byte for byte. The test parses the real features.sp, pulls the enum block, the FEATURE_NAME array and the MakeFeature calls, and reconstructs the convar the way MakeFeature does, which is the format string indexed by enum position, precisely the join the bug broke. Name, constant, convar, default and description compare equal as 22 named subtests. Verified here at 38 tests passing with no skips.

The proof is itself proved: TestFeatureProofCatchesASwappedName exchanges two names in the generated array and fails if the comparison still passes.

Not done here: the generated file has never been through spcomp, and adoption is filed as mvm-z83.16. Until then this round trips but is not known to compile.

title: Can spshell run a generated decision function with no game server
description:
Everything else assumes a generated SourcePawn function can be run and compared against the Go it came from, with no game server. That comparison needs a standalone VM.

SourcePawn ships spshell. Whether our shape of generated function loads and runs there, with no sourcemod.inc and no natives, is not something to assume.

Answer with a spike, not an opinion: one hand written pure SourcePawn function taking floats and returning a float, run under spshell from a Go test, output compared to the same arithmetic in Go.

If the answer is no, say so here and name the fallback: a test plugin that runs the golden inputs at server startup and prints a verdict. Slower, still worth having, worse deal.
close_reason:
YES. A pure SourcePawn function compiles and runs under spshell with no game server, no sourcemod.inc and no natives, and its float32 result matches the Go bit for bit.

spshell is not on this machine and not in the SourceMod drop: build.sh pulls the SourceMod tarball, which has no VM shell. Built from alliedmodders/sourcepawn HEAD f2d11ff with AMBuild, about a minute. One patch needed: AMBuildScript sets -Werror and compiler/errors.cpp:241 has a signed/unsigned comparison GCC rejects, since the tree is clang-only.

The test is table driven over 8 inputs including clamp boundaries, an overheal, a value with no exact float32 and a negative distance. Plain float32 equality, no epsilon, all pass. The score crosses the boundary as raw bits, view_as<int> on one side and math.Float32frombits on the other, because printfloat gives six decimals and would hide the drift the test exists to catch. The test was proved able to fail: perturbing the Go side alone to hurt*30.5 reports 77.5 under spshell against 77.79167 in Go.

The fallback named in this bead, a test plugin printing a verdict at server startup, is not needed.

One real finding, filed as spg follow-ups: the SourceMod 1.12 spcomp64 cannot compile for spshell. It implicitly includes its own float.inc declaring the float operators as __FLOAT_DIV__, while spshell binds them lowercase as __float_div, so an SM-compiled plugin dies on the first division with Native is not bound. The differential test compiles with the 1.13 spcomp built beside spshell; the plugin build keeps the SourceMod one.

title: Rewrite the plugin in Go, and generate all of the SourcePawn
description:
tf2-mvm-bots-go is the rewrite of tf2-mvm-bots in Go. Everything ends up here.
SourcePawn becomes a build artifact and stops being a place anybody writes.

That is the aim, and it is a wider one than this epic was opened with. What was
written first was "not a rewrite of the plugin": Go would own the tables, the pure
decisions and the experiment, and everything touching the engine would stay hand
written SourcePawn behind a rule that generated code never calls back into it.
docs/design.md is corrected rather than quietly edited.

## What the measurement says it costs

docs/parity.md classifies all 47 files and 24688 lines, and the number that decides
the shape of this is not lines but calls: 436 of 756 functions contain at least one
engine call, holding 14942 lines, and 187 of them hold three or more each.

Under the old aim those functions were the floor and stayed by hand, which is where
"generate 40 percent" came from. Under this aim they are the work. The generator has
to emit engine calls, which is exactly what the small-generator rule was written to
avoid, so that rule goes and the cost it was holding down comes back.

That is the honest price of the decision and it is worth stating once: the cheap
version of this epic generated the pure 40 percent and left a working plugin. The
full rewrite has no such halfway point that is worth shipping, because a plugin half
authored in each language is the ownership problem this was meant to end.

## What is in scope

Everything in tf2-mvm-bots that is not data:

- the plugin, all 24688 lines, including the SDKCall, DHook and raw address sites
- the test-bed, which is already Go and lives in the wrong repository
- the statistics, host and refund plugins under testbed/stats
- the shell and Python around the test-bed, including rcon.py, which internal/rcon
  already replaces

Out of scope, because it is not code: gamedata offsets, the map configs, the popfiles.

## The rule that keeps it honest

Never let a fact live in both places for a day. A kind of thing moves wholly or not at
all, and the plugin repository stops owning it the same day. mvm-z83.16 is the gate on
everything for that reason.

## Order

The migration order is by kind, not by file, so ownership is one sentence that stays
true rather than a list of 47 filenames that changes weekly.

Nothing about the engine-call generator is measured. It is the piece this aim rests on
and it does not exist yet.
notes:
## Re-prioritised after reading all 75 beads, 2026-08-29

Two reviews are in docs/closed-bugs-vs-design.md and docs/open-bugs-vs-design.md.

Over the 31 closed beads that are real defects: prevented 0, caught earlier 10, does nothing 21. Not one closed bug is the features.sp name drift this epic opens with. That bug happened once, before the record starts, and mvm-z83.2 has already killed it.

Of the fourteen open P1s that are not children here, the design as drafted helps two, and only to measure.

So the transpiler is the expensive part with the least evidence behind it, and three of the ten caught cases are the noise floor and the golden harness rather than the generator. The cheap parts carry most of the value. Work them first: mvm-z83.22, .23, .24, .25, .27, .28.

The one thing the design missed outright is mvm-z83.22. The decision function that produced the most bugs is action selection, it is pure, it fits the subset, and it was not on the list.


## The hand-written floor is nine times what this epic assumed, 2026-08-29

docs/parity.md classifies all 47 files and 24688 lines. Generatable 9856, 40 percent: decisions 2959, action shape 3610, tables 3287. Hand written 13777, 55.8 percent. Delete 1055.

The under-250-sites figure in the design was a real count of the wrong thing. It counts three call kinds and counts sites, when what decides whether a function can be generated is whether it contains any engine call at all. 436 of 756 functions do, holding 14942 lines. 320 functions are already pure, 249 become pure with a hoist, and 187 functions holding 10053 lines have three or more engine calls each. Realistic floor about 10800 lines, 44 percent, against the roughly 1200 implied. design.md is corrected rather than quietly edited.

Parity is therefore generating 40 percent of the plugin, not 90. That is still worth having and it is not what was said at the start.

Migrate by kind and not by file, so the ownership rule is one sentence that stays true rather than a list of 47 filenames that changes weekly. Never let a fact live in both places for a day, which makes mvm-z83.16 the gate on everything.

title: A sniper sent to the front strafes without firing
description:
FIXED in v2.37.0, and made unreachable by v2.38.0.

Peppy on v2.36.0: a sniper rescued from a stall reached the front and then
wandered without ever firing, stall #4, #5, #6 climbing in the log.

## The cause

The round-running branch of GetDesiredBotAction answers a rifle sniper with
Plugin_Continue, because Timer_PlayerSpawn is meant to have given him his sniping
behaviour already. When it did not, he had nothing for the whole wave.

FEATURE_ATTACK_STRAFE was the wrong first suspect: a sniper is already exempt
from StrafeWhileFighting. What looked like strafing was a bot with no behaviour
at all being nudged around.

## The fix

A sniper caught stalling fights like one who never had a rifle, through
CTFBotDefenderAttack.

v2.38.0 then fixed the missing sniper mission that caused the stall in the first
place, so this path should stop being reached. It stays as the safety net for a
sniper who loses his mission some other way. See [[mvm-bj8]].

title: Arm order biases every A/B result, not only the crash count
description:
The runner played one arm from start to finish before the next, which made "the
first arm" and "the first round on a freshly recreated server" the same thing.

## Measured

Five watchdog trips in a day all landed in whichever arm ran first, never in the
second, across four features. Two of those provably never fired: idlewatch
logged zero "no behaviour" lines, so its arm ran the same code as its control
and still crashed twice against zero.

It is not only the crash column. Sniper damage per wave, same lineup and map:

  restartsniper  on 10611  off 15602
  restartab      on  7776  off 17132
  idlewatch      on  6550  off 13504

In all three the snipers sat in SniperLurk for 1.00 of samples with healthy
movement and no path failures, so they behaved the same and scored lower anyway.
The idlewatch pair cannot be caused by its feature at all.

So arm order biases damage and wave counts, not just crashes.

## Fixed

playArms interleaves the arms and roundOrder flips them every round, so no arm
keeps the first slot. Tested in order_test.go.

## Next

Every A/B run before this fix needs re-running before its result means anything,
including the three sniper fixes refused in mvm-bj8. The perch rewrite stays
refused: its sniper damage collapsed 34x, far outside anything this explains.

title: testbed -maps refuses the second map: RED reaches 0 defenders
description:
A run with -maps 'mvm_decoy mvm_mannworks mvm_rottenburg' played Decoy and then refused Mannworks with 'RED reached 0 defenders and not 6', exiting before the second and third maps ran.

The changelevel path is the suspect: LoadMission execs server.cfg, and on the map change the exec answered EOF because the connection had dropped. Without it the mod has no team composition and RED stays empty, which is exactly the failure the refusal names.

So a multi-map A/B has to be one invocation per map with a fresh container today, which is the slow path. See mvm-bj8, where it cost the Mannworks and Rottenburg arms.

title: The engineer nest relocate trips the watchdog at a wave transition
description:
A crash this repo already knows about and ships disabled.

sm_redbots_manager_engineer_nest_relocate defaults to 0, and the comment above
it says why: turning it on trips the server's watchdog at the first wave
transition, reliably, on mvm_decoy with two engineers.

That makes it the only crash here anybody can reproduce on demand. Every attempt
to reproduce the Mannhunt crash has failed, about thirty five runs across five
approaches, and this one is described as reliable.

Both are watchdog trips with engineers involved, so they may be the same fault
reached two ways. That is worth finding out before more time goes on inference.

The feature is worth having on its own terms: the bomb takes a different route
between waves and a nest that covered the approach in wave one can be facing a
wall in wave three, which is what mvm-dop is about.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Measured, and it does not crash. It does make the team worse.

Decoy, mvm_decoy_advanced, two engineers, two attempts each arm:

                                 on                off
  waves                           6                  6
  waves cleared                   0                  2
  crashes                         0                  0
  robots killed                60.5               79.0   outside 78 to 93
  defenders died               16.0               13.5   outside 8 to 15
  held for                    115.1              130.4   outside 129 to 134

Six waves with the relocate on, across two wave transitions each, and the server
stayed up both times. The comment in the source says it trips the watchdog at
the first transition, reliably, on this map with two engineers, which is exactly
what this run is. So either something fixed it since that was written, or the
comment is stale.

What the run does show is that the feature costs the team the mission: nought of
six waves cleared against two, with robots killed and defenders died both
outside the control's band. An engineer who moves his nest between waves rebuilds
instead of holding, and the wave arrives while he is carrying.

So the convar stays at nought, and now for a measured reason rather than a
remembered crash. The comment above it should say that instead of pointing at a
TODO item nobody can find.

This bead was filed on the hope that it was the same watchdog fault as the
Mannhunt crash and could be caught in the act. It is not that, and there is now
no reproducible crash in either repo.

title: The test-bed produced runs nobody should have believed
description:
The test-bed produced runs nobody should have believed, and now refuses instead.

## What was wrong

Five ways a shell run could look ordinary and measure nothing: two runners at
once, a stale plugin, the mission named on a map already up, the mission named
before the map, and a wave nobody fought. All five wrote a results file.

## What replaced it

go run ./testbed/cmd/testbed, one binary in place of run.sh, ab.sh, sweep.sh and
batch.sh. It refuses rather than produces: a lock so only one runner exists, the
loaded plugin checked against the source, the map loaded before the mission is
named and the mission verified, and RED checked for defenders from the game
rather than from player names.

It watches a running wave too, and names what went wrong in about a minute
instead of timing out: no robot on BLU once a wave has begun, a statistics file
that stops growing, RED emptying, or rcon quiet three reads running.

Reporting carries the band rule from docs/testbed-metrics.md and says when an
arm has shown nothing, when a control is too small for a band, and when a column
was never written to.

## What it cost to get there

Eleven faults in the runner itself, every one found by running it, and every one
of which the shell would have turned into a plausible file. The comments in
testbed/internal record them individually.

## Still open

- crash detection is rcon going quiet; the container log grep for 'core dumped'
  that run.sh had is not carried over
- the map is never verified, so a typo measures whatever was loaded
- results carry no record of the arm, the build or the preconditions
- run-native.sh still refers to flags that no longer exist

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Done so far, all pushed.

testbed/cmd/testbed replaces run.sh, ab.sh, sweep.sh and batch.sh. The three
wrappers each carried their own idea of what a valid run was, which is how one
mistake kept reappearing in different clothes. One place decides now.

Refusals, each one of the failures above:

- a lock file holds the test-bed, and a second runner is told who has it
- the version in source/tf2_defenderbots.sp is compared with the version the
  server reports, and a mismatch stops the run
- the map is loaded, then the mission named, then the mission verified
- RED must hold the lineup before a wave counts

Watching, rather than waiting and reading the wreckage:

- no robot on BLU for five polls: the mission is loaded and not playing
- the statistics file not growing for six polls: the plugin is gone
- RED emptying mid-wave: the rest measures a team nobody asked for
- rcon stops answering: a crash in what is being measured, counted as one

Each names its reason in about a minute instead of a twenty five minute timeout
and an empty file.

Reporting carries the band rule from docs/testbed-metrics.md: it says outright
when an arm's median falls inside the control's quartiles, when the control is
too small for a band, and when a column was never written to. That last one came
from a test catching the report giving a confident verdict about two columns of
zeros.

Tests cover the lock refusing a second runner, arm parsing, all three verdicts,
and all four watcher rules.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Still to do, in the order they matter:

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The smoke test found a fault in the runner itself, which is the point of it.

A changelevel onto the map the server was already on left RED at nought
defenders, every time, on Decoy: a map that fills fine from a fresh container.
The mod disables its bots in OnMapStart and waits to be started again, so the

The container recreate is already a map load, and it is the one the mission gets
named after, which is the order Mannhunt needs. So the changelevel now only

Three attempts at this, and the shape is worth keeping: each fix was right about

missing, then the run's shape never reached compose, then the arm was set before

comments.author: m-this

  RED holds 6 defenders

Version checked, map not needlessly reloaded, mission named after the load,
