title: The test-bed cannot reproduce the faults the fixes target
description:
Fixes were being measured against faults that never happened, so the arms came
out identical and the runs said nothing.

## The injectors

  sm_redbots_debug_wedge_seconds      v2.24.0, holds a bot in place
  sm_redbots_debug_refuse_ammo_paths  v2.25.0, refuses path answers to a pack
  sm_redbots_debug_unreachable_goal   v2.29.2, sends him at a point off the mesh
  sm_redbots_debug_old_wedge_recovery v2.29.1, restores the broken recovery
  an action stack emptier             unbuilt, for [[mvm-6rt]]

## What they were worth

The wedge one paid for itself twice. Twelve forced holds proved the recovery
does work, and a forced A/B firing nought times in both arms is what exposed the
kick counting wedges that a successful rescue resets.

The old-recovery one is the important one in hindsight. Until it existed every
A/B compared the fix against itself, which is why a day of runs came out
identical and why I kept reading noise as a result.

## Correcting the premise

The test-bed can reproduce the wedge unforced, about three times in thirteen
minutes on Mannhunt. What it could not do was run that mission, and that was the
runner naming the popfile at the wrong moment rather than anything about the
fault.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
First of the three injectors is in, defenderbots v2.24.0.

sm_redbots_debug_wedge_seconds holds one defender in place for that many seconds
after a wave starts, and sm_redbots_debug_wedge_class picks which one. Both are
zero and do nothing until a run sets them.

Held rather than frozen, on purpose: the bot is put back where it was every
frame, so he still asks for paths, still runs his actions and still fails to
arrive. That is what the watchdog sees in a real wedge. Freezing the entity
would test a different bug.

It stops itself when something moves him more than 120 units, so the recovery
working is not fought by the injector. That also makes the log line the result:
'left the hold' means something rescued him.

Run queued on Decoy, three attempts with the idle watchdog on and three off, the
hold set to 90 seconds. This is the first time any of the engineer fixes will be
measured against a fault that actually happened.

Still to build for the other two: a convar that refuses the first path to any
ammo pack, for [[mvm-zx0]], and one that empties a bot's action stack, for
[[mvm-6rt]].

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Two of the three injectors are in.

  sm_redbots_debug_wedge_seconds        v2.24.0, holds a bot in place
  sm_redbots_debug_refuse_ammo_paths    v2.25.0, refuses path answers to a pack
  action stack emptier                  not built, for [[mvm-6rt]]

The wedge one has already earned itself. Twelve forced wedges produced 36 stuck
lines and not one successful recovery, which is a finding no amount of waiting
for a natural wedge had produced in a day of runs. It also exposed a gap in the
logging: the stuck line printed the total stuck count, not the wedge count the
give-up threshold is on, so a run could not tell whether the branch was reached.
Fixed in v2.25.1, which also says which of the two refusals MoveWedgedDefender
took.

That is the argument for this bead in one paragraph: three A/Bs measured nothing
because the fault never happened, and the first injector answered a question in
one run.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Two of the three injectors are in and one has earned itself, but the bead's own
premise needs correcting.

The test-bed can reproduce the wedge: Mannhunt does it unforced, about three
times in thirteen minutes, at 1014 885 274, with no robot on the map. What it
could not do was run the mission, and that turned out to be the runner naming
the popfile at the wrong moment rather than anything about the fault.

So the injectors matter less than this bead assumed. What they did prove is that
the recovery works: twelve forced holds on Decoy, and the log shows twenty five
seconds from hold to rescue every time.

What they could not prove is anything about the nest move or the kick, because
both sat behind counters a successful rescue reset. That was a logic bug, fixed
in v2.28.0, and the injector is what exposed it: zero fires in both arms of a
forced A/B is not a null result, it is a mechanism that cannot run.

Third injector, emptying a bot's action stack for mvm-6rt, still unbuilt.

title: Mannhunt does not play in the test-bed: wave 1 lost with zero robot kills
description:
Mannhunt does not play in the test-bed: the wave starts and no robot spawns.

Every counter stays at nought for the whole timeout. RED holds its six
defenders, verified from the game, and mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 is loaded and
confirmed. The population simply does not build.

Not the map: mvm_mannworks_advanced cleared a wave with 73 robot kills and
mvm_mannworks_intermediate lost one with 50, both on the same map through the
same runner. Not the load order either, which was a real fault and is fixed:
the map is loaded first and the mission named after, and Decoy plays perfectly
that way.

I closed this once on 22 robots seen after a hand made changelevel. Six runs on
the same order have never reproduced it, so that close was premature.

It no longer blocks the crash work: the engineer wedges on Mannhunt during setup
with no robots on the map, so [[mvm-ipf]] can be measured there without a wave.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Wording, since it matters for anyone reading this later: Mannhunt is a mission,
mvm_mannworks_intermediate2, on the Mannworks map. Not a map. The same map runs
other missions.

The popfile is not missing. tf2_misc_dir.vpk carries mvm_mannworks,
mvm_mannworks_advanced, mvm_mannworks_expert1, mvm_mannworks_intermediate,
mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 and mvm_mannworks_ironman, so the test-bed's game
install has the mission it is being asked for.

The stalled wave is emptier than 'lost' suggests. Every counter is zero for the
full 1455 seconds: robot kills, giant kills, defender deaths, credits dropped,
credits picked up, damage, healing, upgrades. Nothing happened at all. The wave
began, no robot ever spawned, and the timeout was recorded as a loss.

So this is not the defenders failing to fight. It is the population never
producing anything.

Next, and it is the diagnostic this bead already named: run mvm_mannworks on a
different mission. If that plays, the fault follows the popfile. If it stalls
too, it follows the map.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The stall follows the popfile, not the map.

  mvm_mannworks_advanced       cleared, 73 robot kills, 200s
  mvm_mannworks_intermediate2  every counter zero for the full timeout, nine
                               attempts across four builds

Same map, same team, same test-bed, same build. So nothing is wrong with
mvm_mannworks or with the defenders: mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 specifically
produces a wave where no robot spawns.

mvm_mannworks_intermediate is running now, which says whether it is that one
popfile or both intermediates.

This matters beyond the test-bed. [[apw-eei]] is a report of Mannhunt crashing
in real games, and Mannhunt is the mission this cannot run. If the popfile is
mishandled somewhere in the chain that loads it, the same handling is in front
of the players who reported the crash.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
A hypothesis worth testing, from what is different rather than from the popfile.

Mannhunt plays fine on a real server. k-kaneta's log of 2026-08-27 has it
clearing waves 1, 2 and 3 at 21:13. So the popfile is not broken and the game
can run it.

What the test-bed does differently: it sets tf_mvm_popfile on a map that is
already up and then sends mp_tournament_restart. A launcher-started server gets
the mission with the map. For most missions setting it live is enough, and the
run.sh check confirms the game accepted the name. For this one the game may
accept the name and never re-parse the population, which would give exactly what
is seen: the right popfile reported, and no robot in it.

If that holds it is a test-bed fault, not a mod one, and the fix is a changelevel
to the same map after setting the popfile so the population is parsed fresh.
That costs a map load per run and buys the ability to measure any mission.

Not editing run.sh while a run is in flight. mvm_mannworks_intermediate is
playing now and says whether this is one popfile or both intermediates.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Three missions, same map, all set live the same way:

  mvm_mannworks_advanced       cleared, 73 robot kills, 200s
  mvm_mannworks_intermediate   lost, 50 robot kills, 134s
  mvm_mannworks_intermediate2  zero of everything, nine attempts

So the popfile-is-not-re-parsed hypothesis is refuted. Setting a popfile on a
live map works: two other missions on this map did it in this session. It is
mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 alone, and both the other Mannworks missions spawn
robots and get fought.

That also rules out the map, the team, the build and the procedure. What is left
is that one popfile and how the game handles it here.

Next, and it is a capture rather than a guess: run Mannhunt once with the server
console kept, and read what the game says between tf_mvm_popfile and the wave
starting. A population that fails to parse says so on the console, and nothing
has looked there yet. Every reading so far has been of run.sh output or the
stats file, neither of which carries the game's own parser errors.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Solved. The popfile has to be named before the map is loaded, and run.sh set it
after.

Proved by hand over rcon: changelevel mvm_mannworks, then tf_mvm_popfile
mvm_mannworks_intermediate2, then mp_tournament_restart. The server now holds 22
TFBot clients, which are the mission's robots. Through run.sh, with the popfile
set on a map already up, the same mission produced zero of everything for the
whole timeout, nine times across four builds.

So my earlier refutation was wrong, and wrong in a way worth writing down. I
tested the reparse idea with mvm_mannworks_advanced and mvm_mannworks_intermediate,
both of which play when the popfile is set live, and concluded the popfile was
re-parsed fine. Two missions tolerating it does not mean all do. That is what
made this look like a property of one popfile rather than of the procedure.

Fixed in run.sh: after the name is accepted, the map is loaded again, bounded at
180 seconds, then the usual settle. Checking that the game accepted the name was
never enough, because accepting a name and building its population are two
different things.

This unblocks [[apw-eei]] and [[mvm-ipf]], which could not be measured on the
mission the crash reports name.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Confirmed end to end. run.sh now loads the map, names the mission, and the
server holds 23 bots on mvm_mannworks with mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 current.
Every earlier automated attempt had the mission named and none of its robots.

The order took two goes to get right and both failures are worth keeping:

- naming the mission on a map that has been up since the container started
  reports the right popfile and builds none of its robots
- naming it and then loading the map throws the name away, because a changelevel
  resets tf_mvm_popfile to the map's own mission. That run played
  mvm_mannworks.pop and reported no waves at all, and I only caught it by asking
  the server what popfile it held afterwards.

Map first, mission second. The comment in run.sh carries both failures so the
order does not get reversed by someone tidying it.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Reopening: Mannhunt still does not spawn robots, and the earlier close was
wrong.

Six runs through the Go runner, on a build and a load order that both check out:

  mhcrash-off-1  wave 1 lost, 0 robots killed, 100s
  mhcrash-off-2  wave 1 lost, 0 robots killed,  98s
  mhcrash-off-3  wave 1 lost, 0 robots killed, 100s
  mhcrash-on-2   wave 1 lost, 0 robots killed,  87s
  mhcrash-on-3   wave 1 lost, 0 robots killed, 100s
  mhcrash-on-1   no wave at all

RED held six defenders every time, verified from the game rather than guessed
from names, so the lineup is real. The wave begins, no robot appears, and it is
recorded as lost after about a hundred seconds.

What I closed this on was 22 TFBot clients seen after a hand made changelevel
followed by naming the popfile. That is the only time robots have ever appeared
on this mission, and I closed the bead on one observation without repeating it.
The runner boots the container onto mvm_mannworks and names the mission after,
which is the same order, and gets none.

So either the hand made sequence differed from what I wrote down, or it was not
reproducible. Both mean the close was premature.

The watcher caught it correctly each time: 'no robot has been on BLU for 5 polls,
so the mission is loaded and not playing'.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Reopened and the fault is not what the close said.

run.sh naming the popfile at the wrong moment was real and is fixed, and the Go
runner does it correctly: map loaded, mission named, mission verified. Decoy
plays perfectly through it, 77 robots killed in a smoke run.

Mannhunt still does not. Six runs through the fixed runner, every wave about a
hundred seconds with nought robots killed, RED verified at six defenders from the
game each time. The population does not build.

The 22 robots I closed this on were seen once, by hand, and have not been
reproduced by any automated run on the same order. That close was premature.

It no longer blocks the crash work, which is the useful part: the engineer
wedges on Mannhunt during setup with no robots on the map at all, so the wedge
can be measured there without the wave.

title: Medics do not heal between waves, so no uber is ready at the start
description:
Reported by Peppy: 'medics seem to not wanna heal when not in an active wave so
they dont build uber'.

The consequence is the part that matters. Uber charge is built by healing, so a
medic who heals nobody during the break walks into wave one with an empty
charge. The break is the only quiet time to build one, and it is the wave start
that most wants it.

Not the same as [[mvm-e4g]], which is closed. That one was the medic having no
behaviour at all between waves, and its fix sent him walking to the front with
his patient. Its own description says the reason he was excluded before was that
'between rounds he heals nobody, so nothing suspends for him'. So the idle time
is fixed and the healing is not, which is exactly what this report describes.

Worth checking before writing anything: whether the medic refuses to heal
between rounds because something gates it, or because nobody is hurt. A team at
full health at the upgrade station gives a medic nothing to heal, and the fix
for that is to overheal rather than to heal. Overhealing also builds charge, so
either way the answer is the same shape.

The testbed already samples the medic every five seconds with a healing field
and records healing done per wave, so this is measurable without a play-test:
compare healing during the break against healing during the wave, and read the
charge at wave start.

title: The engineer's sentry action throws when the bot has already left
description:
From k-kaneta's bundle of 2026-08-27, sourcemod/errors_20260827.log, twice on
mvm_mannworks:

  Exception reported: Client index 6 is not in game (param 1)
  Blaming: tf2utils.smx
    TF2Util_GetPlayerObjectCount
    redbots3/util.sp::GetObjectOfType
    behavior/engineerbuildsentrygun.sp::CTFBotMvMEngineerBuildSentrygun_OnEnd

The trigger is in the launcher log in the same second: 'RED holds 5 of 6 between
waves. 1 bot(s) take the empty seats'. The roster changed, the bot's action
ended, and OnEnd asked the game about a client that had gone.

A thrown native takes the callback with it, so the rest of OnEnd never ran. The
comment above that log line already says this happens and had the wrong reason.
close_reason:
Fixed in v2.21.1. PlayerObjectCount in util.sp is the one boundary: it returns
zero for a client who is not in game, and TF2Util_GetPlayerObjectCount is
called nowhere else.

Four call sites went through it: GetObjectOfType, DetonateObjectOfType,
ClearBuildingsBeforeKick and CountDisposableSentries. Every one loops over the
count, so zero is the right answer rather than a refusal: a player who is not
there owns no buildings.

Compiles clean, no new warnings. Not measured on a server, because the testbed
is running the balancing arms and building under a run voids it.

title: The teleporter exit on Rottenburg drops you off a ledge
description:
Reported 2026-08-27: on Rottenburg the engineer places the teleporter exit next
to a fall, somewhere a player can die by falling.

A teleporter exit is a spot the whole team arrives at without looking, at speed,
usually mid-wave. An exit beside a drop turns the team's own building into a
hazard, and the player who used it did nothing wrong.

Same family as mvm-fgs on Bigrock and mvm-1pq, which was an exit built inside
the blast that kills the sentry: a spot chosen without regard to what is around
it. Three maps now, so the fault is likelier in how a spot is picked or vetted
than in each map's config.

Worth checking together with the bots falling on Rottenburg in the same session,
since a ledge the nav walks along would explain both.

configs/defenderbots/map/mvm_rottenburg.cfg holds the spots.
notes:
MEASURED, offline, across every shipped config at once. mvm-z83.27.

Rottenburg's declared exit is not beside a drop. No fall over a step within 150, 300 or 500 units of 1723 -199 -407, nor beside any of the 8 exit-ring points around any of its three declared nests. Rottenburg's 11 hurting falls are all above z 0 and every spot the config names is below z -140.

Rottenburg sets MovingNests, so the exit that dropped the player was ring-placed around a relocated nest. Nothing vets the exit ring: TELEPORTER_EXIT_RADIUS_SAFE is 500, eight sides, no drop check. Filed as its own bead.

Share of areas whose exit ring has a hurting fall beside it: Decoy 32 percent with 28 lethal, Mannhattan 10, Mannworks 10, Coaltown 6, Bigrock 1, Rottenburg 1.

The three-maps hypothesis holds but not on the maps this bead names.

title: The engineer walks the map to place his teleporter exit
description:
The engineer cannot reach Bigrock's teleporter spot, so he builds where he
stands, in the bot lane.

## The cause

The exit spot is at -178 3921 318 and both nests sit at z 250 to 260, so it is
about 70 units up a rock. BuildStandPoint snaps to the nearest nav area within
120 units and gets the floor below, which passes the storey check. He walks to
the foot of the rock, every side is refused from down there, the deadline is set
to now, and the stand point becomes his own position.

## What shipped, behind FEATURE_ENGINEER_CLIMBS, off

Two halves. He crouch jumps at a named spot 24 to 72 units above him, bounded at
six attempts. And the fallback goes to the nest ring rather than to his feet.

Measured on Bigrock, four attempts each arm: distance from the sampled exit to
the rock spot was 3384 units with the switch off and 237 with it on, so the
fallback works. The jump does not. No sample under 100 units and the minimum
equal to the median, so he never lands on the rock at all.

It is off because half of it works and the half that was asked for does not.

## The line that separates the three candidates is in (2026-08-28)

Behind redbots_manager_debug_actions, TeleporterClimbToSpot now writes a
[teleclimb] line naming the reason and the numbers behind it: the rise against
its 24 to 72 window, the flat distance against 140, and the climb count against
six. The call site writes one too when the branch is not reached at all, so
silence means the debug is off rather than the branch being skipped.

Each candidate now writes a different line:

  "nothing to climb"     the window does not match the real rise
  "too high to climb"    the same, from the other side
  "too far out to climb" he is refused on distance, not height
  "climbing"             the jump is being made and does not carry
  "not asked"            the branch never runs

## Next

Run Bigrock with sm_redbots_manager_debug_actions 1 and
sm_redbots_feature_engineer_climbs 1, and read which line comes back. The switch
stays off until then.
notes:
CAUSE FOUND, offline. mvm-z83.27.

The bead has the mechanism right and misses the decisive fact: there is no nav area on the rock at all. The spot is 68 units above the nearest surface anywhere on the map.

So BuildStandPoint at util.sp:630 is not choosing badly between candidates. All 8 sides are accepted, all 8 land on the floor below with drops of 60 to 92, every one under BUILD_STAND_STOREY of 100, and the worst misses the refusal by 8 units. None lands on the spot's own ground because the spot has none.

title: Bots never leave spawn on some community maps
description:
What kelly-cs's PR #1 solves, and the reason it exists at all: it is the
prerequisite for community map support in tf2-archipelago PR #2.

## The problem

Some community maps have a usable nav mesh and the bots still never leave
spawn. They are prepared, they have shopped, and they stand there. On a map the
run has drawn, that is the whole team doing nothing for the mission.

Reported on Area 52 and Thriller. It happens occasionally on Valve maps too,
which makes it a bug here and not only a custom-map one.

## What the PR does

Watches a prepared defender that stays in or near a RED spawn and makes no
progress leaving it, then teleports it to the map's objective: the capture
trigger, then func_capturezone, then a control point, then the shortest bomb
travel by nav distance. Map-independent, and it still needs usable nav near one
of those.

Three convars, and sm_dump_spawn_nav to see what the watcher thinks.

## Why it is worth having beyond custom maps

A bot that cannot leave spawn asks for a path over and over. The one in-play
crash of 2026-08-26 was the engine watchdog firing inside NavAreaBuildPath,
twelve seconds after a stuck engineer was logged. Whether this fixes that is
unmeasured, but the two are the same shape.

## Related

mvm-6rt, mvm-ipf and mvm-zx0 are engineers stuck on particular maps. This is the
general case and the recovery rather than the cause.

title: Scale BLU down when few humans are playing
description:
Clarified by the ask, and it is not what the title first said. Balancing here
means making a difficult mission winnable when few people turned up, by taking
the robots down rather than by leaning harder on the RED bots' AI.

  "helping on difficult mission based on the number of actual players in the
  server, to not depend too much on bots ai. it should reduce blue team bots
  damage and health, and speed? need to test out things"

That last clause is the design. Nobody knows which of the three matters, so the
deliverable is the three knobs plus the runs that say which one to keep.

## The three

- BLU damage
- BLU health
- BLU speed

Speed is the one to be most careful with. A slower robot is not simply a weaker
one: it changes how long a wave takes, how much the bomb travels between deaths,
and how much money is on the field at once. It may turn out to be the strongest
lever or the one that ruins the pacing, and only a run will say.

## Scaled by what

The count of humans on RED, not the team size setting. Six players who own the
slot should see the mission Valve tuned; one player alone should see it bend.
The scale moves when somebody joins or leaves, so it is read where the roster
changes rather than once at wave start.

## Method

docs/testbed-metrics.md is the rule: a knob ships on only once a run has said it
helped, and mvm-15t exists because a one-map result was not trusted. Feature
switches in source/redbots3/features.sp so the two arms of an A/B are the same
build, all three defaulting to off.

Waves lost is the number that decides it. Deaths per wave is the number that
says whether it bent the mission or removed it: a scale that makes the robots
harmless has not balanced anything.

## Related

apw-7ts asks for the same thing from the Archipelago side, as an upgrade
multiplier that grows as the slot empties. Same question, other half of the
lever: this one weakens BLU, that one strengthens RED. Whichever reads better in
play should be the one that ships, and they should not both be on at once.

## Where it is exposed

The launcher's Bots page and the .env, if it ships.
close_reason:
Done. Three levers built, all three measured, one kept.

Health at 0.5 moves robots killed from 62.5 to 108 against a band of 52 to 64,
and clears three waves in eight where twenty four attempts cleared none. Damage
worked more weakly, speed showed nothing, and both were removed on the
reporter's call in v2.23.0.

The reason the first measurement said health and speed did nothing was real and
is fixed: both were written on the robot inside the spawn frame, where the
popfile overwrites them, and health also needs 'max health additive bonus'
because TF2 recomputes the maximum from attributes.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Built, in v2.19.0, and off by default. Nothing measured yet.

Three convars, each the scale at one human on RED, rising to 1.0 at six:

  sm_redbots_manager_blu_damage_scale
  sm_redbots_manager_blu_health_scale
  sm_redbots_manager_blu_speed_scale

So 0.7 means a lone player fights robots at seven tenths, three players at about
six sevenths, and six players fight the mission Valve wrote. The assist fades as
the team fills rather than switching off at a threshold nobody can feel.

Counted on humans, not on how full RED is. That is the whole point of the ask:
bots filling the seats is what this exists to stop leaning on, so a team of six
bots still gets the full assist.

Where each lands:
- health, on BLU spawn, after the popfile has decided what the robot is worth.
  Both current and max, or a robot spawns hurt instead of smaller
- speed, on the same spawn, through the move speed bonus attribute
- damage, on SDKHook_OnTakeDamage on the victim. Hooked on everybody who joins
  and asking whether the attacker is a robot, because a wave brings robots by
  the hundred and a defender joins once

## One thing I changed my mind about

The bead said feature switches in features.sp. I wrote them, then took them out.
The convar at 1.0 already means off, so a switch that also had to be on is two
ways to say one thing, and a run could turn the switch on and measure nothing.

What the switches were for is still needed, so it moved: BluAssist_Describe
appends what is set to the line the results already carry, and the test-bed
gained TESTBED_BOT_CVARS for setting any convar rather than only a feature.
A results file still says which arm produced it.

Baseline arm running now: six waves of Decoy with all three off.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
First measurement: the damage lever on Decoy, six waves each arm.

                        off        at 0.7
  cleared               6 (100%)   6 (100%)
  defenders died        28         20
  deaths per wave       median 5   median 2
                        range 1-9  range 1-8
  robots killed/wave    median 91  median 78
  damage dealt          107212     95151

The direction is right and the size is worth having: a third fewer deaths, and
the median wave went from five dead to two.

## Why this is not a result yet

The ranges overlap almost completely, 1-9 against 1-8. docs/testbed-metrics.md
says an arm ships on when it clears the spread of the arm it was measured
against, and this does not come close. Six waves against that much wave-to-wave
variance cannot separate them.

## The bigger problem with the experiment

Both arms cleared all six waves. On Decoy with six bots the mission is already
winnable, so the lever moved the margin and not the outcome, and the outcome is
what this bead is about: making a difficult mission winnable when few people
turned up.

Measuring a balancing lever needs a mission the bots actually lose. mvm-72s says
Bavarian Botbash wave 3 wipes the bot team, which is the shape of thing to
measure against: waves lost is the number that decides this, and it was zero in
both arms here so it decided nothing.

Next: rerun the pair on a mission the bots lose, then health and speed the same
way, then a second map before anything ships on.

## A note on reading the report

go run ./testbed/report A.jsonl B.jsonl prints "B -> A" in its compared block,
so the second file is the before. I read it the wrong way round first and had
the lever looking harmful for a minute.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The damage lever at 0.7, read against the band. It does nothing.

Eight attempts, mvm_rottenburg_advanced1 wave 1, six bots and the host. The band
in docs/testbed-metrics.md is twenty four attempts on the unchanged build, so it
is the control and only this arm needed running.

                    band median   band quartiles   at 0.7
  held for          160s          154 to 192       155.8   inside
  defenders died    24            22 to 31         21.0    just under
  robots killed     58            52 to 64         54.5    inside

Eight of eight lost, against twenty four of twenty four for the band.

The rule on this repo is that an arm whose median falls inside those quartiles
has shown nothing. Two of the three are inside and the third is one point under
the lower quartile, which is not a result either. The wave is lost every time
in both arms.

So a thirty per cent cut to robot damage does not bend this mission. That is
worth knowing plainly: the earlier Decoy reading, deaths 28 to 20, was the
margin moving on a mission that was already won, and it did not carry.

## What this does not say

It does not say damage is the wrong lever, only that 0.7 is too small a dose to
show up here. Running 0.5 next tells the two apart: if a cut that large still
leaves the median inside the band, damage is the wrong lever and health and
speed are where to look. If it moves, the lever works and the question becomes
what dose is fair rather than whether it does anything.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Dose-response, same wave, same band. Damage works, but only at a big dose.

  band, 24 attempts   0 cleared    robots killed median 58, quartiles 52 to 64
  0.7,   8 attempts   0 cleared    median 54    inside the band
  0.5,   8 attempts   1 cleared    median 75    outside it

Held for: band median 160 quartiles 154 to 192; at 0.7 155.8; at 0.5 189.3.

At 0.5 three attempts ran past 270 seconds against a band that tops out at 286
across twenty four, and one of the eight cleared a wave the unchanged build lost
twenty four times out of twenty four.

## What it says

Damage is a real lever and 0.7 is too small a dose to see. Robots killed at 0.5
sits outside the band's quartiles, which is the documented bar, and it is the
number that moved most: the team gets through half again as many robots.

## What it does not say

One clear in eight against none in twenty four is suggestive and not proof on
its own. Held-for is still inside the band at both doses, so what changed is how
much the team kills rather than how long they last.

And a lever that needs a thirty to fifty per cent cut to show up is a blunt one.
Worth measuring health and speed against the same band before choosing: the
point is the mission bending, and one of the three may do it at a dose that does
not read as the robots being made harmless.

title: A bot shopping at the station never mirrors the player's ready
description:
Reported from a nightly run: an engineer beside spawn who never pressed F4,
while a player on RED had.

## Cause

`UpdateDefenderReadiness` says of itself, at
`source/redbots3/nextbot_behavior.sp:762`:

> Several places set a bot ready and gating each of them would be four chances
> to miss one, so this takes the ready away again while the nest is unfinished,
> **every frame, wherever it came from.**

It did not run every frame. `CTFBotTacticalMonitor_Update` returns early for a
bot standing in the upgrade zone with a `DefenderUpgrade` action, and that
return sat above the readiness call. So a bot shopping at the station had no
readiness of its own at all. Only the upgrade action's own exits set it, and the
human-mirror never applied to it.

The mirror is the half that matters here. With a player on RED the bots are
supposed to follow him:

    if (AnyHumanOnRed())
        SetPlayerReady(actor, AnyHumanReadyOnRed());

A bot that never reaches that line does not follow anybody. The upgrade station
on Decoy is beside spawn, which is where the engineer was standing.

## Fix

The readiness update now runs before the early returns, which is what the
comment already claimed. `SetPlayerReady` no-ops when the flag already agrees,
so running it on more frames costs nothing on the wire.

`READY_GRACE` is 90 seconds and only ever forces ready, so starting its deadline
during shopping cannot hold a wave that would otherwise have started.

## If it recurs

This is the mechanism found and fixed, not a confirmed reproduction of that
exact engineer. If a bot is seen unready beside spawn again, it is a different
path, and the thing to capture is whether he was inside the upgrade zone.
close_reason: Fixed. UpdateDefenderReadiness moved above the upgrade-zone early return in CTFBotTacticalMonitor_Update, which is what its own comment already claimed. Compiles clean, warning count unchanged at 54.

title: Decoy ships with no sniper spots, left over from a test
description:
`configs/defenderbots/map/mvm_decoy.cfg` carries this, and nothing else where
the spots used to be:

    //TEMPORARILY REMOVED FOR A TEST

The `SniperSpot` block held six origins. Commit 5aedaff, "a sniper with no spot
fights, and the test-bed counts duplicate buildings", took them out to test the
no-spot path. They were never put back.

## It is in the shipped tag

`v2.15.0` is what `DEFENDERBOTS_VERSION` names and what the nightly builds, and
`git show v2.15.0:configs/defenderbots/map/mvm_decoy.cfg` has no `SniperSpot`
section at all. So every nightly run of Decoy plays with zero sniper spots.

The regression is visible in one line of the server console. Cowser's v1.9.0
bundle logged:

    Config_LoadMap: mvm_decoy: 6 sniper, 3 nest, 0 nest-tank, 0 nest-notank,
    3 dispenser, 0 tele-in, 1 tele-out

A current run should log `0 sniper` on the same map.

## Fix

Restore the six origins from 5aedaff and delete the comment. They are in the
history, so this is a revert of that hunk rather than a re-survey:

    git show 5aedaff -- configs/defenderbots/map/mvm_decoy.cfg

Then check the other map configs for the same thing. One test comment left in
one file is a habit, not an accident, and `Config_LoadMap` prints a count for
every category on every map, so a sweep of the counts against the configs finds
any others cheaply.

Worth adding a test that fails when a map config carries a "TEMPORARILY" or
"TODO" marker, or when a category the map is expected to have comes back zero.
The line that would have caught this was already being printed and nobody was
reading it.

title: Engineer freezes during setup on Decoy
description:
k-kaneta on 1.9.0: engineers can freeze during the setup phase on Decoy with no
warning. Still not reproduced.

## The detector now exists (2026-08-29)

wave.IdleReport reads the bot samples every run already wrote and names any
defender whose action stack holds only monitors, which is a bot handed nothing to
do. It runs on every attempt without being asked for.

Validated against the injector: sm_redbots_debug_empty_stack marks one engineer,
and the report reads him at 72 of 72 samples with no action and nothing fired,
against nought for every other defender in the same run.

## Not reproduced, and one near miss

Reading the report over every run of 2026-08-28 turned up engineers at 100% idle
in idlefault-on-* and idlefault-off-*. Those are the runs the injector was armed
in, so they are the fault being injected and not the bead reproducing. Every
other run of the day has no fully idle engineer.

## What the injected runs do say

FEATURE_WATCH_IDLE_BOTS does not reliably rescue an empty stack: with it on, one
run still read 60 of 60 samples idle and another 18 of 54, against 72 of 72 and
55 of 90 with it off. So the rescue is not the thing to lean on if this bead ever
does reproduce.

## Next

Sweep class x custom loadouts x manager mode with the report asserting on each
run. The stock sniper of [[mvm-bj8]] lived in one cell of that matrix and nothing
ever played it.
design:
## Prior art: Valve's own MvM engineer never sits still

Source SDK 2013 ships
`src/game/server/tf/bot/behavior/engineer/mvm_engineer/tf_bot_mvm_engineer_idle.cpp`.
It is the robot engineer rather than a defender, but it is the same problem and
`DefenderEngineerIdle` in our stuck trace is plainly modelled on it. Read it,
never copy it: the SDK licence requires derivatives stay free and carry Valve's
LICENSE, which this repo cannot currently satisfy since it has no LICENSE file.

The one structural difference worth the read: **Valve's Idle only ever returns
Done() when the bot is dead.** Every other tick returns Continue(). It has no
terminal state where there is nothing left to do, which is exactly the state a
bot stuck for twelve seconds is in.

It gets there by re-searching rather than deciding once. Each tick it checks
whether it holds a valid nest hint, and if it does not, it looks for one again,
throttled by a one-to-two second cooldown so the search does not run flat out.
A nest that cannot be found this tick is simply looked for again on the next.

That is the thing to check on our side. If the pick runs once and schedules
nothing when it comes back empty, a bot that fails the first search has no
second one, and it stands there until the wave ends. The cooldown is what makes
retrying cheap enough to do forever.

Its selection is also more forgiving than one pass. It sorts candidate nests by
distance to the bomb, prefers stale nests left by dead engineers, then unowned
free ones, and if nothing sits in the wanted band it will take an out-of-range
nest and advance or retreat to it instead of giving up. It also refuses nests
too close to the bomb. A search with one acceptance rule fails far more often
than one with a fallback tier.

Worth reading for mvm-zx0 and mvm-ipf too, which are the same file family: the
build and repair states are `tf_bot_mvm_engineer_build_sentry.cpp` and the
teleporter pair beside it.
