title: Bots ignore the tank, and a bad lineup cannot kill it
description:
k-kaneta, playing 1.9.0:

> Tank seems a bit problematic? some bot doesn't really care about tank, and bad
> team comp can make some tank unkillable possibly

Two separate faults, and the second is the one that ends runs.

## Bots do not target the tank

Some bots carry on with the robot wave while the tank rolls past. The tank is a
different kind of target: it does not shoot back, it never stops, and ignoring
it costs the mission rather than the fight in front of you.

Find what the bot AI treats as a threat and check whether the tank is in it at
all. A tank that is never a target explains "doesn't really care" exactly.

## A lineup that cannot out-damage it

The worse half. A tank has a fixed health pool and a fixed time to reach the
hatch, so there is a damage-per-second floor below which it simply arrives. A
lineup with no burst — the reason a Demoman or a Heavy is usually there — sits
under that floor, and no amount of playing well moves it.

This overlaps mvm-lfh (the Demoman is the weakest seat and is in every lineup)
from the other side: that bead asks whether the seat earns its place, this one
finds the case where the lineup needs it and does not have it.

Two things worth having, in order:

1. Bots target the tank when one is on the map, and weight it by how close it
   is to the hatch. A tank at the last stretch outranks anything else alive.
2. The lineup accounts for it. If the mission has tank waves and the chosen
   comp has no burst damage, either the comp changes or the run says so before
   the wave rather than after the loss.

## Test

Decoy has tank waves and is what the playtesters are on. Run it with a
deliberately poor lineup (the all-Scout case the config already allows via
`srcds_bot_team_comp`) and confirm both that the bots shoot the tank and that
the wave is winnable.
design:
## Prior art, and the cause of the first half

Read against Source SDK 2013, which carries the whole TF bot tree officially.
Read it, never copy it: its licence requires derivatives stay free and ship
Valve's LICENSE, and this repo does not even have a LICENSE file of its own yet.

The tank is not invisible to the engine's threat model. `CTFBaseBoss` is
declared `: public NextBotCombatCharacter`, and Valve's
`src/game/server/tf/bot/tf_bot_vision.cpp` collects other NextBots alongside
players when it gathers potentially visible entities. So a tank is a thing a
TFBot can see.

The gap is ours, and it is simpler than "doesn't weight the tank properly".
Every threat scan in `source/redbots3/nextbot_behavior.sp` is a
`for (int i = 1; i <= MaxClients; i++)` loop over player slots. A tank is the
entity `tank_boss`, which holds no player slot, so it is outside every one of
those loops. Nothing rejects the tank as a target; nothing ever offers it as
one.

That explains the shape of the report exactly. k-kaneta said *some* bots ignore
the tank, not all of them, and the exception is the Demoman:
`source/redbots3/demoman_stickies.sp` has bespoke tank handling
(`STICKY_TANK_RANGE`, `FEATURE_DEMO_TANK_PIPES`). One class was taught about
tanks by hand and the rest were not.

`tank_boss` appears twice more and neither is targeting:
`nextbot_behavior.sp:1697` is a path-obstruction filter, and `dbtm.sp` counts
spawns.

So the fix is not a weighting change. Threat selection has to be able to
consider a non-player entity at all, which is a wider change than it looks:
every scan assumes a client index. Decide whether the tank becomes a synthetic
threat those loops can carry, or whether tank targeting sits beside them as its
own pass.

For the second half, the damage floor, `src/game/server/tf/player_vs_environment/
tf_base_boss.h` has the accessors that set the sum: initial health and max
speed. Health over the time it takes to walk its path is the DPS a lineup has
to beat.

title: The red team caps at six, and raising it stops bots spawning
description:
Blabber:

"is it possible to fill red team up more than 6?"
"the bots are really dumb so i'd like to add more but the max player count is 6"
"i tried changing the number to 12 but then it stops adding bots"

Two separate things, and the second is ours.

MvM is built around a six-slot red team: tf_mvm_defenders_team_size, the
upgrade station, the ready-up panel and the scoreboard all assume it. Raising
it is a game-side question and may not be winnable.

But raising it silently breaks us rather than refusing: the bots stop being
added at all, so a player who tries twelve ends up with fewer bots than they
had at six. Whatever the real ceiling is, find it, clamp to it, and log the
clamp. Failing loudly at seven beats spawning nothing at twelve.

First job is to reproduce: set the size to 12 on a testbed run and find where
the add path gives up (slot allocation, the team assign, or the ready gate).
design:
## Cause

Nothing in this mod ever wrote `tf_mvm_defenders_team_size`.
`sm_redbots_manager_defender_team_size` was raised to twelve, twelve bots were
asked for with `tf_bot_add ... red`, and the game went on refusing RED past its
own six. The bots went nowhere and nothing said why, which is the "stops adding
bots" in the report.

There is a second disagreement worth knowing about. The Archipelago plugin
reads the *game's* convar for its own fill and trim
(`tf2_archipelago/bots.inc`, `DefenderTeamSize`). So on a server running both,
a mod set to twelve and a game left at six had the plugin actively trimming RED
back to six while the mod tried to fill it. They now agree, because the mod
writes the game's number.

## What was changed

`ConVarChanged_DefenderTeamSize` writes the wanted number to
`tf_mvm_defenders_team_size`, reads it back, and clamps itself to what stuck.
The ceiling is therefore the game's answer at runtime rather than a constant
guessed here, and every call site keeps reading one convar and gets a number the
game will honour. The clamp is logged and announced in chat.

The convar also gained bounds and a description. It had neither.

## Still to do: the reproduction the bead asked for

Whether the game accepts more than six is not answered by this. The code asks
and obeys, which is correct either way, but nobody has yet run the testbed with
the size at twelve to see what `tf_mvm_defenders_team_size` reads back as.

That run is the remaining work, and it decides whether this is now "twelve bots
work" or "the game refuses and says so". Either is an improvement on twelve
bots silently becoming none.

title: Bots spy-check the human player and each other
description:
SwagDoll420: "another bug I found is that when playing as Spy, your teammates keep
trying to call you out as an enemy spy. They also keep trying to Spycheck each
other, and it keeps screwing me over."

Two symptoms in one report:

1. The bots call out the human player as an enemy Spy when he plays Spy.
2. The bots spy-check each other, and the shooting costs the player his run.

Not diagnosed. What the code does today, as a place to start rather than as a
cause: `behavior/spycheck.sp:222` and `:240` pick suspects from the actor's own
team, and neither line filters out a real player. `nextbot_behavior.sp:1034`
suspends the running action for `CTFBotSpyCheck` when it is possible.

The obvious fix is not obviously right. A disguised enemy Spy is meant to look
like a teammate, so a rule that says "never suspect a teammate" removes spy
checking altogether. The discriminator has to separate a human on RED from a
BLU Spy who appears to be on RED, and whether `TF2_GetClientTeam` already
reports the true team rather than the disguise decides how much work that is.

The paranoia behaviour shipped since 1.3: "Spy checking: paranoia from the last
sighting, suspect the teammate who was not there a moment ago." A human player
who moves differently from the bots fits that description every time.
close_reason:
Fixed and measured, and both halves of the report were the same cause.

The sighting rule in Event_PlayerDeath was 'a Spy killed somebody on another team', which a defending Spy satisfies every time he stabs a robot. So the player's own Spy put his whole team on alert, which is why this only happens when somebody plays Spy. A sighting is now a robot's Spy.

The suspect finder also skipped no humans, so a player could be picked as the disguised one. Every robot in this mode is a fake client, so a real player on RED cannot be an enemy Spy. The price is a human on BLU via the mod's join-blue command being unstabbable, which is smaller than a Spy player being frisked by his own team.

Measured with a friendly Spy in the lineup: 187 of 3443 samples spy checking before, 0 of 1676 after. Two lineups without a Spy spent 0 of 8273 samples spy checking, so the trigger was never an actual robot Spy. Firing with a teammate in the crosshair is unchanged at 15 to 18 per cent, which is bots shooting past one another rather than at them, and harmless with friendly fire off.

title: Change bot classes and loadouts mid-mission
description:
Asked independently by two people.

SwagDoll420: "Are you able to switch the bot's classes in between waves?"
CaptPurpleHeart: "is there a way to change the bots mid-mission?"

omaewh4: "Change what? classes and loadouts? It's not here yet".
notes:
Asked a third time, and this one gives the reason.

Swagdoll: "I really wish it was possible to change the bot's classes mid wave,
it would be really useful for when the best bot counters are different for
certain waves"

That is the case for the feature. It is not convenience, it is that a lineup
picked for wave 1 is the wrong lineup for wave 5, and the player has no move to
make about it short of restarting the mission. Note he says mid *wave*, not
between waves like the earlier two asks; between waves is the cheaper half and
probably where this starts.

Third independent request, so P3 -> P2.
The shape it should take, decided.

## Where it lives

A Bots tab in the launcher window, between Session and Log. The tab is only
populated when a server is running; with nothing up it stays empty rather than
showing dead selects. Tab order matters for the same reason the existing comment
in gui_windows.go gives: the run first, then what you do to it, then the log
last, because the log is for when something is wrong.

Note this is a cross-repo bead. The widgets are in tf2-archipelago
(launcher/internal/gui), the behaviour is here.

The picker already exists and is pre-launch only: botTeamPicks and botTeamFrom
in launcher/internal/gui/botteam.go, seat class plus seat loadout, feeding
settings.BotTeam. The live tab is the same widgets with an Apply button instead
of a save, so this is mostly a matter of reusing botteam.go rather than writing
a second picker. Loadouts change live in the same tab; a loadout swap and a
class swap are the same round trip.

Apply writes sm_redbots_manager_team_composition over rcon and tells the mod to
reseat. Nothing new in the protocol.

## The part that is not the GUI

Bots that change class are despawned and respawned, and they lose everything
they bought. On the way back in they must have the money they have earned, and
they must spend it.

Today the respawn path in events.sp sets:

    TF2_SetCurrency(data, GetStartingCurrency(g_iPopulationManager)
                          + GetAcquiredCreditsOfAllWaves())

That is the game's own wave accounting and it is right as far as it goes. It
misses Archipelago money, and it misses it everywhere, not only here:
MvM_GrantCredits in the AP plugin's mvm.inc pays each live player a Cash Bundle,
and MvM_IsPlayer is `!IsFakeClient(client)`. Bots have never received a single
Cash Bundle. 200 credits each, and the team the player is relying on never sees
any of it.

So the respawn number is starting, plus acquired across all waves, plus every
Cash Bundle the run has been granted. The third term does not exist yet in any
running total, because a bundle is a one-shot drop at the moment it lands. It
needs to be counted and kept somewhere both sides can read.

Then they buy: on respawn the bot runs the full upgrade pass and spends down to
what it can no longer afford, rather than trickling purchases over the next
wave. A class swap between waves that leaves six unupgraded bots on the field is
worse than not swapping.

## What to check when it is done

Swap the whole team mid-mission on wave 5 and confirm each bot's currency
matches a human's in the same run to the credit, and that the upgrade pass has
spent it before the wave starts.
The money half of this bead is done, so a mid-mission class change no longer has
to solve it.

A bot that is despawned and respawned as another class comes back through the
join path, and that path used to set currency from the game's own record alone:
starting currency plus credits acquired across the waves. Neither term has ever
seen a Cash Bundle, so every reseat threw the team's Archipelago money away.

It now goes through SetCurrencyWithBundles in redbots3/archipelago.sp, which
adds what the Archipelago plugin says it has paid. Optional native, zero on a
server without the plugin, rechecked whenever a library comes or goes.

What is left on this bead is the part that was always the work: the tab, the
selects, the apply, and the bots buying everything they can afford on the way
back in. The number they buy with is now right.
close_reason: Built and shipped in v2.18.1: the lineup changes on a running mission from the Bot Switcher tab in both interfaces, from the settings save, and from !ap bots. Money survives it, measured on a live server. Documented in both languages. What is left is a play-test with a human on RED, filed separately, because that is confirmation rather than work.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Where it has to be reachable from, decided in the session of 2026-08-26:

- The `!ap` menu in the game, so a player switching a lineup between waves never
  leaves the server.
- A tab on the launcher's home page, in the window and in the terminal both,
  named "Bot Switcher", sitting between the mission list and the log. Not a
  second editor: the same seats, and an Apply that reaches the running server.

Both interfaces have to read well: columns lined up, and the seats the mod draws
named as such rather than left blank.

And the constraint that decides the mechanism: the bots must not lose money
across a switch. That is what makes a kick-and-rejoin viable at all, because the
join path already sets currency through SetCurrencyWithBundles. It is to be
measured on a live server, not read off the code.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Built and measured, 2026-08-26.

## The mod

The lineup convar now acts when it is retyped, which it never did:
CollectMissingTeamComposition only names seats nobody holds, so a full RED was
already the team it wanted whatever the convar said.

ReseatDefenderBots kicks exactly as many bots as the new list has seats nobody
holds, picked from the classes the list no longer asks for. The one-second fill
timer replaces them against the new list, so the team converges without a second
mechanism. A kicked bot comes back through the join path, which is where the
seat, the loadout and SetCurrencyWithBundles already live, so no class-change or
refund path had to be written.

Mid-wave the change is held until the break. Kicking a bot during a wave drops
its buildings and walks the replacement in from spawn with the bomb halfway
home.

sm_redbots_reseat is the blunt one for a loadout change: reload the file and
recycle the whole team, because a weapon is handed out on the way in and never
again, so a change that moves no class still has to reach every bot.
sm_dump_credits is the instrumentation for the money question.

Measured on a live testbed server, from the mod's own log:

  Reseat: the lineup wants 4 seat(s) nobody holds, kicked 4 bot(s) for them
  Fill: asked for 4, RED holds 2 of 6
  Fill: the named team filled 4 of 4
  Reseat: the lineup changed mid-wave, holding it until the break

Both branches, on a running mission: the between-waves swap kept the two bots
whose class the new list still wanted and replaced the other four, and the
mid-wave change deferred rather than tearing the team apart.

## The launcher

internal/botlive holds the part neither interface owns: the commands to send and
in what order (the reseat last, because the loadout file is read when it runs),
what the team looks like seat by seat, and LiveOnly.

LiveOnly is the one that matters to anybody playing. Saving a setting on a
running server restarted it, which ended the mission. It now compares everything
that is not the bot team, so a lineup change applies over RCON and a port change
still restarts. Written as a comparison of everything else rather than of the
team, so a setting added later is not live until somebody says so.

A "Bot Switcher" tab in both interfaces, between the mission list and the log:
the seats in three columns, the classes the mod may draw the rest from, and one
button that applies. Not a second editor, because the seats and the weapons
already live on the Bots page of the settings.

## In the game

!ap bots opens the same team as a menu: pick a seat, pick a class. It edits the
mod's convar directly and the mod's own change hook decides whether that is a
reseat now or one held for the break, so there is no second copy of that rule.
Gated on the same flag as the mission switch: both decide what everybody on RED
plays for the rest of the run.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The money question, measured rather than read.

sm_dump_credits added for it. Sampled every two seconds across a whole-team
swap on a live server, six bots, mid-mission:

  t+2s   scout 400  scout 400  scout 400  scout 400  sniper 400  sniper 400
  t+4s   scout   0  scout 400  scout   0  scout 400  sniper  50  sniper 400
  t+8s   scout   0  scout   0  scout   0  scout   0  sniper  50  sniper  50

Every bot came back holding 400, which is what the game's own accounting says it
was owed, and spent it down over the next few seconds. Not one credit lost
across the swap, and no trickle: they buy on the way in rather than over the
wave that follows.

That is the join path doing it, through SetCurrencyWithBundles, which is the
reason kick-and-rejoin was the right mechanism and no refund path had to exist.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Whether it crashes the server, since kicking six clients mid-mission is the sort
of thing that would.

Control, current tip, nothing touched: two waves of Decoy, no crash.
Reseat run, same map: three lineup changes on a running mission, one of them the
whole team at once, three waves. No crash either. The crash counter in the
container was four before both runs and four after.

The first run of the evening did crash three times, all of them at startup and
all before the first reseat was sent, which is the intermittent segfault mvm-y7e
already covers rather than anything new.

One correction to the launcher on the back of this. Apply sent
sm_redbots_reseat every time, which recycles the whole team, so a one-seat
change threw six bots' upgrades away when the mod's own convar hook would have
kicked one. botlive.Commands now sends the recycle only when the rendered
loadout file actually differs, and leaves a pure lineup change to the hook.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Correcting the comment above: the reseat run did crash. I read the counter
before the run had finished.

Final tally, one run each:

  control, nothing touched      2 waves, 0 crashes
  reseat run, 3 lineup changes  1 wave finished, 1 crash

The crash was at 21:57:30, 88 seconds after the last reseat at 21:56:02 and well
into the wave that followed it. Normal play happened in between: shopping,
Fred building a sentry, Albert putting up a shield. So it is not a kick blowing
up in the handler.

One sample each is not enough to convict or acquit the reseat, and I am not
going to claim it is clean on this evidence.

The one thing a reseat does that an ordinary wave does not is take a bot off the
field while it owns buildings. Fred built a sentry seconds after coming in, and
a kicked engineer's buildings outliving their owner is a well-worn way to crash
a Source server. That is the mechanism worth eliminating before running the
comparison again.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The crash has a name, and it is not the reseat.

I had been counting "core dumped" lines, which was the wrong thing to count.
Most of them are the test-bed restarting the server while it stages the mod:
every one of those is preceded by "installed the bots and the statistics
plugin". Only one crash across the whole evening happened during play, and it
reads:

  [defenderbots] stuck: Waldo (engineer) at 346 551 544 for 12s,
                 MainAction < TacticalMonitor < DefenderEngineerIdle < ScenarioMonitor
  WatchDog! Server took too long to process (probably infinite loop).
  FATAL ERROR: Host_Error: WatchdogHandler called - server exiting.

That is the engine watchdog killing the process on a long frame, not memory
corruption from kicking clients. The segfault is the watchdog's exit, not the
cause.

Waldo came in on the fill at 22:01:32 and was never reseated, so this particular
crash cannot be laid at the reseat's door at all. The stuck engineer belongs to
the family mvm-6rt, mvm-zx0 and mvm-ipf already cover, and the watchdog to
apw-7v6.

Two things follow. The reseat stands, with the building teardown kept: it is
right whether or not it was ever the cause. And the test-bed should stop
reporting an install-time restart as a crash in what is being measured, because
that is what sent me chasing this for an hour.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Shipped, in mod v2.18.1 and launcher f146b92.

What is done: the lineup changes on a running mission, from the launcher tab in
both interfaces, from the settings save, and from !ap bots in the game. Money
survives it, measured. The recycle is narrowed to weapon changes so a one-seat
swap costs one bot its upgrades rather than six.

What is not done, and is what the bead's own "what to check when it is done"
asks for: nobody has played a real mission through this. Every measurement here
is from the test-bed with no humans on RED, and the seat a human takes is seat
one, which is the seat the switcher renumbers around. That wants a play-test
before this is called finished.

Left open for that reason.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Correcting the comment above, which was wrong.

I claimed most of the "core dumped" lines were install-time restarts, on the
grounds that each was preceded by "installed the bots and the statistics
plugin". That line prints every thirty seconds for the whole run. Every line in
the log is preceded by it, so it separates nothing. The inference was worthless.

Where that leaves the evidence, honestly:

  control run            2 waves    0 crashes in the measured window
  reseat run 1           1 wave     1 crash
  reseat run 3           0 waves    1 crash

One of the two, at 22:03:54, is a watchdog kill after Waldo got stuck in
DefenderEngineerIdle for 12 seconds, and Waldo was never reseated. That one is
not the reseat. The other has no watchdog line, so it is a real segfault and I
have not explained it.

So the reseat is not cleared. Two crashes in two reseat runs against none in one
control run is not proof either, but it is not nothing, and I am not going to
call the feature safe on it.

Symbolising core.409 next rather than running more pairs: a stack says what a
counter cannot.

mvm-427, which I filed off the bad inference, is wrong as written and needs
rewriting or closing.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The reseat is cleared, properly this time.

The crashes I could not explain were the test-bed copying a live mapped
cbasenpc.ext.2.tf2.so over itself. build.sh gave the staged prebuilt extensions
a new timestamp on every build, so the container's thirty-second installer saw
them as new and rewrote them under the running server. I rebuilt several times
tonight with a run in flight, which is why the reseat runs crashed and the
control did not: the control was the one run I did not build during.

Full working from the core is on mvm-tnt, now closed. Fixed in build.sh with
cp -p.

So the evidence against the reseat was an artefact of how I was working, and I
put it on this bead twice as though it were a property of the feature. The one
real in-play crash of the evening was the watchdog after a stuck engineer, on a
bot that had never been reseated.

What still stands unchanged: the lineup change works, the money survives it
measured, and nobody has played a real mission through it yet.

title: Custom bot loadouts, picked per weapon slot
description:
Cowser asked for it: "it'd be nice to have more customization for what they can
use... like instead of Scorch Shot for the Phlog build, it's the Gas Passer. or
instead of Kunai, it's Big Earner"

omaewh4: "Oh so you mean creating your own loadout, a little like the 'team
profile' i did with the save/load/delete functionality?" then "adding that to the
backlog, that does not touch bots AI so will be a joy to do lol"

Drafts already exist: specs/custom-loadouts.md here and the launcher side in
tf2-archipelago.
close_reason: Built, in both interfaces, with docs. The catalogue is generated from the mod's pools and the game's schema, the resolution layer is botloadout.Library with the custom: key, and the Loadouts page builds and names them. No mod change was needed: GetServerLoadoutWeapon takes whatever index the file carries.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Started on the data half, which the launcher-side draft says to get right first.

gamedata/weapons.go in tf2-archipelago, generated rather than typed:
gamedata/cmd/weapons/generate.py reads the WEAPONS_* pools out of
source/redbots3/loadouts.sp here, and the names out of the game's own
items_game.txt and tf_english.txt. So the catalogue cannot drift from either
the mod or the game, and regenerating is one command.

251 weapons, none nameless.

Two things left out. Stock, because the mod spells it as the default index and
every menu offers it separately. And the repaints: dropping the 15xxx block was
not enough, because the Botkillers and the Festives sit in the 6xx to 11xx
range with the real weapons. Filtering by number left twelve Scatterguns in the
Scout's primary menu; filtering by what they are leaves five.

Getting there needed two parser fixes worth remembering. The item blocks in
items_game.txt nest, so a non-greedy regex ends at the first inner brace and
silently truncated two thirds of them; it counts braces now. And the stock
weapons carry no item_name at all, only "Upgradeable TF_WEAPON_X" -- those are
the MvM stock guns, so they are dropped rather than named.

WeaponsFor(class, slot) and WeaponByIndex are in. weapons_test.go fails if a
class loses a slot, a repaint gets in, or one index picks up two names.

Not done: the settings sub-tab, the CustomLoadout type and the custom: key
prefix. All of that is described in docs/custom-loadouts.md in tf2-archipelago
and none of it needs a mod change, because GetServerLoadoutWeapon takes whatever
index the file carries.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The catalogue is in and pushed: tf2-archipelago 9a7904d.

251 weapons with WeaponsFor(class, slot) and WeaponByIndex, plus a test that
fails if a class loses a slot, a repaint gets in, or one index picks up two
names.

What is left is the launcher menu, and none of it needs a mod change:

- SrcdsBotCustomLoadouts on settings, keyed by the name given
- the custom: key prefix, so a custom loadout is a loadout key like any other
  and BotTeam, Seats and Render stay untouched
- a fourth sub-tab beside Team, Classes and Looks, with the name box and
  Load / Save / Remove copied from presetRow
- the same rule in the terminal

docs/custom-loadouts.md in tf2-archipelago has the design. The one rule to keep
is unknown-is-stock: a saved team naming a loadout since deleted must still
load, which is already how LoadoutByKey behaves.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The resolution layer is in too, and a built loadout now reaches the file the
mod reads.

botloadout.Library holds the built-in presets plus whatever the player has
built. Its zero value is the presets alone, so every caller that has no custom
loadouts keeps working untouched: Render, Anything and the two config paths all
gained a library without a single call site having to care.

settings.SrcdsBotCustomLoadouts is the table, keyed by the name typed. A seat or
a class names one with the custom: prefix, so a built loadout is a loadout key
like any other and BotTeam, Seats and the convar never learned the difference.

Rules worth keeping, each with a test:

- unknown is stock, so a team naming a loadout since deleted still loads rather
  than refusing to open and losing the seats and the blacklist with it
- a loadout belongs to one class, because a Medic cannot hold a Gunslinger
- a built-in key is never read as a custom one
- an index the catalogue does not carry shows as its number, since the mod
  validates nothing and a hand-typed index is still a legal pick

One behaviour did change, and for the better. CustomSeats used to call any
non-empty seat key custom, so a seat naming a loadout that does not exist wrote
a file with class-only blocks in it and told the mod to read it. It is stock
now, and nothing is written. A test in botlive covers both readings.

End to end: srcdsconfig writes "class" "pyro", "primary" "594" and
"secondary" "1180" into loadout.cfg from a Built named in a seat.

Still to build: the menu. A fourth sub-tab beside Team, Classes and Looks, with
the name box and Load / Save / Remove copied from presetRow, and the same in
the terminal.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The menu is in, in both interfaces. The feature is complete.

A Loadouts page in the settings, beside Team, Classes and Looks in the window
and as a seventh tab in the terminal: pick a class, pick a weapon per slot, name
it, Save. Load and Remove beside it, the way the saved teams already work.

The saved ones then appear at the bottom of every weapon menu for that class, on
the Team page and the Classes page, in both interfaces. Built in the settings
and pickable without leaving them, because the menus ask the Loadouts page for
its library rather than holding a copy.

Four slots, not five. configs/defenderbots/loadout.cfg carries primary,
secondary, melee and pda2, and writeSlots names nothing else. The Spy's sapper
is in the mod's weapon pools and has no key in that file, so it is not offered:
a menu entry the mod never reads is worse than a missing one, because it reads
as a broken server rather than a missing feature. I had it in the first draft
and took it out after checking writeSlots.

The trap worth knowing about, now covered by a test. The window reads its menus
as indexes, so the list a menu was filled from and the list it is read back
against must be the same one. Filling from the presets and reading against
presets-plus-built would turn a built loadout at the bottom into whichever
preset sits at its index. loadoutKeyAt takes the library for that reason.

Docs in both languages, Vale clean, and the tab count in the Linux page went
from six to seven.

title: Engineer gets stuck inside a prop on Mannhunt
description:
An engineer wedges at 1014 885 274 on Mannhunt and cannot get out.

## What is known

The wedge is real and reproduces on demand: about three times in thirteen
minutes, unforced, with no robot on the map.

The recovery that should move him was broken. MoveWedgedDefender asked the nav
mesh for the nearest area, which for a bot standing on valid nav and jammed in
scenery is the one under his feet, so the point it picked landed back on him and
the move was thrown away. Fixed in v2.21.3 by searching the neighbouring areas
too.

That fix is measured. Three A/Bs against the old behaviour, with the wedge forced
and robots on the map: nought of six waves cleared before, six of nine after,
and two later runs agreeing.

## What is not known

Whether any of this is what crashed k-kaneta's server. That account, a wedged bot
asking for an impossible path and burning the frame the watchdog kills, is
refuted: v2.30.0 times every path compute and a run with the wedge held, the goal
made impossible and the old recovery in place logged no search over 20ms. Five
approaches, about thirty five attempts, no crash and no long frame.

## Removed along the way

A nest move and a kick, both written for this bead. Neither reached its own
threshold in forty minutes of the real fault, so both were deleted rather than
left as code that cannot run.

## Next

The cores, not the test-bed. Symbolise the two dumps in k-kaneta's bundle and
read the faulting frame instead of inferring it from bot behaviour near the
timestamp. See [[apw-eei]].

The comments below are the working record, in order.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Raised to P0. This map is where a player proved the engineer AI causes the
crashes.

  omaewh4: "Did you have an engineer in the team? Can you try without one?"
  k-kaneta: "ok mannhunt works if there is no engie"

So the prop this bead names is not only a stuck bot: it is what kills the
server. A wedged engineer asks for a path, is reset, comes back to the same
prop and asks again, and the watchdog kills the server on that answer.

v2.20.1 moves a bot wedged three times at one spot, which took Mannworks from
crashing at wave zero to four clean waves. Whether it catches this prop is
unmeasured and is the next run to do: Mannhunt, current build, an engineer in
the lineup.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Mannhunt is a mission on Mannworks, not a map of its own. That matters here:
this bead's prop and the wedge already fixed are very likely the same one.

Measured on Mannworks with Mean Machines, which is the same geometry a Mannhunt
run walks:

  before v2.20.1   crashed at wave zero, engineer stuck 9 to 11 times at
                   1014 885 274, no sentry built
  after            4 of 4 waves, no crash, the wedge recovery fired 4 times and
                   moved him off that spot each time, 42 sentries built

k-kaneta's control says the engineer is what crashes Mannhunt, and the fix moves
a wedged engineer on the map Mannhunt is played on.

Not closed yet. The recovery fired at 1014 885 274, and this bead names a prop
without coordinates, so the two are not yet known to be the same spot. The run
to do is Mannworks with an engineer across its other missions, reading the
"was wedged at" lines: if they all name one place, this bead and mvm-4hs are the
same thing and this one closes.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Mannworks run of 2026-08-27 did not produce a wave result and is not evidence either way.

wave_begin fired at t=4s on mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 with 7 on RED. Thirty
minutes later the stats file still has one wave_begin, no wave_end, and rcon
reports 7 bots total: the six defenders and the test-bed host, no robots alive.
So the wave neither cleared nor lost, it stopped.

No crash: the server answers rcon, the plugin still samples every five seconds,
and the engineer is still logging 'ran out of time to place it' for a dispenser.
Whether the robots never spawned or the wave stopped counting them is not
something this run can say, so I am not filing it as the Mannhunt fault yet.

Next: same mission again with the pop spawn logged, or a different Mannworks
mission to see whether the stall follows the map or the popfile.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
k-kaneta's debug bundle of 2026-08-27 names the spot and gives the control.

Build in the bundle is defenderbots v2.17.1, so this is before the wedge
recovery, and none of it says whether v2.21.0 fixes it.

Three access violations, 0xc0000005:

- 20:03:05 on mvm_coaltown_expert1, 3s after an engineer stuck line
- 20:41:26 on mvm_mannworks_intermediate2, same second as one
- 20:44:04 on mvm_mannworks_intermediate2, 1s after one

Both Mannhunt crashes are the same place: 1014 885 274, wave 1, in
DefenderBuildSentrygun < DefenderEngineerIdle. Both follow the identical shape,
three stuck cycles twelve seconds apart, each ending 'sentry ... ended with
nothing' and starting again, and the crash lands on the third:

  20:40:28, 20:41:13, 20:41:26 crash
  20:42:55, 20:43:51, 20:44:03 crash

The control is in the same log. At 21:13 Mannhunt loads again with no engineer
on RED (demoman player, three soldiers, heavy, demoman) and clears waves 1, 2
and 3. Both crashing attempts had an engineer. That is k-kaneta's 'mannhunt
works if there is no engie', with a coordinate attached.

The wedge is not always fatal: 1014 885 274 appears ten times across five
different engineer bots, and only twice does the server die. So the wedge is the
condition and something else decides.

STUCK_WEDGE_GIVEUP is 3, which is exactly the cycle count that crashes here, so
v2.21.0 should move the bot before the third. That is an argument, not a
measurement, and the run to make is Mannhunt with an engineer on the current
build.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Mannhunt run on v2.21.2, three attempts. The wedge recovery does not fire, and
the reason is in MoveWedgedDefender.

The engineer wedges at 1014 885 274, the same coordinate as k-kaneta's crashes.
The server log counts it reaching 'stuck #9' at that spot. STUCK_WEDGE_GIVEUP is
3, so MoveWedgedDefender was asked six times and returned false every time: not
one 'was wedged at' line in any of the three runs.

Why it refuses, from the code:

  CNavArea area = TheNavMesh.GetNearestNavArea(here, ...)
  CNavArea_GetRandomPoint(area, destination)
  if (GetVectorDistance(here, destination) <= STUCK_RADIUS) return false

He is standing on valid nav. He walked there. So the nearest area is the one
under his own feet, and a random point in it lands within STUCK_RADIUS of him
often enough that the guard on line 1366 throws the move away. The recovery is
built for a bot that is off the mesh and this bot is on it, wedged in geometry.

That also explains why it worked when it was measured. Mannworks Mean Machines
went from crashing at wave 0 to four waves cleared, and that bot was in a
different situation. The fix is real, it just does not cover this one.

What it needs: a destination in a different area, not a random point in the one
he is already in. Adjacent areas, or retry until the point is outside
STUCK_RADIUS with a bounded number of tries, then give up honestly.

Separate and worth its own look: all three runs had robot kills of 0 and wave 1
lost, and one produced no wave result at all. Mannhunt is not being played, it
is stalling, which is the same thing the run of earlier today showed. No crash
in three attempts, but with the waves not running that says very little about
[[apw-eei]].

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Fixed in v2.21.3, verification running.

MoveWedgedDefender now looks past the area under his feet. WedgeEscapePoint
tries MOVE_WEDGED_TRIES points in his own area, accepts the first that clears
STUCK_RADIUS, and when none does walks the four directions of adjacent areas and
tries each of those. Bounded twice: four directions, eight points per area.
Returns false honestly when nothing near him is far enough, which is the case
the old code hit every time by only ever asking his own area.

Compiles clean. Running three Mannhunt attempts now. The line to read is
'was wedged at ... moved to', which appeared zero times across three runs
before this.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Verification on v2.21.3, confirmed loaded over rcon this time. The result is not
what either side expected, and it is not a pass.

Since the restart onto 2.21.3: zero 'stuck:' lines and zero 'was wedged at'
lines in 641 lines of server log. But the engineer is still frozen. Attempt 2
has Wesley with no behaviour in 69 per cent of samples, longest 45 seconds, at
1014 885 274, the same coordinate as always.

So the recovery did not fire because the watchdog never armed. UpdateStuckWatchdog
only counts a bot as stuck when wantsToBeElsewhere is true, which is bPathing or
IsStuck. This engineer is not pathing: he has no behaviour at all. A bot that has
stopped asking to go anywhere is invisible to a watchdog that looks for a bot
failing to get somewhere.

That reframes this bead. On the 2.21.2 runs he logged stuck #1 through #18 at
that spot, so he was pathing and wedged then. Now he is action-less at the same
spot. Two different states at one coordinate, and only one of them is what the
wedge recovery was built for.

The v2.21.3 change is still correct on its own terms: the old code could never
move a bot standing on valid nav, and that was a real defect. It just is not the
thing keeping this engineer at 1014 885 274 in these runs.

Contaminating all of it: all three attempts lost wave 1 with 0 robot kills, same
as every Mannhunt run today. The mission is stalling rather than being played,
so this is not a clean measurement of anything and should not be read as one.
That stall needs its own bead before Mannhunt can verify anything.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Fixed the fault the verification actually found, v2.22.0, behind
sm_redbots_feature_watch_idle_bots, default off.

UpdateStuckWatchdog armed only when wantsToBeElsewhere was true, which is
bPathing or IsStuck. An engineer with an empty action stack is neither, so 45
seconds motionless at 1014 885 274 produced no stuck line and no rescue. A bot
that has stopped asking to go anywhere is the one least likely to recover on its
own, so it was the wrong bot to skip.

The action stack is now read once at the top of the watchdog rather than only at
the logging line, and an empty stack counts as wanting to be elsewhere. The
existing reset is the right remedy: ResetIntentionInterface is what gives a bot
its behaviour back. The log line says 'no behaviour' instead of an empty stack,
so the two states are told apart in a run rather than guessed at.

This is a different fault from the v2.21.3 one and both were real. v2.21.3 fixed
a recovery that could never move a bot standing on valid nav. This fixes a
watchdog that never asked about a bot with nothing to do.

Cannot be verified on Mannhunt while [[mvm-ed0]] stands: every run there loses
wave 1 with zero robot kills, so nothing is being measured. Decoy is the map to
try, which is [[mvm-6rt]] and is queued.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Correction: the wedge recovery does work, and the earlier note on this bead
saying it never fired is wrong.

114 'was wedged at' lines in the SourceMod log, with the destination on each:

  Stuck: Waldo was wedged at 370 589 544, moved to 445 963 554
  Stuck: Waldo was wedged at 359 585 544, moved to 414 841 554
  Stuck: Waldo was wedged at 380 616 544, moved to 331 541 554

The mistake was mine and worth naming: I ran a multi-file grep -c across the
logs, got a column of per-file counts with zeros among them, and read the total
as zero. The line was there the whole time. The v2.21.3 change, searching beyond
the area the bot stands in, is doing its job.

What the wedge count now shows, since v2.25.1 prints it separately from the
total: wedge #3, recovery fires, count resets to 1, he walks back and wedges
again. Reaching stuck #64 on one engineer.

So the fault is not a recovery that refuses. It is a bot that is rescued and
returns, and each round trip costs the path searches the cores blame. That is
the case [[apw-eei]]'s v2.26.0 kick is for, and this makes it the right shape
rather than a guess: after eight wedges the rescue is not working for this bot
and he is taken out.

Neither of the two zero counts I reported earlier should be trusted. This one
was read from a single grep with a total, not a column.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The wedge does not need the wave, and that unblocks measuring it.

The Mannhunt probe: BLU stays at nought for two minutes after the round restart,
on the right popfile, so the population genuinely never builds in the test-bed.
That is [[mvm-ed0]] and it is still open.

But the console during those same two minutes:

  sentry failed for Wesley at 1261.3: could not reach the spot, took another
  stuck: Wesley (engineer) at 1014 885 274 for 12s, stuck #20, wedge #2
  sentry failed for Wesley at 1273.0: ended with nothing

The engineer wedges at 1014 885 274 with no robot anywhere on the map. Same
coordinate as k-kaneta's two crashes, same action stack, during setup.

So every attempt to measure this through waves was solving the wrong problem.
The wedge is reproducible on Mannhunt in about twenty seconds, and the crash
chain the cores show, a bot that cannot reach its goal asking for a path on every
reset, does not involve robots at all.

Measuring it that way now: fifteen minutes per arm, counting stuck lines, nest
moves, kicks, and whether the server is still answering. That is a direct test
of v2.26.0 and v2.27.0 rather than a wave that never happens.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The first wedge A/B was contaminated and its control means nothing.

  on:  0 stuck lines in 15 minutes, alive
  off: 0 stuck lines in 15 minutes, alive

Two arms agreeing looks like a clean negative and is not one. Both ran on the
same server without a restart. The nest moved during the on arm and stayed
moved, so the off arm started with an engineer whose nest was already off the
bad ground. It inherited the fix it was supposed to be a control for.

Re-running with the container recreated between arms, and the control first so
the treated arm cannot leave anything behind for it. Thirteen minutes each.

The measurement is still the right one: the wedge reproduces on Mannhunt during
setup, at 1014 885 274, with no robot on the map, in about twenty seconds. The
control arm should show stuck lines climbing the way it did before any of this,
and if it does not then the wedge is not as reproducible as the earlier runs
suggested and that is worth knowing too.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The corrected A/B is a clean null, and it says something useful.

  off: 3 stuck lines in 13 minutes, alive, 0 nest moves, 0 kicks
  on:  3 stuck lines in 13 minutes, alive, 0 nest moves, 0 kicks

Server recreated between arms, control first. The arms are identical and neither
fix fired once.

The arithmetic says why. A nest move needs WEDGE_RESCUES_BEFORE_NEST_MOVES of 2
rescues at one spot, and each rescue needs STUCK_WEDGE_GIVEUP of 3 wedges: six
wedges at the same place. The kick needs STUCK_WEDGE_KICK of 8. At three wedges
in thirteen minutes, the nest move is about twenty six minutes away and the kick
thirty five. A wave lasts two.

So the thresholds are set for a fault that arrives far faster than this one does.
Both fixes are unreachable in the time a mission actually runs, which is why
neither has ever been seen to fire outside the forced-wedge run.

Also correcting an earlier reading: 'stuck #20' is m_iStuckCount, which is
cumulative for that bot on that map, not a rate. I quoted it as twenty wedges in
two minutes and it was twenty since the map loaded. The real rate is three per
thirteen minutes.

Next is not another A/B at this rate. It is the forced wedge, which is what the
injector in v2.24.0 exists for: hold the engineer, drive the counters past both
thresholds, and compare arms on whether the server survives.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The forced run on Mannhunt measured nothing: the injector never fired, because
it hangs off Event_MvmWaveBegin and Mannhunt's wave is the thing that does not
happen. Three stuck lines in both arms again, no holds logged.

What the log does carry, from the earlier runs where it did fire:

  DebugFaults: holding Wesley (engineer) at 1014 885 274 for 240s
  DebugFaults: Wesley left the hold, 306 units away, so something moved him
  DebugFaults: holding Bob (engineer) at 1014 885 274 for 240s
  DebugFaults: Bob left the hold, 185 units away, so something moved him

Twenty five seconds from hold to rescue, both times, at the crash coordinate.
Something moves a held engineer quickly, which is the recovery doing its job.

Re-running the forced A/B on Decoy. The wedge recovery is not Mannhunt logic, it
is the watchdog, and Decoy is where the injector demonstrably fires: twelve holds
in an earlier session. Measuring the mechanism where it can be exercised beats
measuring it where the wave never starts.

Mannhunt's own fault stays [[mvm-ed0]] and is not this bead.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The forced wedge on Decoy, and it is a negative result about my own fixes.

  off: 11 stuck lines, 0 nest moves, 0 kicks, server alive
  on:   5 stuck lines, 0 nest moves, 0 kicks, server alive

Neither fix fired in either arm, so both arms ran the same code and 11 against 5
is variance between two single runs, not an effect. Reading it as a halving
would be reading noise.

Why they do not fire, from the log of the runs where the injector worked:

  DebugFaults: holding Wesley (engineer) at 1014 885 274 for 240s
  DebugFaults: Wesley left the hold, 306 units away, so something moved him

Twenty five seconds from hold to rescue. MoveWedgedDefender succeeds, and
succeeding sets m_iStuckWedgeCount back to nought. So the count never climbs to
the eight the kick needs. And the nest move needs two rescues from within
STUCK_RADIUS of the same spot, which needs the bot to wedge, be rescued, walk
back to the same place and wedge again before anything else resets him.

So both fixes sit behind counters that the working recovery keeps clearing. They
are close to dead code as written: v2.26.0 and v2.27.0 have never fired outside
a single nest move seen once.

That is the thing to fix, and it is not a threshold tweak. Either the counters
have to survive a successful rescue, or the trigger has to be 'rescued from here
before' rather than 'wedged here N times'. The second is what the fault actually
is: a bot that keeps coming back.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Forty minutes of Mannhunt on v2.28.0, both switches on, the real fault rate with
nothing forced:

  stuck 3, rescues 1, nest moves 0, kicks 0, server alive

from one spot and the kick five. Forty minutes produced one rescue. At this rate
the nest move is over an hour away and the kick most of a day, while a mission
lasts twenty minutes. Both are unreachable in practice, and fixing the counter
bug in v2.28.0 did not change that: it made the kick possible in principle and
it is still never going to happen.

So v2.27.0 and v2.28.0 are dead code as written. Not mistuned. The trigger is
wrong: they wait for repetition that a working recovery prevents, because every
rescue puts the bot somewhere else and he does not always come back.

What did hold up: the server ran forty minutes on the map that crashed
k-kaneta's twice, with three wedges and no crash. The recovery moved him when it
needed to. That is v2.21.3, which is the fix that was actually broken before:
the old code could never move a bot standing on valid nav, which is every wedge

Honest limit on that: no wave ran, so the frame load is lower than a real game.

title: Engineers leave the nest mid-wave hunting metal and get stuck on geometry
description:
An engineer walks off mid-wave for metal he cannot reach, gives up, and comes
back. Reported by Jebby.

## The fault, from reading

He does not pick blind: ComputeHealthAndAmmoVectors ranks candidates and runs
IsPathToVectorPossible on the nearest four. The choice is validated once in
OnStart and then held for the life of the action. Update repaths to the same
entity every second and throws the answer away, so a refused path leaves him
drifting on a zero length path until the pack expires.

Two smaller faults in the same function: the ranked runners-up were discarded, so
there was nothing to fail over to, and m_iAmmoPack was not cleared in OnStart.

## The fix

v2.21.4, behind sm_redbots_feature_ammo_failover, default off. The ranked list
survives, three consecutive refusals advance to the next candidate, and
exhausting the list ends the action and holds it off for three seconds.

## Why it is not closed

The A/B measured nothing: path_failed was nought across 568 engineer samples in
both arms, so the fault never happened and both arms ran the same code.

sm_redbots_debug_refuse_ammo_paths exists for that (v2.25.0) and has never been
run. The run to do is Rottenburg, refuse 4, failover on against off, reading
samples on a zero length path per engineer.
design:
Prior art worth reading before touching this: Source SDK 2013 carries the MvM
engineer states at
`src/game/server/tf/bot/behavior/engineer/mvm_engineer/`, and the idle state
there re-evaluates its nest on a one-to-two second cooldown rather than holding
a decision made once. mvm-6rt has the detail. Read it, never copy it: the SDK
licence needs derivatives to stay free and carry Valve's LICENSE.

Relevant here because "leaves the nest mid-wave hunting metal" is a bot whose
current action stopped being the nest. Valve's version keeps a nest hint and
re-checks that it is still valid, which is a different shape from walking off
and finding out later.

  worst cumulative path failures for an engineer  0, 0 and 14
  samples walking with a path of zero length      27 to 42 per run

So on Coal Town he never fails a path at all, and even on Rottenburg the failures

(v2.12.0, mvm-297) and the tactical monitor no longer computing a path to every

The 'walking with a path of zero length' column is the one to watch if it comes

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The wedge recovery does not cover this one, and it is worth saying why so
nobody assumes it does.

MoveWedgedDefender fires on a bot that has not moved STUCK_RADIUS in
STUCK_TIME. This engineer moves: he walks away, fails to reach the metal, gives
up and walks back. The watchdog never sees a stationary bot, so nothing here
touches it, before or after the v2.21.3 fix.

This is goal selection, not recovery. He picks a metal target without checking
that a path to it exists, and the failure mode is giving up rather than failing
over to a closer one. A reachability check before committing, or a fallback to
the next nearest source, is the shape of it.

Still not diagnosed. Nothing has reproduced it in the test-bed: the report is a
play-test and no run has been aimed at it.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Read the code. The bead's reading is half right, and the half that is wrong matters.

Refuted: the target is not picked without a path. CTFBotGetAmmo_OnStart takes its
candidates from ComputeHealthAndAmmoVectors, which sorts by straight line, runs
IsPathToVectorPossible on the nearest four, and returns only the ones that answered
yes with their travel length. The pack the engineer sets off towards was reachable
when he chose it.

Confirmed, and this is the actual hole: nothing checks it again. The choice is made
once and held for the life of the action. CTFBotGetAmmo_Update repaths to the same
entity every second through RepathToPos and throws the result away. RepathToPos does
call NotePathResult, so m_bPathFailed is correct and PathFailedFor(actor) would say
so, and no caller in getammo.sp ever asks. The action ends on three things only: the
pack going invalid, ammo full, or the monitor pre-empting it. A refused path is none
of them, so the bot keeps Update-ing a path of zero length and gets moved by
NudgeTowardsGoal at 120 units a step until the pack expires. That is the walking with
a path of zero length column from the 2026-08-25 comment, 3 to 16 per cent of engineer
samples on every run, and it is the same shape as the report: he walks, he does not
arrive, he eventually stops.

Two smaller faults found in the same function. The ranked candidates other than the
winner were discarded, so there was nothing to fail over to even if somebody noticed.
And m_iAmmoPack was never set to -1 at the top of OnStart, so on the first call of a
client's life it holds 0 and the "could not find ammo" branch cannot fire; the action
starts against entity 0 and ends one frame later in Update.

Change, behind sm_redbots_feature_ammo_failover, default 0:

- OnStart keeps the whole ranked list, up to AMMO_CANDIDATES_MAX (4, the same bound
  ComputeHealthAndAmmoVectors already path-searches), ordered by travel length, and
  clears m_iAmmoPack first.
- Update counts consecutive PathFailedFor answers. Three in a row, so about three
  seconds, moves him to the next candidate. Nothing is removed from the list on the
  way in; this only reorders what he tries, per the rank-it-last rule.
- Running out ends the action and holds CTFBotGetAmmo_IsPossible at no for three
  seconds, so the monitor does not re-enter on the next frame with the same four.

Only getammo.sp and features.sp changed. engineeridle.sp needed nothing: it picks no
metal source, it only decides whether the sentry wants some.

Not closed. The run that would settle it is a 6-wave A/B on Rottenburg with an
engineer in the lineup, because Rottenburg is the map that produced refused paths at
all (24 of 1002 samples) and Coal Town produced none, so Coal Town cannot separate the
arms. The metric is samples walking with a path of zero length, which is the number
the change is aimed at, read per engineer. Waves cleared will not separate this and
should not be used to judge it. Second number to watch is the engineer's distance from
his own sentry while fetching, median and worst: the fix should not raise it, and if
it does the failover is sending him further out than the thing it replaced.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Diagnosed, and the reading on this bead was wrong. Fixed behind
sm_redbots_feature_ammo_failover, default off, in v2.21.4.

He does not pick blind. ComputeHealthAndAmmoVectors collects up to 64 candidates
in tf_bot_ammo_search_range, sorts by straight line distance, runs
IsPathToVectorPossible on the nearest four and returns only the ones that
answered yes, with their travel length. OnStart takes the shortest. So 'picks a
metal target without checking a path exists' is refuted.

The fault is that the check happens once and is then held for the life of the
action. Update repaths to the same entity every second through RepathToPos and
throws the answer away. RepathToPos does call NotePathResult, so PathFailedFor
knows, and nothing in getammo.sp ever asks it. The action ends only on the pack
going invalid, ammo full, or pre-emption, and a refused path is none of those.
So he keeps updating a zero length path and drifts under NudgeTowardsGoal at 120
units a step until the pack expires. That is the 'walking with a path of zero
length, 3 to 16 per cent of engineer samples' already in this bead's telemetry,
and it is exactly what Jebby described: walks, never arrives, gives up.

Two smaller faults in the same function: the ranked runners up were discarded so
there was nothing to fail over to, and m_iAmmoPack was not cleared at the top of
OnStart, so on a client's first call it holds 0 and the 'could not find ammo'
branch cannot fire.

The change keeps the ranked list, bounded at four, counts consecutive
PathFailedFor answers and advances to the next candidate after three, about
three seconds. Nothing is removed from the list, only reordered, per the rank it
last rule in how-bots-break.md. Exhausting the list ends the action and holds
IsPossible at no for three seconds so the monitor does not re-enter with the
same four.

The run: 6 wave A/B on Rottenburg with an engineer, the switch as the arm.
Rottenburg is the only map that produced refused paths at all, 24 of 1002
samples, and Coal Town produced zero and cannot separate the arms. The metric is
samples walking with a path of zero length per engineer. Waves cleared will not
separate this. Guard metric: median and worst distance from his own sentry while
fetching must not rise, or the failover is sending him further than what it
replaced.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
A/B on Rottenburg advanced1, v2.23.0, three attempts each arm. The failover
never fired, so this measures nothing about it.

  ammo_failover on    271 engineer samples, 10 on a zero length path (3.7%), path_failed 0
  ammo_failover off   297 engineer samples, 11 on a zero length path (3.7%), path_failed 0

path_failed is zero in both arms. Not one refused path in 568 samples, so there
was nothing to fail over from and the two arms ran the same code. The 3.7 per
cent on a zero length path is identical either way and is something else, not
the fault this bead describes.

That is the second time today a fix has been measured against a condition that
did not reproduce. The earlier reading of 24 refused paths in 1002 samples came
from a different run, so the condition happens on Rottenburg but not reliably.

What this needs is a way to make a refused path happen on demand rather than
waiting for one. Options: a map and spot where a metal pack is known to be
unreachable, or a longer run, or a debug convar that refuses the first path to
any pack so the failover path is exercised deliberately.

Waves cleared was 0 of 6 both arms, which was expected and cannot rank them.

The v2.21.4 change stays behind its switch, default off. It fixes a real defect,
the once-validated choice held for the life of the action, but nothing has shown
it helping.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The injector for this bead is in, v2.25.0.

sm_redbots_debug_refuse_ammo_paths refuses that many path answers per walk to a
pack, counted down as they are handed out. It sits in front of PathFailedFor
rather than replacing it, so a route that really failed still reads as failed

That makes the A/B on this bead measurable. The last one showed path_failed of

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Still in progress and honestly stalled. The fix is in v2.21.4 behind

measured nothing because path_failed was zero across 568 engineer samples in

title: Rescue Ranger engineers never refill the sentry when it runs out of ammo
description:
Jebby: "idk if this is just on decoy but rescue ranger engi bots will absolutely
refuse to refill their sentry when its out of ammo"

Reported on Decoy; he was not sure whether the map matters. Rescue Ranger
specific as reported, untested against the stock shotgun.
close_reason:
Fixed and measured. A Rescue Ranger bolt repairs a building and does not reload one; only a wrench hit puts shells back. A sentry at full health with an empty magazine still answers yes to SentryNeedsMetal, so CanRepairFromRange let the engineer stand across the map firing bolts into something already whole, forever. From his point of view he was fixing it, which is why it reads as refusing.

Range repair is for damage only now. The building samples carry the magazine, which nothing counted before.

Coal Town, six waves each way with the Rescue Ranger loadout: samples of a full health sentry under fifty shells 21 of 126 before and 6 of 116 after, median magazine 104 to a full 200, five of six waves cleared either way. Not map specific as far as this shows: the mechanism is the weapon, not Decoy.

title: Engineer upgrade priority puts the PDA behind weapons and resistances
description:
EZKSupernova, who traced most of his losses to it:

"I think it should be set so the Engi fully upgrades the PDA (but not disposable
mini because that sucks) before even touching his other weapons or his
resistances. Very nearly all of my wave failures have been because the Engi
wasn't pulling his weight. I'm on Wave 6 rn and there's no building health, no
sentry firing speed, no metal capacity, all of which are mandatory upgrades."

He names three he considers mandatory and one to skip: building health, sentry
firing speed, metal capacity; not disposable mini-sentry.
design:
## Confirmed in play, and the line is found

Reported again from a nightly run of Decoy: "they always buy their mini sentry."
That is the same complaint EZKSupernova made, from a second player
independently, so the behaviour is real and repeatable rather than one bad run.

`source/redbots3/behavior/upgrade.sp`, in the `TFClass_Engineer` case, ranks:

    engy dispenser radius increased   330
    engy sentry fire rate increased   320
    engy disposable sentries          310
    engy building health bonus        260
    metal regen                       220
    maxammo metal increased           210

So the disposable mini is bought **third**, ahead of two of the three upgrades
EZK called mandatory. He asked for building health, sentry firing speed and
metal capacity, and explicitly not the mini. Sentry fire rate already outranks
it; building health and metal capacity do not.

That is the whole of "they always buy their mini sentry": at 310 it is bought
on nearly every run, before the nest is durable.

## The value is deliberate, so this is a decision and not a defect

The comment above the line explains why it is 310 rather than absent. The
upgrade was refused for a long time because nothing in the mod placed the second
building, so the game dropped it wherever the engineer faced and the result was
"minis pointing at walls". `behavior/engineerbuilddisposable.sp` now stands it
beside the real one, on ground that sees what the real one sees, and the
promotion followed that work.

The file also states the rule for changing it:

> Measured beats read. If the ordering is to change it should change because a
> run said so, not because a page did.

Two player reports are runs, not pages. But they are reports of what was bought,
not measurements of what it cost, and the credits that go into a mini are
credits that did not go into building health.

## What settles it

The testbed already does A/B runs; `testbed/results/` holds several. Run the
same missions with `engy disposable sentries` at 310 and at something under
`maxammo metal increased`, and compare waves cleared and sentry uptime. That is
the same shape of evidence that put the value at 310, so it can move it.

If the A/B is close, prefer the players. Two independent reports of the same
purchase feeling wrong is worth more than a result inside the noise, and the
mod has demoted an upgrade on that basis before.

One thing to check while there: whether the mini is worth more on a map with
several nests than on Decoy, which has three. If the answer is map-dependent the
priority may want to read the nest count rather than being one number.
close_reason: Measured and acted on. Six waves of Decoy per arm, same build, only sm_redbots_feature_engineer_disposable moved. Defender deaths per wave: off [0,3,5,7,9,10] against on [11,12,14,15,15,17], so the spreads do not touch and the worst wave without the mini beat the best wave with it. Sentries lost 7 against 14, robots killed 73 against 36.5 median, waves cleared 3 of 6 against 2 of 6. The switch now ships off, which is what EZKSupernova asked for. Caveats: one map, six waves an arm, and the arms ran under different machine load; deaths are far less load-sensitive than durations and the separation is total, but a second map is worth running. The rest of his ask, PDA before weapons and resistances, is untouched and belongs in its own bead if it is still wanted.

title: The engineer walks around holding a building and never puts it down
description:
Reported from play on Coal Town, mid wave and between waves both, and the mid
wave one costs the team its sentry for the whole wave.

The carry has no clock. `CTFBotMvMEngineerIdle_Update` only tries to place while
the engineer is within seventy units of the nest centre, so a centre he cannot
reach, or a spot whose placement keeps being refused, leaves him holding it with
nothing in the code to end it. The relocation path has a deadline of its own and
relocation ships off, so nothing else covers it.

`CARRY_GIVE_UP_TIME` is 25 seconds. When it runs out the nest becomes the ground
under his feet, which is what the relocation timeout already does, and the
placing branch below puts it down on the next update.

Not reproduced on the test-bed, and that is worth saying plainly: an engineer
only carries when a sentry buster makes him haul or when a nest moves, and
neither happened in eight waves of Coal Town with relocation on. The fix is from
reading the code against the report rather than from a measurement. The line it
writes is how the next report gets confirmed or denied:

    [defenderbots] carry failed for <name> at <time>: held it too long, putting it down here

Six waves of Coal Town with the clock in and relocation on, five cleared and no
crash, so it costs nothing where it does not fire.
close_reason: Fixed in a87d742: CARRY_GIVE_UP_TIME is 25 seconds, after which the nest becomes the ground under his feet. Not reproduced on the test-bed, so the log line it writes is how the next report is confirmed. Six waves of Coal Town with it in, five cleared, no crash.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: More evidence from the video, and it is the same root as mvm-oh7: while stuck he was scrolling through his weapons and opening and cancelling the build menu. That is two paths undoing each other every frame - the carry logic equipping the wrench and pressing fire to place, and the build gate equipping the toolbox and reopening the menu because it saw no sentry. The gates count a carried building now, which removes the trigger; the 25 second carry clock stays as the backstop.

title: The Gas Passer crashed the server
description:
A Pyro carrying a Gas Passer trips the watchdog at a wave transition:

```
WatchDog! Server took too long to process (probably infinite loop).
FATAL ERROR: Host_Error: WatchdogHandler called - server exiting.
```

Four runs in six on `mvm_decoy`, and clean six waves running with a shotgun in
that slot instead. It was four in six rather than every run because the forced
lineup has no Pyro in it: `sm_redbots_manager_extra_bots` adds one beyond the
composition and sometimes rolls Pyro.

The fault is here, not in the weapon. `EquipBestWeaponForThreat` says to throw
gas whenever `HasAmmo(secondary)` is true, and `HasAmmo` on a weapon that fires
off a charge meter rather than a clip is always true. So the Pyro equips a jar
it cannot throw, every tick, and never picks the flamethrower back up.

Fixed: `IsThrowableReady` asks the meter instead of the ammo, and the three
places in that switch which reached for `HasAmmo` on a jar now go through it.
The Gas Passer's meter is on the player, per loadout slot, because it fills from
damage dealt; Jarate, Mad Milk and the Cleaver fill on a clock the weapon
carries. Both are read.

The loadout still gives the Pyro a shotgun. Putting the Gas Passer back is a
balance question rather than a crash one now, and the file already says the
airblast it costs is worth measuring rather than assuming.

The Gas Passer is not the whole story. 1.5.5-tf2ap.10, which has no loadout file
at all, crashed twice in three runs of the same mission afterwards, with the same
watchdog line. So there is an intermittent watchdog crash in this mod that
predates all of the above, and the Gas Passer made it far more likely rather than
causing it alone. Rates seen so far, all on `mvm_decoy` with six bots:

| build | crashes |
| --- | --- |
| tf2ap.10 | 2 in 9 |
| this branch, Gas Passer | 4 in 6 |
| this branch, shotgun | 0 in 5 |

The core dumps answered it, and the answer is pathfinding. Backtrace from
core.417, taken with the game copied out of the volume:

```
WatchDogHandler <- Sys_Error <- Host_Error
 <signal handler called>
CTFBotPathCost::operator()
NavAreaBuildPath
Path::Compute
ChasePath::RefreshPath
ChasePath::Update
```

So the frame the watchdog killed was inside path computation, not an infinite
loop in this mod. Anything that asks for a path every tick, for several bots at
once, can push a frame past the watchdog on a machine with nothing spare.

One of those was ours and is fixed: `ConfiguredDispenserSpot` called
`IsPathToVectorPossible` for every configured spot, every tick, per engineer.
The spot is chosen once when the action starts now.

Worth knowing for the next one: `IsPathToVectorPossible` is a full
`NavAreaBuildPath`, and it reads like a cheap predicate.

A sweep of every map found two more of the same shape, and both are fixed:

- An engineer with no sentry answered yes to "should the nest advance", and the
  idle action returns without acting when the answer is yes. So he never
  rebuilt, and every one of those frames ran `PickBuildArea` twice, which calls
  `GetBombInfo`, which walks every nav area on the map. Sixty-six times a
  second, per engineer, for as long as he had no sentry. On Bigrock that was
  most of a wave.
- The tactical monitor asked whether health or ammo was worth walking to on
  every frame for every bot, and the slow path computed a path to every
  candidate. MvM floors are covered in `tf_ammo_pack`. The answer is held for
  half a second now and the search is run for the nearest four candidates
  rather than all of them.

The pattern is worth naming, because it has now produced four separate crashes:
a nav mesh call inside something that reads like a predicate, called from a
per-frame path. Anything asking the mesh a question wants a clock on it.

Item 10 is the fourth, and it came with a symbolised backtrace and a limit:
`PATHS_PER_FRAME` caps the whole team at two path computations a frame. That is
the general answer to this pattern rather than another special case, and the
residual intermittent watchdog crash recorded here should be measured against it
before anything else is tried.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 12 — section: Crashes and the test-bed
Original heading: The Gas Passer crashed the server. Fixed; the rest of the watchdog is still open
close_reason: The Gas Passer half was already fixed by IsThrowableReady. The residual intermittent watchdog is the path budget, mvm 8fd422e: a symbolised core put the killed frame in CNavArea::GetZ under NavAreaBuildPath with maxPathLength=0, reached from the per-frame path refresh inside PlayerRunCmd, and PATHS_PER_FRAME caps the whole team at two path computations a frame. Since it landed: 41 runs and 231 waves finished with no crash at all. The rates it is measured against are 2 crashes in 9 runs on tf2ap.10 and 4 in 6 on this branch with a Gas Passer. Reopen if one appears; a core is worth taking, see docs/how-bots-break.md.

title: The test-bed needs a machine with memory free
description:
Measurement stopped being possible partway through a session, on both builds at
once. 1.5.5-tf2ap.10 played six waves cleanly earlier the same day and then
failed four runs in a row, three of them before a single wave started, with the
watchdog line from item 12. The code did not change between those runs.

What did change is the machine:

```
7.8 GB of memory, around 200 MB free
5.0 GB swapped out
swap-in bursting to 20 MB/s while a run was playing
```

A page fault that stalls the server is indistinguishable, to a watchdog that
measures frame time, from an infinite loop. Running `--no-build` to skip the
per-run image build did not help, so it is the steady state rather than the
build spike.

Two ways out, and they are worth knowing before trusting any number this
test-bed produces: give it a machine with a couple of gigabytes free, or stop
whatever else is running on this one for the duration. What is not worth doing
is reading a crash rate measured under paging as a property of the code, which
is a mistake this file has already recorded once in item 12.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 13 — section: Crashes and the test-bed
Original heading: The test-bed needs a machine with memory free. Open
close_reason: Turned from a warning into a check: run.sh reads MemAvailable and refuses to start below 1500 MB, TESTBED_MIN_FREE_MB=0 to override. The reason is in docs/testbed-metrics.md. Verified by forcing the threshold high and watching it stop. Today's 41 runs and 231 waves ran with about 4 GB available and no crash, which is the other half of the same claim.

title: None of it is play-tested
description:
Every number in the work above is an argument. The nest range floor, the buster
distances, the crowd worth a sticky cluster, how long a Spy has to stand behind
a bot: all of them were reasoned about and none of them were measured.

`testbed/` exists for exactly this, and it works: a fake client holds a seat and
readies up, the mod spawns six bots, they shop, the wave begins, and every wave
is written down. Run a mission before the changes and the same mission after,
and read `report.py`. Do the baseline twice before believing either.

Original heading: None of it is play-tested. Open, and the test-bed can run now
