comments.author: m-this
comments.text: Still open, and the tooling it asked for now exists. Built since: a baseline band for a mission (24 attempts of Bavarian Botbash wave 1, in docs/testbed-metrics.md), per-wave quartiles printed beside every median so an arm can be judged, --wave to jump straight to the wave under test, the popfile read back so a refused mission stops the run, and wave results no longer truncated at 2047 characters. 41 runs and 231 waves went through it today. What the item actually names is still unmeasured: the nest range floor, the buster distances, the crowd worth a sticky cluster, how long a Spy has to stand behind a bot. Each is a feature switch away from an A/B now.

title: Nest relocation trips the server watchdog
description:
`sm_redbots_manager_engineer_nest_relocate` was 0 because turning it on killed
the server at the first wave transition. Reproduced again today on Decoy with two
engineers: the server crashed before a single wave finished.

This time there is a backtrace rather than a guess. The core was read with the
game's own binaries copied out of the container, which is what makes the frames
resolve:

```
WatchDogHandler <- Host_Error <- Sys_Error
 <signal handler called>
CNavArea::GetZ <- CNavArea::ComputePortal
CNavArea::ComputeAdjacentConnectionHeightChange
SMPathFollowerCost::operator()
NavAreaBuildPath (maxPathLength=0)
Path::Compute
natives::nextbot::path::ComputeToPos
 ... SourcePawn JIT frames ...
CHookManager::PlayerRunCmd
CBasePlayer::PhysicsSimulate
```

So the frame the watchdog killed was a nav mesh search, reached from this mod's
own per-frame path refresh inside `PlayerRunCmd`, with no bound on the search.
An unreachable goal makes `NavAreaBuildPath` walk the whole mesh, and six bots
asking in the same frame multiplies it. Relocation makes unreachable goals more
likely, which is why it shows there first and why the same shape has now produced
four crashes.

The fix is a limit rather than a special case. `PATHS_PER_FRAME` is 2: the
per-frame refresh computes at most two paths a frame across the whole team, and
anybody refused tries again next frame. At 66 ticks that is 130 a second against
a refresh that wants one every 0.2 seconds per bot, so nothing waits for a path.
A behaviour that computes once when it starts is never refused, because it has no
retry.

Measured:

| | result |
| --- | --- |
| relocation on, before | crashed before wave 1 finished |
| relocation on, after | 3 waves cleared, then 3 more waves, no crash, no stalls |
| relocation off, after | 2 waves cleared, 206 robots, 17 deaths, 31819 damage |
| relocation off, before | 2 waves cleared, 206 robots, 17 deaths, 32314 damage |

The last two are the regression check: the budget changes nothing about a normal
run.

The convar stays 0. The crash is what kept it off; whether the feature is worth
having is a different question and wants its own measurement.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 10 — section: Crashes and the test-bed
Original heading: Nest relocation trips the server watchdog. Fixed, and the feature is still off by default
close_reason: Closed

title: One ask adds twice
description:
`sm_addbots N` runs `AddBotsBasedOnLineupMode(N)`, which calls
`AddBotsFromTeamComposition(N)` first. That added the seats the named team still
wanted and returned a bool: true only when it filled all N. A team that does not
name every seat cannot, so the caller fell through to the lineup mode and asked
it for N again, on top of what had just been added.

`AddBotsFromTeamComposition` returns the count it added now, and the caller
subtracts it before falling back.

Three lines of telemetry made it visible, and they stay: every
`AddBotsBasedOnLineupMode` logs what it was asked for, what the named team
filled, and what the lineup mode was left to add.

Measured on the test-bed, one wave of Decoy, `BOT_TEAM_COMP` naming three
classes with `BOT_TEAM_SIZE` at six, which is what a tf2-archipelago player
produces every time a seat is left on "Let the mod pick".

| | RED at wave 1 | the log |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 10 | filled 3 of 6, the lineup mode adds 6 more |
| after | 7 | filled 3 of 6, the lineup mode adds 3 more |

RED is seven rather than six because the test-bed's own host client holds a
seat. Nine bots plus the host is what Peppy reported and what the first run
reproduced.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 18 — section: Bugs from the 1.9.0 play-test
Original heading: One ask adds twice. Fixed and measured
close_reason: Closed

title: Bot seating for specific classes
description:
Reported three times, and the 1.9.0 play-test named the mechanism. Peppy: "the
bot seats I set as 'Let the mod pick' still picks from classes that I have
unchecked in the Classes tab."

Two halves, one each side. tf2-archipelago was dropping draw seats out of
`sm_redbots_manager_team_composition`, so a team of nothing but draws wrote an
empty convar; that is its item 9 and it is fixed there.

An empty convar is what makes `GetWantedTeamComposition` fall back to the map
config's own composition, and `IsBotClassBlacklisted` returned false for every
class any composition named. That rule is right for a team somebody typed into
the console and wrong for a default this mod guessed at: a guess does not get to
overrule a class the server was told never to play. It asks the convar alone
now.

Nothing said why a bot was the class it was, so `AddDefenderTFBot` writes one
line whenever the blacklist changes its mind, naming the wanted class, the class
it settled on, and where the lineup came from.

Measured on Decoy, whose map config names `scout,soldier,demoman,heavyweapons,engineer,medic`,
with `BOT_CLASS_BLACKLIST=medic` and no convar lineup. Two waves, both cleared,
and no medic on RED in 433 bot samples:

```
Adding demoman (wanted medic), lineup from the map config
```

A team typed into the convar still beats the blacklist, which is the rule that
was kept rather than measured.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 7 — section: Bugs from the 1.9.0 play-test
Original heading: Bot seating for specific classes. Fixed and measured
close_reason: Closed

title: Bavarian Botbash wave 3 wipes the bot team
description:
Swagdoll: "Bavarian Botbash Wave 3 is still basically impossible for me. That
Giant Crit Heavy and his two Giant Medics keep wiping everything and I'm not good
enough at Sniper to counter it."

Not solved. Six attempts at the wave with nobody on the server, in two
configurations, and all six were lost. What follows is what was measured, what it
ruled out, and the two changes that survived.

**The first three sessions measured the wrong mission.** `tf_mvm_popfile
mvm_rottenburg_advanced_bavarian_botbash` was refused, the server kept playing
Rottenburg's own default, and nothing said so. The real names are in the game's
VPK and there are two: `mvm_rottenburg_advanced1` and `_advanced2`.

```
grep -ao 'mvm_rottenburg[a-z0-9_]*' tf/tf2_misc_dir.vpk
```

`run.sh` reads the popfile back now and stops with the name it is actually
playing, because everything downstream of a silent substitution is fiction.

**A second instrument was lying.** Three of four wave results in a run came out
exactly 2047 characters long: SourceMod's `File.WriteLine` formats through a 2048
byte buffer and the wave result had outgrown it. Truncated JSON is skipped by
every reader, so a four wave run looked like a one wave run. It writes with
`WriteString` now. Any measurement in this file taken on a long line before this
was measuring fewer waves than it thought.

**The uber is not being wasted.** A `uber_held` line is written whenever a
defender dies while a live medic holds a full charge. Over a whole wave 3 there
were none, so the charge is not sitting in his pocket while the team dies.

**The medic's patient churned, and fixing it changed nothing here.** He re-picked
the biggest body every two seconds, and maximum health follows the upgrades the
team buys, so the winner flipped between bodies a few points apart: 18 patient
changes in one wave. A tie keeps the man he has now, `MEDIC_PATIENT_MARGIN`, and
that is 7 changes. The beam is on somebody 27% of the time either way, so the
churn was real and was not what keeps the beam off.

**Where they wait for the wave is worth something on a hard mission and costs on
an easy one.** `MoveToFront` sends everybody to the robots' own gate. Waiting
beside the engineer's sentry instead, three attempts each on the real wave 3:

| | deaths | robots killed | held | distance to a sentry at wave start |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the gate | 22 | 36 | 135s | 823 |
| the nest | 18 | 38 | 127s | 588 |

On Decoy's own mission the same change unconditionally was worse: two waves
cleared and 206 robots killed at the gate, one wave cleared and 165 at the nest.
So the rule is the mission, `hold_the_nest`: meet them at the gate while the team
can afford to, hold the nest when it cannot. Decoy with the rule in place is back
to 206 robots and both waves cleared.

It ships **off**, because it does not clear the bar this file now holds
everything to. Read with the spread beside it, the nest arm's own quartiles are
13 to 23 deaths and they contain the gate arm's median of 22. Four waves an arm
cannot see a difference this size. The switch is there and the measurement that
would settle it is sixteen waves an arm against the baseline band below.

What is still true after all of it: the wave is lost every time, at 18 to 23
defender deaths an attempt. The bots do already shoot robot medics, 56 samples of
it in one wave, so the idea this item started with is in the mod and working.
Nobody has added a balancing knob and nobody should.

The demoknights were the next guess and they were measured too. `ThreatPriority`
ranks a medic, a support class, a giant and a bomb carrier, and a charging
demoknight is none of those: it closes seven hundred and fifty units a second, so
it is outside urgent range until it is inside melee. A `charge_first` rank above
the medic, three attempts: 18 deaths, 39 robots, 119 seconds, against 18, 38 and
127 without it. No effect, and nothing proved the rule ever fired, so it was
reverted rather than shipped as a switch nobody has evidence for.

Two more theories were measured on the real mission and both were wrong.

The engineer spends the wave failing to build. On the real wave 3 he is inside
`DefenderBuildSentrygun` for 24 samples, walking between spots three thousand
units apart, and his sentry is up for half the wave; across the container's life
17 build attempts produced 8 sentries and no give-ups. `PickBuildArea` ranks
spots against the bomb and the bomb moves up the map, and the idle action asks it
again every one to two seconds while he has no sentry.

Holding the nest for the wave instead made it worse: sentry uptime 50% to 29%,
deaths 18 to 22, and the engineer walked further rather than less. The re-picking
is finding him a spot he can actually reach, so the churn is a symptom of spots
that refuse him rather than the cause of the walking.

`IsTankWave` reading live wave icons was the other theory: the game clears icons
as a wave is beaten, so the answer can flip mid-wave, and Rottenburg keeps its
two conditional nests at opposite ends of the map. Caching it for the wave
changed nothing here because wave 3 has no tank in it at all. The reasoning still
holds for a wave that does, and it is worth doing when there is a tank wave to
measure it on.

Spacing was the sixth, and it is the first theory that fitted the deaths: they
are shelled, so standing apart should cost the robots their splash. It worked as
designed and lost anyway. Median distance to the nearest teammate went from 414
units to 564, and deaths went from 18 to 22 with the same robots killed. Spread
out, they lose the medic's beam, each other's fire and the sentry's cover, and a
robot demoman kills them one at a time instead of two at once. Reverted.

The eighth came from the build logging once it worked, and it is the closest any
of them got. Two of five build attempts end with no sentry and none of them end
on a reason the action names, so they are interruptions rather than refusals, and
the trace has the engineer walking to the upgrade station mid-wave with nothing
built. Holding him back from shopping while his nest is down: robots killed 38 to
49, and deaths 18 to 22 with sentry uptime 50% to 41%. He is present and shooting
and his sentry is the one he could not afford to upgrade, so it dies faster.
Reverted, and the trade is worth remembering: an engineer's damage is his sentry
plus himself, and this bought one with the other.

Then the reproduction itself was checked, and it was the wrong question all along.

Playing the real mission from wave 1 rather than jumping into wave 3: the bots
lose **wave 1**, eight attempts out of eight, at 15 to 31 defender deaths each.
Wave 3 is not the wall. This mission is beyond the team from its first wave, and
Swagdoll reaches wave 3 because he is on the server.

Two things were checked along the way and both corrected something believed here:

- Every bot is at stock maximum health in every run on every map, which read like
  a team that never upgrades. It is not: Mann vs Machine sells no maximum health
  upgrade at all. `sm_dump_upgrades` lists the sixty three the game has and there
  is no such line. Stock health is what a human team has too.
- They do shop. The wave line carries `upgrades` now, and a first wave of this
  mission has 28 upgrade steps bought across the team before it starts.
- `--wave` does not grant the credits of the waves it skips, so a jumped wave is
  played by an unupgraded team. That is sound for an A/B, where both arms are
  equally poor, and worthless for "can they win this wave".

Eight attempts at wave 3, eight measurements, and eight losses at wave 1 when the
mission is played properly.

The teleporter is a real defect and neither order fixes it. Over four attempts at
wave 1 there are 116 samples of an entrance standing and 33 of an exit, so most of
the metal goes on the half that moves nobody. Two fixes were measured:

| | entrance | exit | rides | held | deaths a wave |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entrance first, as shipped | 116 | 33 | 11 | 217s | 32.2 |
| replacing a lost exit mid wave | 31 | 29 | 4 | 166s | 26.5 |
| exit first | 44 | 89 | 15 | 166s | 29.5 |

The pair is complete far more often either way, and both hold the wave for less
time. The engineer finishes one half per break on this map, whichever half he
starts with, because the entrance is a walk to the far end of it. Replacing the
exit mid wave takes him off his sentry, which is the same trade that lost when he
skipped shopping to build: **anything that takes the engineer off his sentry
during a wave shortens the hold.** That is now three measurements saying it.

And a lesson about the measuring rather than the bots: four attempts cannot
resolve a difference in how long a wave is held. The unchanged arm's own
durations are 163, 189, 272 and 241 seconds. Differences of that size between
arms were read here as signal in both directions before the spread was looked at.
Only the state counts are trustworthy at this sample size: 16 attempts at wave 1
across every arm, 16 losses, and a teleporter that is one ended.

The lineup looked like the answer and then did not replicate, which is the most
useful thing measured here.

The map's lineup for Rottenburg names no Pyro, and wave 1 kills the team with
rockets: 62 per cent of the deaths are robot Soldiers and 73 per cent are
explosions. Giving the Scout's seat to a Pyro by hand, eight attempts against
eight: the team held 254 seconds against 176 and killed 88 robots against 58,
which reads as the largest effect anything produced all session.

Then the same lineup was produced by a rule instead of by hand, so that the mod
would field a Pyro whenever the coming wave is explosive, and eight more
attempts came back at 179 seconds and 54 robots. That is the baseline, not the
Pyro arm. Two of the three arms agree and the exciting one is the odd one out,
and its own durations run from 88 to 282 seconds, so it was a lucky sample read
as a discovery. The rule was reverted.

The lesson is the one this file keeps having to learn: an arm that is not
replicated is a story. Eight attempts is enough to see a wave lost sixteen times
out of sixteen and not enough to see a change in how long it is held.

Asked for from play and measured against that band: the classes that fight at
range wait at the engineer's nest and the ones that have to close wait at the
gate, rather than the whole team doing one or the other. Sixteen attempts: 166
seconds held, 25 deaths, 56 robots killed, every one of them inside the
baseline's quartiles. No detectable effect, so `hold_the_nest` stays off and the
switch stays there. It is the first change on this mission that could be called
either way with confidence rather than argued about.

Also asked for from play: a Spy for the big waves. Sixteen attempts with the
Scout's seat given to one, against the same band: 160 seconds held and 25 deaths,
both unchanged, and 44 robots killed against a baseline of 58 whose quartiles are
52 to 64. Outside the band and worse.

The Spy is the top damage dealer on the team while he is doing it, 72102 across
those waves against the Heavy's 62041, and the team still kills a quarter fewer
robots. The seat he took collects the money, and money is upgrades. A class that
does damage is not the same as a seat that is worth having.

There is a baseline band for this wave now, twenty four attempts on the
unchanged build, and it is in `docs/testbed-metrics.md`: 160 seconds held with
quartiles of 154 to 192, 24 deaths with quartiles of 22 to 31, 58 robots killed
with quartiles of 52 to 64, and none of the twenty four cleared. Every future
change to this mission is read against it, and anything whose median lands inside
those quartiles has shown nothing. That is the tool this item needed from the
start.

Money was instrumented properly and then ruled out, and the ruling out included
correcting a reading of my own.

The first version counted what the wave paid and what the team picked up, and the
field for credits spent was declared, printed and never filled. With the whole
life of it counted, dropped, picked up, bonus, spent and still in hand:

- The team collects 78 per cent of what a wave pays out, median over twelve
  waves, as little as 54 per cent of one. That is about 200 credits a wave left
  on the floor.
- It ends a wave holding a median of 3328 credits, which looked like hoarding and
  is not. Forty five shopping trips end with a median of 30 credits in the wallet
  and a range of 0 to 905: they spend what they have. The 3328 is money collected
  during the wave, and the wave is lost before the break that would spend it.
- Thirty five of those forty five trips end on "nothing left worth buying" and
  ten on the game refusing a purchase, which ends the whole trip rather than
  trying the next thing on the list. That last one is worth fixing on its own
  terms and is not worth thousands of credits.

Two changes were measured against the 78 per cent and neither moved it: letting a
bot walk to a pack within 400 units with a threat in sight, and steering the
attack sidestep onto a pack within 600. Both came back at 79 per cent, and an
early three wave read of one of them at 65 per cent was noise, which is the
third time that has happened on this mission and the reason the band exists.

What this item actually is: the bot team is below what an advanced Two Cities
mission asks from its opening wave, and no single behaviour explains it. That is
a programme rather than a bug, and the honest thing to tell the player is that
the bots need him. The measurements above rule out the medic's charge, his
patient, target priority, where the team waits, how spread out it stands, and
whether the engineer shops before building. What is left is a lot of small things
at once, which is what "the bots are not good enough yet" looks like from
inside. What is
left to try, in the order a measurement is cheapest:

- Count what actually kills them by robot class and weapon on this wave rather
  than in the aggregate. `killed us` says pyro and heavy on the wrong mission and
  has not been read for the right one.
- Sentry uptime through the wave: the engineer put 8% of his buildings' damage
  back on the wrong mission, and a nest that is down is a team fighting in the
  open whatever it decided to shoot.
- Whether the team should retreat at all. Nothing in this mod ever gives ground,
  and a wave that walks over a held line is the one case where falling back to
  the next choke is what a person does.
notes:

title: One engineer builds two dispensers, reproduced on the testbed
description:
Peppy: "Engineer bots can sometimes build 2 dispensers."

The per-owner building samples walk `TF2Util_GetPlayerObject`, which is the
game's own list and holds one entry per type, so a second dispenser on one
builder is exactly what that list cannot show. A second instrument walks the
entities instead and counts them against `m_hBuilder`.

First run, four waves: two engineers each held two dispensers, for three samples
each. Second run, with entities that are being placed or carried excluded: none
at all, over four waves.

So no engineer ever holds two built dispensers. What he holds is the blueprint,
which is a real `obj_dispenser` with his name on it, while his own dispenser
stands at the nest. That is what a person watching sees as a second one, and it
is why the report says "sometimes".

Both are written down now: a `duplicate` line if a builder ever holds two of a
type, and a `ghost` line for each blueprint or carried building. A three wave run
had eight ghost samples on one engineer, dispenser and sentry, so a blueprint can
be out for the length of a walk across the map.

That is the honest end of this item unless somebody sends a screenshot of two
dispensers standing. If it turns out to be the blueprint that bothers people, the
fix is the engineer cancelling the placement when he stops walking to a spot, and
the `ghost` lines are what would measure it.
design:
## Cause found, and the other candidate is measured out

`listed` answered it. Four waves of Decoy: `held:2 built:2 listed:2`, eighteen
times. `listed` is the count from `TF2Util_GetPlayerObject`, the list every gate
in this mod asks. It agreeing at 2 means the gates could see both buildings, so
nothing was blind and the fix does not belong in `GetObjectOfType`. That branch
is closed.

The real cause is a one-frame race in
`source/redbots3/behavior/engineerbuilddispenser.sp`:

    VS_PressFireButton(actor);                                  // acts next tick
    int dispenser = GetObjectOfType(actor, TFObject_Dispenser);  // asked now
    if (dispenser == INVALID_ENT_REFERENCE)
        return action.Continue();                                // so it presses again

The press puts the building down on the tick after it, so a question asked in
the same frame is always answered "none". The action carried on, the toolbox
re-armed, and it pressed again. Two dispensers, one engineer.

The same trap as `m_bInUpgradeZone` in the refund probe, where the trigger only
sets the property on the next tick.

## Fixed

The check runs before the press and ends the action as soon as a dispenser
exists, so a re-armed toolbox cannot produce a second. A press is also given a
tick to land before another is allowed.

`engineerbuildsentrygun.sp` has the same shape and got the same guard. That one
is **recognised, not measured**: a sentry standing twice under one engineer is
what was reported as three sentries for two engineers, but no run has counted
it.

## Left open until the verification run says zero

Before: 18 duplicates over four waves. After should be none. Not tagged until
that comes back, because a fix for a race deserves the same bar as a weight
change.

One thing still unexplained and worth writing down: TF2 normally allows one
dispenser per engineer. Two standing, finished, with the game's own list
agreeing, means something on the MvM side permitted it. The fix holds whatever
that is, because it stops the second press rather than relying on the game to
refuse, but nobody knows why the game said yes.

Imported from TODO.md item 16 — section: Bugs from the 1.9.0 play-test

close_reason: Fixed and verified on the testbed. Cause was a one-frame race in engineerbuilddispenser.sp: VS_PressFireButton puts the building down on the next tick, and GetObjectOfType was asked in the same frame, so the answer was always none, the action continued, the toolbox re-armed and it pressed again. The check now runs before the press and ends the action as soon as a dispenser exists, and a press gets a tick to land before another is allowed. Four waves of Decoy: 18 duplicate events before, 0 after, with 138 dispensers and 138 sentries still sampled so the engineers build normally. listed:2 in the before-run ruled out the other candidate: the game's object list saw both, so no gate was blind and the fix did not belong in GetObjectOfType. engineerbuildsentrygun.sp has the same shape and got the same guard, recognised rather than measured. Still unexplained: TF2 normally allows one dispenser per engineer, and why the game permitted a second is unknown; the fix stops the press rather than relying on the game to refuse.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: Cowser, mid-wave: "it was trying to place a dispenser but just couldn't and gave up for some reason". omaewh4 confirmed: "ahh and you were mid-wave? that happened to me too, but on the start of the wave he just put it normally". Start-of-wave places fine, mid-wave gives up — the same blueprint-not-a-building shape this bead already describes, with a trigger attached.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: Original report, Peppy on 1.9.0 release day: "Engineer bots can sometimes build 2 dispensers".

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Reopened: my close was wrong. A photograph from play shows two dispensers standing with one engineer who was never kicked or replaced, and my measurement could not have seen it - every run I checked had the engineer never carrying a building, and the world scan excludes anything being placed or carried.

The mechanism is the carry. TF2 removes a building from the player's object list the moment he picks it up, so GetObjectOfType(engineer, dispenser) answers none while he holds one; the gate in CTFBotMvMEngineerIdle_Update then says 'no dispenser, build one', he places a fresh one, and when the carried one goes down there are two.

Ruled out by test rather than argument: kicking an engineer holding a level three dispenser removed the dispenser and left no orphan, so it is not ownership loss.

Fixed by HasObjectOfType, which counts the carried one, used by the dispenser gate and the teleporter's sentry and dispenser checks. Six waves of Coal Town with relocation on: five cleared, no crash, never more than one dispenser at once. It shares a root with the carry having no clock, which is closed separately.

title: Sniper bots on the stock loadout stand in spawn
description:
Peppy, and he said it predates 1.9.0: "Sniper bots with the stock loadout don't
seem to work, they just stay in spawn."

A sniper had never been in a test-bed lineup: 3417 engineer samples in
`results/` and not one sniper, which is why this survived. Forced into one on
Decoy, on the build with item 17 fixed, he works: `SniperLurk` under his stack
for the whole mission, 1970 damage and 14 kills over three waves.

That is the answer. A rifle sniper is one of the classes `ShouldTakeUpPosition`
refuses, so with item 17's stale shopping flag he had no behaviour for the whole
break and stood where he spawned. The same freeze as the engineers, and fixed
with them.

The rest of this item is a fix that was written, measured and thrown away, and
it is worth keeping because the reasoning was sound and the measurement said no.

`SetupSniperSpotHints` takes the team off every `func_tfbot_hint` when the map
config names no `SniperSpot`, and the game's sniping behaviour walks to a hint of
its own team. So on an unconfigured map a rifle sniper looked like he would have
nowhere to go, and the fix was to let him fight instead. Decoy with its
`SniperSpot` block removed, two waves each way:

| | damage | kills | standing still |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lurking, as shipped | 4521 | 35 | 24 of 63 samples |
| falling back to attacking | 570 | 7 | 11 of 82 samples |

The premise was wrong. The game's lurk finds its own spot without a hint, and a
sniper on his rifle is worth eight times a sniper walking around shooting at
things. The change was reverted. What it did prove is that standing still is what
a sniper is supposed to do, so "he is not moving" is not evidence of a broken
sniper, and the next report of one wants damage per wave beside it.

Forced into a Decoy lineup afterwards he works: SniperLurk under his stack, 1970 damage and 14 kills over three waves. A fallback that made him fight without a hint was measured and thrown away, 4521 damage lurking against 570 attacking.

comments.text: Peppy, reporting it: "Sniper bots with the stock loadout dont seem to work, they just stay in spawn", and then "this was already the case in the previous version btw, just for the record" — so it is not a 1.9.0 regression.

title: The medic had nothing to do between waves
description:
Left behind by item 17. With the shopping flag fixed the medic still spent three
quarters of the break with no behaviour on his stack.

`ShouldTakeUpPosition` refused four classes, on the reasoning that each has
somewhere else to be: the engineer has his nest, the spy is lurking, the sniper
with a rifle has his spot, and the medic follows a patient. The first three hold.
The medic does not: between rounds he heals nobody, so nothing suspends for him,
and following a patient is not a behaviour he has when there is no healing to do.
His patient is walking to the front, so that is where he goes now.

Measured on the same mission as item 17, two waves, both cleared either way:

| | medic, no behaviour in the break | healing done | defenders died | damage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 76% | 876 | 18 | 30922 |
| after | 0% | 1560 | 17 | 32314 |

Every bot on the team is now at 0%. Two waves is too small to call the healing a
win; it is enough to say nothing regressed.

title: On the final wave the bots neither dance nor leave
description:
Found while reading tf2_defenderbots.sp for the port.

RemoveAllDefenderBots takes bDanceInstead, and events.sp passes IsFinalWave()
for it on wave complete: the intent is that the team celebrates rather than
being kicked out from under the players on the last wave of a mission.

What it does instead:

  void MakePlayerDance(int client)
  {
      if (IsPlayerAlive(client))
      {
          //TODO: tauntem
      }
  }

The branch is taken, the continue skips the kick, and nothing happens. So on the
final wave the bots stay, standing still, and are not removed either. Neither
half of the intent happens.

Two ways to make it true, and the choice is a judgement about what the moment
should look like:

  Make it dance. TF2_AddCondition with TFCond_Taunting, or a FakeClientCommand
  of taunt, on whoever is alive. Note the readiness code already fights taunts
  between rounds, so this wants to be after the wave rather than before one.

  Drop it. Delete the parameter and the branch, kick on the final wave like any
  other. Smaller, and honest about what the mod does today.

Carried across unchanged when tf2_defenderbots.sp is ported: a port does not
fix. See mvm-z83.41.

## Done when

Either the bots visibly do something on the final wave, or the parameter is
gone and the file no longer promises they will.

title: The subset has no conditional compilation, and two event handlers need it
description:
Found while porting events.sp.

Event_MvmWaveComplete and Event_PlayerTeam both hold a #if defined block:
MOD_REQUEST_CREDITS in the first, CHANGETEAM_RESTRICTIONS in the second. The Go
subset has nothing for it, and porting either one as written would compile the
block in unconditionally, which is a behaviour change under a build flag rather
than a port.

Three ways out, in the order they are worth considering.

  A build flag is a feature switch that happens to be decided early. The mod
  already has a feature table in internal/tables, and a switch read at runtime
  is one fewer thing that varies between two builds nobody can tell apart. This
  is the honest fix and it is not a port: it needs its own bead and its own
  measurement.

  //sp:when FLAG on a body, emitting the #if around it. Faithful, cheap, and it
  puts a preprocessor into the generator, which is a thing to be sure about
  before doing.

  Leave both handlers in the plugin for good. They are 40 lines together.

Nothing is blocked on this: the rest of events.sp ported around them.

## Done when

Both handlers are either generated or deliberately left, with the reason written
in the file rather than in this bead.

title: A run's attempts play later waves, not the same ones again
description:
cmd/testbed loads the mission for each attempt but the wave counter carries forward: attempt 1 plays waves 1-2, attempt 2 plays 3-4, attempt 3 plays 5-6. The run report adds them up as 'N waves, M cleared', which reads as a pass rate and is not one.

Measured on three runs of the same shape: every one clears 2/2 on attempt 1 and 1/2 afterwards, because Decoy's later waves are harder. Two builds compared by that number are being compared on different waves.

What it costs: a wave lost to a hard wave five reads the same as a wave lost to a regression, which is how a port defect and a mission got confused for a whole session.

Wanted: the report says which waves were played and what happened to each, and the arm comparison stays the only thing read as a build difference.

title: Upgrade shopping list without the JSON handles
description:
What is left of behavior/upgrade.sp is the shopping trip: CollectUpgrades, the sort, ChooseUpgrade and PurchaseUpgrade. The ranking is a table now (internal/upgrade) and the two loadout questions are generated (internal/body/upgraderules).

The obstacle to porting the rest is the data structure rather than the generator. A candidate upgrade is a JSONObject holding four ints (pclass, slot, index, priority), allocated per candidate, pushed into a JSONArray, and read back by allocating another handle per read. CollectUpgrades ends in a sort that used to allocate two handles per comparison, and its own comment records twenty thousand handles per bot for a list of a hundred and fifty.

That is a row of a table wearing a handle. The port should carry it as an ArrayList of four-cell blocks, which is what internal/action/getammo already does for the ammo candidates: one allocation for the list, none per row, and the same SortCustom over the same cells. No JSON, no per-entry handle, and the order is unchanged because the priority and the random tiebreak are the same numbers in the same comparator.

Proof: the ranking is already compared against the shipped scores by internal/upgrade/upstream_test.go. What the shopping trip needs on top is a test-bed run comparing credits left unspent and what each class bought, against the same mission on the current build.

title: Generator: writing into a caller's buffer
description:
EngineerTeleporter_LastResult stayed hand-written in source/redbots3/teleporter_result.sp when the teleporter behaviour was ported.

A generated function fills a buffer with strcopy(dest, sizeof dest, from), reading the length off its own declaration. This one takes (char[] buffer, int maxlength) from its caller, and a generated body has no way to name that length, so writing 512 into a caller's 64 would overrun it.

Closing this deletes teleporter_result.sp.
close_reason: //sp:length names the parameter that carries a buffer parameter's length, so a generated function fills the caller's size. teleporter_result.sp and nest_dump.sp are both deleted: EngineerTeleporter_LastResult and Command_DumpNest are generated now.

title: Generator: string tables and function values
description:
ComputeHealthAndAmmoVectors and SortByStraightLineRange stayed hand-written in source/redbots3/healthammo_search.sp when getammo was ported.

Two constructs missing from the Go subset:
- a table of string literals walked by index, which SourcePawn writes char x[][] and FindEntityByClassname reads
- a function passed as a value, which ArrayList.SortCustom takes

Closing this deletes healthammo_search.sp and moves both into internal/action/getammo.
close_reason: Both closed. ArrayList.SortCustom takes the comparison by name, which the emitter already wrote correctly, so what was missing was the extern and a Handle tag; a package-level [N]string now emits as char x[][]. internal/action/getammo generates ComputeHealthAndAmmoVectors and SortByStraightLineRange, and healthammo_search.sp is deleted.

title: tf2-archipelago pins the mod by hand, and should pin it with go.mod
description:
Half done, sooner than expected.

tf2-archipelago pins github.com/m-this/tf2-mvm-bots-go with a tool directive in go.mod, at v0.2.0, and deploy/bots/build.sh runs the generator from it: the mod's committed generated SourcePawn is regenerated and compared, so editing one of those files in the mod's tree fails the build. go.mod and go.sum are in the bots cache key, so a bump of the pin rebuilds rather than restoring a tree the old generator wrote.

What is not done is the rest of it. DEFENDERBOTS_VERSION still names a tag of tf2-mvm-bots, because that repository still holds 27004 lines of hand written SourcePawn. It goes when the rewrite does, and then the mod is the module and there is one pin instead of two.

## Done when

DEFENDERBOTS_VERSION is gone from versions.env and the bots build produces the mod's plugins from the pinned module alone.

title: The test-bed writes its results into the plugin repository
description:
cmd/testbed resolves the plugin repository through internal/upstream and writes runs into <plugin>/results, because that is where the existing runs are and internal/runmap reads them there.

Results are output, not source, and the repository that owns the code should own them. Moving them is a rename plus a path, and the reason to wait is that the existing runs are the baseline several open beads compare against.

## Done when

A run writes into this repository, internal/runmap reads them from here, and the existing results are either moved with them or explicitly left behind as history.

title: A body cannot compare strings, so IsSentryBusterRobot stays an extern
description:
The subset takes a string literal as a call argument and nothing else, which was enough for FindEntityByClassname. It is not enough for util.sp:549, IsSentryBusterRobot, which reads GetClientModel into a buffer and compares it with StrEqual.

That shape is a char buffer, a length, and a comparison, and the subset has none of the three. It is worth deciding once whether it gets them or whether every such site becomes an extern, because the plugin has many: loadouts.sp dispatches on two levels of string, menu.sp builds its items from them.

## Done when

Either a body can declare a char buffer and compare it, or there is a written rule saying string work stays behind an extern, and SUBSET.md says which.

title: A body cannot call a methodmap, so the vector helpers stay externs
description:
internal/body/scan ported the nine util.sp scans and, since //sp:returns, the two vector helpers with them: WorldSpaceCenter (util.sp:348) and GetAbsOrigin (util.sp:542) are bodies over stocklib's BaseEntity_ forms, and no longer need a methodmap at all.

What still does is everything else that reaches the engine through CBaseEntity(entity).Something(). gosubset refuses a method call and tells the author to write a plain function with the value first, which is right for a body's own code and wrong for SourceMod's API: CBaseEntity is a methodmap the includes declare and there is no plain function behind it.

The bindings already generate Go methods for every methodmap, so the names exist. What does not exist is calling one from a body and emitting the receiver form.

Lower priority than it was: the two functions that made it urgent are across, and every remaining site has a stocklib plain function beside it so far.

## Done when

A body calls a methodmap method on a value from the extern package and the emitted SourcePawn is the receiver form.

title: A comment in a Go body does not reach the SourcePawn it becomes
description:
internal/spbody drops comments. The port of GetNearestEnemyCount lost //Usually not a threat, which is the one line in that loop saying why a sentry buster is skipped.

A reviewer reads the generated SourcePawn beside the plugin it replaces, and a decision with its reason removed reads as arbitrary. The comments are in the AST already, since parseDir keeps them.

## Done when

A comment on a statement or a declaration in a body appears in the generated file at the same place, and the shapes golden shows one.

title: The three test-bed plugins are hand-written SourcePawn nobody has claimed
description:
testbed/stats/mvmbots_stats.sp is 2200 lines, and mvmbots_host.sp and
mvmbots_refund.sp sit beside it. They run inside the server, so they are SourcePawn,
which under the old aim meant they were somebody else's problem and under this one
means they are generated like everything else.

They are a good early target and a bad late one. Good because the statistics plugin is
mostly reading entity properties and formatting JSON, which is the shape a generator
handles first, and because its fields already have a Go counterpart: internal/tables
generates the wave record for both sides. Bad if left until last, because every
measurement the epic depends on comes out of this file, and rewriting the instrument
while using it to judge the rewrite is not a position to be in.

The break instrumentation added on 2026-08-29 is the newest part and the least settled,
so it is the piece most likely to move again before it is worth generating.

## Done when

The three plugins are authored here and the plugin repository holds no SourcePawn that
was written by hand for the test-bed.

title: A scripted player, so a bug that needs a human can be reproduced without one
description:
Several faults on the board need a person on RED and cannot be measured by the
test-bed, which plays with nobody on it: mvm-w9b needs somebody to press the medic
call, mvm-yu8 needs somebody to drive the Bot Switcher, and apw-z7o in the other
repository needs somebody at an upgrade station.

## What it is

A puppet: a fake client the test-bed drives, standing where a player stands.
OnPlayerRunCmd gives buttons, view angles and movement per tick, so firing, walking
and weapon switching are fields rather than plumbing; TeleportEntity places it; chat
is a say command.

Authored in Go and generated, under this epic, which means it has to fit the gosubset
checker and probably needs the OnPlayerRunCmd hook binding first. That ordering is the
work, not the puppet itself.

## What it is worth and what it is not

It turns "needs a play-test" into "needs a script" for anything that is about what a
player does. It does not turn it into a measurement of what a player feels: input
timing, interp and packet loss are not reproduced, so "the medic feels unresponsive"
stays a play-test question.

The reason to want it is narrower and real: a bot medic ignoring a call is a fact
about the ranking, and a puppet pressing the call proves it either way in a run
instead of waiting for somebody to be free.

## Done when

A test-bed run can seat a puppet on RED, have it press the medic call, and the results
file shows whether the beam moved.

title: The repath interval PATHS_PER_FRAME is sized against is an unnamed literal
description:
nextbot_behavior.sp:703 writes the successful-repath delay as a bare 0.2 inside an expression, beside PATH_RETRY_INTERVAL which is a #define at 0.5. The comment above PATHS_PER_FRAME reasons about 'the 0.2 second refresh below', so the budget is sized against a number that has no name to be sized against.

internal/tables has the relation now, PATHS_PER_FRAME * 66 >= 6 / 0.2, but it carries the 0.2 as a Go constant because there is nothing in the plugin to read. A future edit to the literal moves the relation without touching anything the proof looks at.

Give it a name beside PATH_RETRY_INTERVAL and let the table read it out of the plugin like the others. Held out of the port work because it is a change to the plugin, which is mvm-z83.41.

title: spgen checks the edge against HEAD, not against a pin
description:
internal/spgen/upstream_test.go sets upstreamRev to HEAD while its own doc comment gives the reason not to: a proof that fails because somebody saved a file in ../tf2-mvm-bots is a proof people learn to ignore. That is mvm-z83.37, fixed in internal/tables with a pinned rev at a0f9490 and a TestPinIsNotBehindHEAD that logs drift instead of failing.

TestEveryShippedCallSiteIsInTheEdge reads GetDesiredBotAction through git show, so it is one constant away from the same protection. Pin it, and add the same drift log.
notes:
Done, and wider than filed. The pin is now one fact in internal/upstream, not one constant per test package: Rev, Dir, Read and Head, with the reasoning in the package comment. internal/tables and internal/spgen both read through it, so the duplication the spgen comment apologised for is gone. A missing plugin repository is a skip that names MVMBOTS_UPSTREAM; a missing file at the pin is a failure, and functionBody now fails rather than skipping when GetDesiredBotAction is not in the pinned revision.

Moving the pin from a0f9490 to b48ad70 caught real drift, which is the point of moving it deliberately:

The plugin gained medic_answers_call (mvm-w9b) and the Go table did not have it in the same place. engineer_entrance_first (mvm-dh8) sat in the table ahead of the plugin and in the middle of the enum, which is exactly the bug the table exists to prevent, waiting for the plugin to adopt it. The feature is now appended after every shipped one, and TestFeatureTableRoundTrips fails on an ahead feature that sits before a shipped one rather than tolerating it by count.

TestFeatureProofCatchesASwappedName no longer names the neighbouring feature to disambiguate its mutation, so appending a feature does not break it.
close_reason: Closed

title: The generated edge is compiled by one compiler only
description:
TestGeneratedEdgeCompiles compiles gen/sourcepawn/actionsel_dispatch.sp with the standalone 1.13 spcomp. The table is checked under both compilers by mvm-z83.13, the edge is not, and the edge is the file that calls into the plugin.

The obstacle is the smoke harness, not the generated code. testdata/dispatch_smoke.sp declares Action, Plugin_Continue, Plugin_Handled, MAXPLAYERS and ConVar so the standalone compiler has them, and SourceMod's spcomp64 implicitly includes sourcemod.inc which already does: 4 errors, none of them about the generated file.

Put the stubs behind a defined() guard, or give the harness a second entry point that includes sourcemod, and add spcomp64 to that test the way mvm-z83.13 added it to the sweep.
notes:
Done. The smoke harness no longer declares the symbols SourceMod declares. They move to a smoke_env include the test writes: stubs for the standalone compiler, and #include <sourcemod>, <sdktools>, <tf2_stocks> for the compiler the plugin ships with. tf2_stocks rather than tf2, because TF2_GetPlayerClass is a stock there and the edge calls it.

TestTheGeneratedEdgeCompilesUnderBothCompilers compiles gen/sourcepawn/actionsel_dispatch.sp with spcomp64. The four collisions in the description are gone: Action, Plugin_Continue, Plugin_Handled, MAXPLAYERS and ConVar all come from one side or the other and never both.

The edge cannot run, so compiling is the check, and Run would have run it: spshell.Compile stops after spcomp. Without it the SourceMod-compiled edge died on Native is not bound, which is mvm-z83.13's float operator gap showing up again.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] A failed precondition on the last attempt throws away the whole run
description:
The noise floor run played 5 of 6 attempts, then the sixth failed with RED reached 0 defenders and not 6, and the runner exited non-zero having reported nothing.

The five completed attempts were written to results and are perfectly good data. Nothing said so. The run reads as a failure, and only looking in the directory shows five files worth keeping.

The refusal is right, mvm-81n built it on purpose, and a run that cannot meet its preconditions must not be believed. But refusing to report what already succeeded is a different decision, and it wastes about forty minutes of server time per occurrence.

Report what completed, say plainly which attempts are missing and why, and exit non-zero. The caller can then decide whether four attempts of six is enough for what it was asking.

title: ActionHandlerSigN names are positional and renumber on an insert
description:
internal/bindings emits one named func type per typeset signature as Sig1 to Sig29. Inserting a signature into a typeset upstream renumbers everything after it, which is the same shape as the features.sp bug this epic opened with: position carrying meaning that a name should carry.

The doc comments already carry the callback names, OnStart, OnSuspend, Update and so on. Derive stable names from those. The agent judged it too fragile to do blind and it needs the real comment shapes read first.
notes:
Done, and the comment shapes did not hold up the way the bead assumed. Read across all 280 variants: only 146 have a comment at all, and many of those are prose the parser would have taken for a name ("@return True to allow the current entity to be hit", "resumes normal functionality."). A name derived from comments alone would have been wrong more often than right.

Two sources instead, in internal/bindings/typeset_name.go:

A comment that is only a comma-separated list of identifiers gives the name, first entry wins: ActionHandlerOnUpdate, InputFuncCallbackVector, ActionHandlerInitialContainedAction. 96 of 278 land here, and they are the actions headers, which is where the callbacks people write live.

Everything else is tagged with four hex digits of its own rendered signature: ActionEventResponderCallbackSig7a3c. It moves only when that signature's types move. A doc name two variants share is not used by either, because letting the first win would put position back into the name through the side door.

TestInsertingASignatureRenamesNothingElse is the proof: insert a signature in the middle and every other name is still there.

Found on the way: two typesets declare the same signature twice, NativeCall with (Handle, int) returning int and InputFuncCallback with the CBaseEntity-and-int shape. One signature is one Go type, so the repeat is dropped rather than emitted twice or refused, and the refusal count is unchanged at 107.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nine copies of one client scan loop, and mvm-ds3 lives in all of them
description:
util.sp 1183-1690. Nine variants of the same scan over client slots, which is where the duplication and the bug meet: every one loops player slots, and tank_boss occupies none, which is mvm-ds3.

All nine are across, in internal/body/scan, plus IsPlayerSappable and IsPlayerHealingSomething. Each is pinned by the differential test, which compares the answer and the sequence of engine calls against the Go it was ported from.

The three sappable scans shared a run of seven questions in the same order, and that run is one function already: it changes no call order and the trace proves it.

What is left is the collapse that does change call order: one scan taking a predicate, which fixes mvm-ds3 once instead of nine times and is a precondition for the threat record shape in mvm-z83.14 and mvm-z83.6. It waits until the plugin calls the generated scans rather than its own, which is mvm-z83.16.

The rest of the 1000 lines parity.md counts as deletable: menu.sp 153-502, loadouts.sp two level string dispatch, three copies of the same m_ct*Ask memo cache, and a duplicated build ring where the copy is missing the press settle fix.

title: [bug] Rottenburg SniperSpot 4 is 213 units from any nav surface
description:
Found offline by mvm-z83.27. mvm_rottenburg.cfg SniperSpot 4 is "2238 122 -146", verified against the file, and the nearest nav surface anywhere is 213 units away.

No bot can reach it and all 8 stand sides are refused. It has been shipping as a sniper spot that silently does nothing, which is the same shape as mvm-tz9 where Decoy shipped with zero sniper spots for releases.

Same fix as the seven in the sibling bead: correct the coordinate, and let the build refuse a spot with no ground under it.

title: The subset checker collects names per file, so a package cannot be split
description:
checker.collect runs per file, so a package split across two files false-refuses every cross-file type and function as unknown.

Found while writing mvm-z83.22, and it forced the domain and both selection functions into one 358 line file. That is over the repository's own reading limit and it is the checker's fault, not the code's.

Collect package level names across the directory before checking any file.
close_reason:
CheckFiles collects package level types and functions from every file before checking any file. CheckDir parses the directory and calls it once; CheckFile is CheckFiles over one file, so single file use is unchanged.

Measured on the actionsel split as a fixture: per file, domain.go 0 refusals, select.go 12, shipped.go 12. Twenty four false refusals. CheckDir over the same three files: 0.

The two tests that matter are the ones guarding against a rubber stamp. TestUnknownNamesAcrossFiles is table driven over a two file package where the second file reaches for a name no file declares, ten cases, all refused. TestSingleFileCannotSeeThePackage pins the single file gap in place so it stays observable rather than becoming a surprise.

One bug found on the way: an import name is file scoped in Go, and carrying imports forward would have accepted a selector the next file never imported. beginFile resets them, and TestImportsDoNotLeakBetweenFiles asserts the refusal lands in the file that did not import.

Verified here: 82 tests, go build clean, golangci-lint 0 issues.

title: Native bindings carry preconditions and cost
description:
Three closed bugs are pure native semantics: mvm-bj8, mvm-0l5 and mvm-ijg. The bindings generated in mvm-z83.10 know the signature and nothing about what a call costs or what must be true before it.

Add a semantics layer to the generated bindings and lint the call sites against it. The first annotation to write is that IsPathToVectorPossible is a full NavAreaBuildPath, which mvm-0l5 says produced four crashes.

A signature that does not say a call is a full path build is a signature that reads as free.

title: Fault injectors are table rows and the run records which arm it played
description:
The cheapest of the additions. mvm-0lo lists five hand written injectors. mvm-zx0 is open only because its injector was never armed. mvm-81n lists results carry no record of the arm as still open.

One table row per injector, generated into both sides, and the arm written into the run record. Squarely inside internal/tables and it closes a gap in three beads.

title: Cross-file constants carry their relations
description:
mvm-1pq was TELEPORTER_EXIT_RADIUS at 150 against BUSTER_BLAST_RANGE at 400: the exit is built inside the blast that kills the sentry. Neither constant is wrong alone. The relation between them is what was wrong, and it was written nowhere.

Same generator as mvm-z83.2, applied to the constants, with the relations asserted. Also CARRY_GIVE_UP_TIME from mvm-1b7 and PATHS_PER_FRAME from mvm-297.

A constant with no stated relation to the constant it must respect is two facts written down once each and never compared.
notes:
Done as a checked relation table rather than as a generator.

internal/tables/constant.go declares the six constants a relation names, with where each lives in the plugin and what its number counts. internal/tables/relation.go declares the four relations, each with the statement in the plugin's own names, the bug behind it, and the predicate the compiler can run.

TestRelationsHoldInThePinnedPlugin reads every #define out of the pinned plugin and evaluates the relations against the values the plugin actually has:

TELEPORTER_EXIT_RADIUS_SAFE >= BUSTER_BLAST_RANGE, which is mvm-1pq.
TELEPORTER_EXIT_RADIUS < BUSTER_BLAST_RANGE, mvm-1pq from the other side: the tight ring is meant to be inside the blast, and raising it to look safe would take the fallback away from maps with no room at 500.
CARRY_GIVE_UP_TIME > NEST_RELOCATE_HAUL_TIME, mvm-1b7: if the outer clock fires first the relocation never gets its own timeout.
PATHS_PER_FRAME * 66 >= 6 / 0.2, mvm-297: the budget must still cover what the team asks for, or the fix for the stall becomes a stall of its own.

TestRelationProofCatchesABrokenRelation is the proof about the proof: each relation is re-run with its first constant scaled across six orders of magnitude and has to fail somewhere, so a relation that constrains nothing is caught. TestEveryRelationNamesConstantsInTheTable refuses a constant with no relation, because the plugin's own comment is a better home for it than a second copy in Go.

Not emitted, deliberately. These live in three plugin files with the reasoning written above each one, and moving them here would trade a comprehension win for churn mvm-z83.16 has not paid for yet.

The value parser takes a number or a name plus a number, which is the form TELEPORTER_EXIT_RADIUS_SAFE already uses, and fails on anything else rather than skipping it.

Filed on the way: mvm-z83.45, the 0.2 second repath PATHS_PER_FRAME is sized against is an unnamed literal at nextbot_behavior.sp:703, so the relation carries it as a Go constant with nothing in the plugin to read.
close_reason: Closed

title: Emitted files reference types their siblings declare
description:
Emission is per file, so tf2utils needs TFCond, TFClassType and Address from elsewhere and does not compile alone. The bindings package enumerates those edges in a test and stops there, correctly: resolving them is a driver's job.

cmd/gen is the driver. It decides whether the output is one package or many, and it threads each file's resolved constants into the next, which is already known to drop define refusals from 69 to 22.

Until this is done the emitted Go type checks only under a test harness, not as a package anyone imports.
close_reason:
internal/bindgen. One package, not many: SourcePawn's include graph has cycles between core.inc, handles.inc and functions.inc, and Go forbids import cycles, so one package is the only shape that survives. It costs nothing because a binding has no body.

Emission order is the real #include graph topologically sorted, with ties and cycles broken in path order and pinned by a test. Options gained Names alongside Constants so the claimed identifier set threads file to file; without it two includes declaring EF_BONEMERGE produce a package that does not compile.

The proof is a build, not a harness. TestGeneratedPackageBuilds writes 205 files and a go.mod to a temp dir and runs go build with no hand edits. Define refusals landed at 22, matching this bead's prediction.

Two collateral fixes the build forced. The emitted receiver is now this, because nav.inc has a method whose parameter is x and collided with the old receiver. Trailing variadics are rendered rather than refused, because Go can express them and refusing them was wrong; that alone took refusals from 177 to 107.

One generated file holds tags no include declares, and the list is one name, Function. A test caps it at twelve, because anything longer would mean a refusal upstream reappearing as an invented type.

The parity edge is zero. Unbound compares 1085 free call sites and 188 member uses against what the package declares: no unbound natives and no unbound methodmap members. Getting there needed a Code helper that blanks comments and string literals first, because the plugin passes VScript as strings and keeps commented-out prototypes beside the code, which were producing six phantom missing natives.

Limits recorded: Unbound is a name comparison and not a type check, so zero is a floor on the hand written remainder rather than proof of correctness. go build proves the package compiles and not that a binding is right; every body panics and signature fidelity rests on four golden files.

title: Randomness comes in as a parameter or it cannot be compared
description:
UnrankedUpgradePriority calls GetRandomInt, and PickBuildArea's tier assignment uses GetRandomFloat(0.8, 1.75).

A generated function that draws its own random number cannot be compared against the Go it came from, because the two sides draw different numbers. The differential test has nothing to assert.

Randomness enters as a parameter, or as a native binding the harness can pin. Decide which before any decision function that rolls dice moves across.

title: Attribute names become ids before the upgrade order can move to Go
description:
Found by the subset checker against the real code, and it is the one construct that genuinely does not fit.

GeneralUpgradePriority and ClassUpgradePriority, behavior/upgrade.sp:700 and :903, are chains of roughly forty StrEqual(attribute, "damage bonus") tests. The subset has no strings, so this does not translate as written.

It translates after a change the design already wants: the attribute name becomes an int32 identifier assigned by an attribute table in internal/tables, the SourcePawn edge does the name to id lookup once, and the Go body is a switch over the int32. Better than what is there today, because the name table stops being forty string literals duplicated between the priority function and the schema.

A prerequisite, not a free ride. It blocks the upgrade order moving to Go.
notes:
Confirmed by the subset survey. StrEqual and strcmp as dispatch is 96 sites, 94 of them in upgrade.sp:574-760. That ranking is a pure function whose only blocker is a text key, so it is table work in internal/tables and not a subset change. SUBSET.md already prescribes the int32 identifier plus a name table.
Done as the prerequisite it was filed as: the table and the edge lookup, not the ranking itself.

internal/tables/attribute.go declares the 48 names behavior/upgrade.sp dispatches on, each with a written-down id. Ids are never counted and never reused, because a recorded run names the attribute it ranked and an id that changed meaning re-reads old results as something else. TestAttributeIDsSurviveAnInsert holds that.

Two emitters from the one table. gen/sourcepawn/attributes.sp has the enum, the name array and AttributeID, which the edge calls once per upgrade against the chain of up to forty StrEqual the ranking runs today. gen/go/attr/attr.go has the named Go constants, so the ranking becomes a switch over names rather than over numbers and the actionsel exhaustiveness argument works on it.

TestAttributeTableCoversTheRanking reads the pinned upgrade.sp and requires the two sets to be equal in both directions: 48 names, 48 StrEqual sites, nothing in the plugin without an id and no id standing for nothing.

TestGeneratedAttributeLookupAnswersTheDeclaredIDs runs the generated AttributeID under SourcePawn's VM on every declared name and asserts the id is the declared one, plus a name the table does not hold and an empty string, which both come back ATTRIBUTE_NONE. ATTRIBUTE_NONE is a real answer: the schema has hundreds of attributes and this table holds the ones the ranking has an opinion about. The table also compiles under SourceMod's spcomp64, per mvm-z83.13.

The array behind AttributeID is static on purpose. It is that function's own business and not a second public name table, which is what the epic is trying to stop.

Still open, and it is mvm-z83.7: moving GeneralUpgradePriority and ClassUpgradePriority themselves.
close_reason: Closed

title: The golden-input harness takes a struct, not three floats
description:
The spike's harness is ScoreTriples: three floats in, one float out. The real decision functions take structs of plain values.

Emit the golden-input table from a Go struct type and read back N results. This is generator work and it shares the float literal emitter with internal/tables rather than growing a second one.
notes:
Done. spshell.GoldenTable takes a Go struct type and rows of it, and emits a flat cell array with a named constant per column, so the driver indexes by field name rather than by a number nobody can check. Flat rather than an array of enum structs because SourcePawn has no initialiser for one and the driver would have become a filling function the size of the table.

A float32 goes in as its bits and comes back through view_as<float>, so nothing is rounded on the way in either direction. A field type with no cell is refused rather than emitted as a plausible zero, which TestGoldenTableRefusesAFieldWithNoCell covers.

TestGoldenTableRoundTrip runs it on the real thing: rows built from the action selection sweep, one result read back per row, compared with Select.

It shares literal with the rest of spshell rather than growing a second float emitter, and that emitter is now fuzzed against spcomp by mvm-z83.15, which found it wrong on FLT_MAX.
close_reason: Closed

title: A Go type implementing an action interface emits the BehaviorAction subclass
description:
Most of the plugin's line count is action plumbing: 162 lines of BehaviorAction subclassing with OnStart, OnUpdate, OnEnd, OnSuspend and OnResume, and 30 files under source/redbots3/behavior/.

SourceGo has no methodmaps and no inheritance, so this is the part a fork could not have given us and the part worth the most.

This is templating, not translation. A Go type with the callback methods emits the subclass, the constructor and the wiring. The bodies come from the subset generator, so this bead is only the shape.

Start with one small action, movetofront or gethealth, generated beside the hand written one and diffed.

title: Threat priority is the first decision to move to Go
description:
One function end to end before widening. Threat priority is the candidate: it is already a feature switch, it is arithmetic over distances, classes and health, and it has a measurement attached.

Tables, generation, differential test and a testbed run, on this one function. Report here what the loop cost and what it caught. If it caught nothing and cost a week, that is the result and the epic should be argued again.
notes:
Acceptance criterion added from the open-bug review: ThreatPriority must become a function of a threat record, not a loop over player slots. mvm-ds3 is caused by every threat scan looping over player slots while tank_boss occupies none, so the record shape removes the bug as a side effect. mvm-z83.14 forces this anyway.
Done in this repository, except the test-bed run.

internal/threat is ThreatPriority branch for branch, taking a filled record rather than an entity index, which is the acceptance criterion. internal/spgen emits the ranges, the enum, ThreatBand and the lookup, and cmd/gen writes it.

What was proved. TestGeneratedThreatPriorityAgreesWithGo runs all 960 combinations through the generated SourcePawn under SourcePawn's own VM and through the Go, and they agree. Nothing is sampled: the decision reads a distance through exactly two comparisons, so the six ranges are the two boundaries and a point either side of each, and the rest is both answers to each of four booleans times ten classes. TestThreatPriorityCompilesUnderBothCompilers puts the file through spcomp64 as well.

Against the pinned plugin: the two ranges match, the enum is the shipped order, the seven answers the shipped body returns are exactly the seven reachable here in both directions, and the five engine reads in the shipped body are exactly the five fields of the record. That last one is the answer to the question a differential test cannot ask, because the test drives both sides from the same record: an input the plugin reads and the record does not carry would pass every comparison and still be a port that decides with less than the plugin had.

What the loop cost, since the bead asks. About the same again as the code: the decision is 30 lines and the proofs are 200. Most of the cost was not the port, it was noticing what the port was allowed to change.

What it caught.

mvm-z83.46, a real one and P1. The shipped test is || and short circuits, so IsClientInGame is never reached for a non-player. An edge that fills IsPlayer and InGame independently calls it on every entity considered, and SourceMod throws Client index is invalid for anything outside 1..MaxClients. A tank is exactly that, and a tank is the whole reason for the record. The rule is written on the record and in the generated comment and nothing enforces it.

mvm-z83.40 does not apply here, and that is worth having established rather than assumed. Six reads, no writes, no randomness, so the record can be filled eagerly and the edge needs no lazy walk. Action selection needed one because three of its predicates write entity state.

Two facts were one edit away from being written twice. Class is now internal/tf and the float literal emitter is now internal/sp, because a second decision reads each.

The tank behaviour is preserved and named rather than fixed: inside 750 units a tank answers Urgent, past it None, both because that is what the shipped code does. TestTheTankStaysInvisible holds it there.

Still open, and it needs a server: the test-bed run. mvm-z83.42 says the default lineup reaches four of the ten class branches, so a run that compares the arms has to play a lineup with a sniper and a spy in it before it means anything for this function. Not doable here.
Wired up and played, on branch go-threat-priority.

The generated threat_priority.sp is vendored into source/redbots3/generated/ and included by the plugin, which now owns the two ranges and the enum. The shipped chain stays beside it and sm_redbots_feature_generated_threat_priority picks between them, so the port is an arm rather than a replacement. Compiles with no new warnings.

The edge fills the record with inGame behind isPlayer rather than beside it, which is mvm-z83.46 respected at the one call site that exists.

tf2-archipelago has a branch go-bots-ai where deploy/bots/build.sh takes DEFENDERBOTS_SOURCE and stages the mod from a working tree instead of the pinned tag, with make bots-from-tree. It built the mod from this branch and the ref stamp records the commit, so a server can play the port before it is a release.
Played on the test-bed, and the run is the part of this bead that was outstanding.

The port was wired up behind sm_redbots_feature_generated_threat_priority so the two are an A/B rather than a replacement, and mvm_decoy was played four waves an arm, twice, plus a three wave armed run.

What the runs found, in the order they found it.

First A/B flagged defenders died at 13.5 a wave armed against 6.0 unarmed, outside the noise band, with robots killed and wave duration inside it. The mechanism was in the error log and not in the statistics: TF2_HasTheFlag threw 3933 times from ThreatPriorityGenerated, 3671 on obj_attachment_sapper and 262 on tank_boss, and each exception aborted the whole threat choice for that tick. That is mvm-z83.46, wider than it was filed: every field after isPlayer has to be filled behind it, not beside it. Fixed, and two tests in internal/threat now assert the property the guard rests on.

Second A/B after the fix: zero exceptions, SourceMod did not create an error log at all. The arm still read worse, 0 of 4 cleared against 3 and deaths 15.0 against 7.0.

Third run, same code and same arm: 3 of 3 cleared. So the arm gap is spread, not signal. Armed clear counts across three runs were 2 of 4, 0 of 4 and 3 of 3 while the unarmed arm gave 3 of 4 twice with deaths 6.0 and 7.0. Four waves an arm cannot resolve a difference of this size, which is what mvm-z83.8 exists to establish and this run did not establish it: no off against off pass was run.

Instrumentation left in place on the branch. The plugin runs both functions on the armed side and logs where they part company, with the entity, its classname and the range. One three wave run reported no disagreements, and that run could not tell no disagreements from never ran, so a compared and disagreed count per wave was added afterwards and the run that would have read it was stopped part way. That number is still unmeasured.

Honest state: the edge is not proved faithful in a running game. It is proved faithful over the whole domain against the table, which is a different claim.
close_reason: Closed

title: A Go subset that refuses everything it does not support
description:
Not the subset a transpiler happens to handle, but the subset we write, checked by a pass that refuses anything else with a line number.

Roughly: functions, sized numeric types, float, bool, fixed length arrays, structs of those, if, for, switch, calls within the package. No growing slices, no maps, no interfaces, no closures, no allocation, no strings beyond fixed buffers.

Refusing is the value. A generator that quietly does something reasonable with a construct it half supports is how you get a plugin that compiles and is wrong.

Read SourceGo's passes before writing this. It is MIT, so take the mappings with attribution: pass1_illegal_code is this bead, pass3_merge_rettypes turns multiple returns into by-reference parameters, pass9_mutate_ranges handles range loops, pass10_mutate_no_ret_calls handles discarded results. About 30 KB of hard won mappings, cheaper to read than to rediscover. Do not fork the repository: see the section in docs/go-authored-ai.md for why.
close_reason:
The checker accepts the subset and refuses everything else at file:line:col with the replacement named, not just the construct. 66 tests green: 48 refusal cases, 13 acceptance cases, and tests asserting every refusal carries both a position and a non-empty fix. Verified here.

The subset is in internal/gosubset/SUBSET.md. Sized types only, no int or uint, since a cell is 32 bits and the width should be written. No strings, slices, maps, pointers, interfaces, closures or allocation.

range and len are accepted without type information, and SUBSET.md argues why that is sound rather than lucky: the type rules leave nothing to range over but an array or an integer, because no slice, map, channel or function value can be declared or imported.

Taken from SourceGo under MIT, attribution in ATTRIBUTION.md. pass1_illegal_code is the same refusal list and all of it was kept. pass3_merge_rettypes is why several return values are accepted, the generator turning results after the first into by-reference parameters, and correspondingly why pointers are refused in author code: the only pointers in the output are the ones the generator puts there. pass9 is why range is accepted, pass10 why a discarded call result is. Rejected: pass1 permits map[string]V onto StringMap, and this subset has neither strings nor maps.

The subset was checked against the real code rather than invented. ThreatPriority and SelectMoreDangerousThreat fit exactly, with the engine reads becoming fields on a struct the caller fills, which is the never-call-back rule working. ScoreNestArea and its helpers fit once the ArrayList walks become a fixed array plus a count. Both are in testdata as acceptance tests.

title: The telemetry field names come from the same table as the report columns
description:
mvmbots_stats.sp writes a JSON object per wave and testbed/report parses it. The field names are written twice and nothing checks them, so a renamed field reads as a zero rather than an error.

Same treatment as the feature table: one Go declaration of the wave record, generating the SourcePawn writer and the Go parser.

Depends on the feature table landing first, because it is the same generator.
close_reason:
The wave record is one Go declaration of 112 fields, each carrying its json name, its format verb and its SourcePawn argument. The Go field name and Go type are derived, not transcribed. It emits the FormatEx in mvmbots_stats.sp and the tagged Go struct the report unmarshals.

Round trip proved, all 112 fields matching on name, verb and argument expression, in order. Placeholders and arguments are counted against each other, so a format string with one more %d than arguments fails at the table rather than shifting every field after it, which is the failure mode that made a renamed field read as a zero.

Every json tag testbed/report/main.go reads today is a field the writer writes. TestWaveProofCatchesARenamedField renames robot_kills and fails if the comparison still passes.

Not done here: testbed/report/main.go still hand writes its own subset struct. Proved to be a subset, not replaced, because that is a change in the plugin repository. Filed with adoption in mvm-z83.16.

title: Bot hats throw an unhandled exception in WearHat
description:
TF2Util_EquipPlayerWearable throws from WearHat, cosmetics.sp:221, called by
Timer_GiveBotCosmetics at cosmetics.sp:129:

  Assertion failed - wearable entity 339 not attached to player.
  Gamedata may need to be updated

From Peppy's server, in every bundle he has sent: 14 in one, 6 in the next, and
the same line back to 2026-08-22. A different entity index each time.

The exception unwinds the timer, so the rest of that bot's cosmetics never run.
g_iEquipping is left non-zero because the line that clears it is after the throw,
which is the state the refusal handler reads.

## Not the sniper bug

Separate from mvm-bj8, and only found while reading those logs. Snipers stall on
servers with hats off too.

## Next

Read what TF2Util_EquipPlayerWearable asserts on: probably the wearable is
already parented, or the item is one the class cannot wear, which is the same
family as the "Item 30373 cannot be worn by class 2" line printed 102 times in
the first bundle. Then either refuse it before the equip or clear g_iEquipping
in a way the throw cannot skip.

title: Something walks the engineer into the same wedge on Mannworks
description:
The wedge recovery on mvm-hnb moves a stuck bot off the geometry it is inside,
and on Mannworks with Mean Machines it fired four times in four waves. Three of
those were the same coordinates: 1014 885 274.

So the recovery works and the cause does not go away. Something keeps routing
the engineer into one spot he cannot get out of, and the net catches him every
time rather than once.

Worth finding, because a bot that is teleported out mid-wave has still lost the
seconds it spent wedged, and the recovery is a safety net rather than an answer.

Where to look: 1014 885 274 on mvm_mannworks, and what the nest picker offers
that leads him through it. configs/defenderbots/map/mvm_mannworks.cfg holds the
spots.

Related: mvm-ipf and mvm-zx0 are the same shape on other maps and may share the
cause.
notes:
CAUSE FOUND, offline, without playing a wave. mvm-z83.27.
